## 1.0.0 (2026-09-26)

### ✨ New Features

* publish Anghami 8.0.28 patches ([d901fbe](https://github.com/mohamedamrnady/anghami-patches/commit/d901fbe7750a593804b17d56e3dc6b7b400ee707))

Patching on a phone takes about a minute now, down from three. Reels get a 10 second skip when you double tap either edge, and a tap shows their controls without pausing. Hold a feed video for 2x, pinch a story or a profile photo to zoom, and pick your own background color for dark or light mode. You can also put your own words or a picture at the top of Home, save a GIF from a comment, and hide profile notes or the Related posts list. Reel captions keep the bottoms of their letters again too.

New in this release

- New patch, `Longer music on photo stories`, with its switch under Stories. Turn it on and a song you add to a photo for your Story plays for up to 30 seconds instead of 15 (issue #156, requested by @uk609x-gif). Videos keep Facebook's own lengths. It starts off. Checked on an emulator in the photo story editor, where the song's trim window covers 30 seconds with the switch on and 15 with it off. A posted story hasn't been tried yet.

- New patch, `Hide profile notes`, with its switch under News feed. Turn it on and the note bubble on profile pictures goes away, including the Drop a thought prompt that sits on your own picture (issue #195, requested by @JFG1000). The picture itself still opens when you tap it. It starts off. Checked on an emulator on your own profile, where the bubble is gone with no gap, a tap on the picture still opens its menu, and turning the switch off brings the bubble back. A friend's note is only checked in tests so far.

- New switch under Search, `Hide "People you may know" in search`. When you open search, the People you may know row Facebook puts there before you type doesn't show. Your recent searches stay, and For you keeps its own switch. It's part of `Hide suggested and promoted posts` and starts off (issue #80, found from @MF-Debug's diagnostic report). Checked in tests, not yet on a phone.

- New switch under Comments, `Tap anywhere on View more replies`. On some accounts only a tap right on the words of a View more replies row opens the replies, both in a post's comments and in the comments shown under a post in the feed. Facebook picks per account which of two layouts that row gets, and the switch gives every account the one where the whole row takes the tap. That layout spaces the row a little differently (issue #219, requested by @pseudoparenchymatous). It starts off. Checked in tests, and in a post's comments on an emulator, where a tap at the far end of the row opened the replies. The row under feed posts is checked in tests only so far.

- New switch under Stories, `Pinch to zoom`. Pinch a story, or a photo on someone's profile, and it grows under your fingers the way photos in the feed already do. Move your fingers to look around, and it goes back when you let go (issue #220, requested by @jonandeva). Photos in the feed keep Facebook's own pinch. It starts off. Profile and Page photos and stories were checked on a phone. A second switch under it, `Stay zoomed`, keeps the zoom when you let go (asked for by @lijovklm). Drag it with one finger or pinch again, then tap or press Back to put it back. A story stays paused the whole time. It starts off. On Page photos it was checked on Android 16, with Back, the back swipe and a tap each putting the photo back without leaving the Page. On a story it was checked on a phone too: the zoom stayed and the story stayed paused, a drag moved it around, and Back or a tap put it back without skipping to the next story.

- A third switch under `Pinch to zoom`, `Double tap to zoom`. Double tap a photo on someone's profile and it zooms in 2x around where you tapped. Double tap again to put it back (asked for by @lijovklm on issue #220). A single tap still opens the photo, a moment later than before, and stories keep their taps the way Facebook has them. It starts off. Checked on a phone on a profile's cover photo, where a scroll that starts on the photo still scrolls, and on a profile picture, where a press and hold opens the same menu with the switch on or off.

- New switch under Reels and Watch, `Newest reels first`. The Reels tab plays the newest posted of the reels Facebook has already loaded for you first, instead of its own pick. It can't fetch newer reels, so it's the newest of what Facebook picked for you (issue #134, requested by @AbdulrahmanAlamodi). It starts off. Checked in tests and on an emulator.

- New row under Appearance with the AMOLED black theme, `Background color`. Type a color code like #0D1117 and dark mode's backgrounds switch to it after Facebook restarts, with no repatch (issue #214, requested by @M7amma). Cards and menus get a slightly lighter shade of it. Grays up to about #535353 work, and a color too light for Facebook's text is refused with a note saying why. Leave it blank for the color you patched with. Settings backups carry it too. The row isn't there when Material You is in the same build. Checked on an emulator: Home, Menu, Marketplace, a post and its comments, and Facebook's settings all take the color, and a blank row brings back the patched one. The Hushfacebook settings page follows it too, with its cards and dialogs a shade lighter. On a light gray like #535353 its text and switches get lighter as well, so they stay easy to read.

- A second row next to it, `Light background color`, does the same for Facebook's light mode (issue #214). Type a light color code like #FFF8E7 and, after Facebook restarts, most of the feed takes it in place of white, and so do the Menu, your profile card at the top of it and Facebook's own settings. Gray buttons shift with it so they still stand out, and Facebook's text gets a little darker where it needs to so it stays easy to read. A color too dark for that is refused with a note naming the darkest gray it takes, #A6A6A6. Leave it blank for Facebook's own white. Settings backups carry it, and like the dark row it isn't there when Material You is in the same build. Checked on an emulator with #FFF8E7, where Home, the Menu and its profile card, a post's comments and Facebook's settings all took it, and dark mode looked the same as before.

- New switch under Reels and Watch, `Hide the slow connection message`. When a video or GIF takes a while to load, the "This is taking a while. Try checking your network connection." message stops popping up, and the video keeps loading like before (issue #222, requested by @CiupaSs). It's part of `Clean up Reels` and starts off. Checked in tests, not yet on a phone.

- Two new switches under Menu, `Hide Help and support` and `Keep Settings and privacy expanded` (issue #224, requested by @sleeepingfatcat). The first takes the Help and support section out of the Menu. The second opens Settings and privacy with its rows already showing, and a tap on its header won't fold them away. Both start off, and the second takes effect after Facebook restarts. Checked on an emulator, where Help and support was gone and Settings and privacy opened with its rows out and its arrow pointing up. With the switch off it folds up like before.

- New switch under Reels and Watch, `Play whole reels in the feed's Reels row`. The reels in the Reels row on your Home feed keep playing instead of repeating their first second, so you can see what a reel is before you open it (issue #228, requested by @lijovklm). It's part of `Clean up Reels` and starts off. Checked on an emulator, where Facebook had told each tile to stop at one second and loop. With the switch on the tile played on for the whole recording.

- A GIF in a comment can be saved now. Press and hold a GIF comment and the menu that comes up has `Save GIF`, which saves the moving GIF to your Pictures folder, not the still frame the comment list shows (issue #226, requested by @pseudoparenchymatous). Facebook only offers Save photo for photo comments, so a GIF got nothing before. It comes with `Download any photo` and goes away when that's off. Checked on an emulator with two GIPHY comments, each saved as a full animated GIF.

- New patch, `Double tap to skip`, with its switch under Reels and Watch. Double tap the right edge of a reel to jump 10 seconds ahead, or the left edge to go back 10 (5 on one under 30 seconds). A double tap in the middle works like before (issue #225, requested by @lotslove). It's Facebook's own skip, which most accounts never get. It starts off. Checked on an emulator on a 1:36 video in the Reels tab, where each edge showed +10s or -10s and moved the video, and the like count didn't change. With the switch off the same double tap did nothing.

- New patch, `Tap shows the controls`, with its switch under Reels and Watch. A tap on a playing reel brings up its controls while it keeps playing, so you can reach the skip and mute buttons without stopping it (issue #225, requested by @lotslove). They go away on their own after 3 seconds, or right away on a second tap, and the button in the middle still pauses. Facebook built this layout and ships it turned off. It starts off. Checked on an emulator in the Reels tab, where a tap showed the controls around a pause button while the time kept moving, they hid about 3 seconds later or on a second tap, and the middle button paused the reel. With the switch off a tap paused it like before.

- New switch under News feed, `Hide "Related posts" under posts`. It takes away the Related posts list Facebook adds under some posts, the one whose titles are written by Meta AI. The post, its buttons and its comments stay (issue #231, requested by @MF-Debug). It's part of `Hide suggested and promoted posts` and starts off. On an emulator with Facebook 584 the switch was asked about that list as the feed scrolled and answered it, with no crash. The account there doesn't get the list itself, so it hasn't been seen leaving a screen yet.

- New patch, `Home header text`, with its row under Appearance. Type a few words and they sit at the top of Home where the Facebook logo was, at the logo's height and in the colors Facebook gives its logo in light and dark mode (issue #230, requested by @schuani). Up to 30 characters, and a long line shrinks so it still fits beside the buttons. Leave it blank for Facebook's logo. Settings backups carry it. Checked on an emulator in dark mode over two fresh starts, where "Good morning" showed in white in the logo's place. The light mode colors are checked in tests. A second row, `Home header picture`, puts a picture of your own there instead, in its own colors. Pick one from your phone and a copy shrunk to fit is kept with Facebook's files, so the original can go. While it's chosen it takes the place of your words, and `Remove the header picture` brings back the words or the logo. Settings backups leave the picture out, since it can't travel in one. Checked on an emulator, where a picked picture showed at the top of Home with its shape kept, after the restart button and again after a fresh start, and the logo came back after Remove.

- New switch under Reels and Watch, `Hold a feed video for 2x`. Press and hold a video playing in your feed or in Watch, the edge included, and it plays at double speed until you let go, the way a reel already can (issue #229, requested by @lijovklm). A video already at 2x or faster is left alone, and `Keep the video speed` doesn't hold on to the 2x once you let go. With `Long press opens comments` on, a hold on a feed video speeds it up instead. It comes with `Hold a reel for 2x`, works without that patch's switches and starts off. Checked on an emulator with Facebook 584, where holding the middle of a video in the Groups feed and then its left edge played it at 2x until the finger lifted, then back at normal speed, with nothing opening.

Fixes

- `Hide sponsored reels` also keeps ads out of the row of reels in the Home feed, the one you scroll sideways (issue #216, reported by @KingKode123). That row takes its ad tiles from a second ad pool of Facebook's, and only the Reels tab's pool was held before. Now that pool answers that it has no ad, so the row moves on to the next regular reel. On an emulator with Facebook 584 the row's pool was asked for an ad and gave none, with no crash, but that account showed no ad tile in the row to begin with, so an ad hasn't been seen leaving it yet.

- Reel captions don't lose the bottoms of their letters anymore (issue #96, issue #212). Facebook's Reels footer gives the caption a box a little taller than the space around it and cuts off what doesn't fit, so y, g and p and Bengali vowel signs got clipped on the last line, even in Facebook's own font. The space under the caption is empty, so the caption now draws into it. The first reel after Facebook starts gets it too. Checked on a phone over five fresh starts into Reels and six reels in a row, every caption whole, with the buttons beside it unchanged.

- `Menu tiles to hide` offers the Finds tile now, so it can go the way the others do. Facebook gives that tile no link of its own and has its server pick where it goes, so the list never saw it. A tile like that now goes by Facebook's id for the app behind it (issue #224, requested by @AlexanderQueen). Checked on an emulator, where Finds showed up in the list and left the Menu once ticked.

- Save on a story someone shared from Reels takes the reel now, not a picture of it. That kind of story is a still, the reel's first frame with a play button on it, and Facebook keeps the reel itself tucked inside the story as a sticker, so `Download any story` saved the still. It finds the reel there and saves its video at the best quality listed, named after the reel (issue #207, found from @jeiejs's diagnostic report). Checked in tests, not yet on a phone.

- With `View stories anonymously` on, a story you watched partway opens where you left off after Facebook restarts, not back at the first card. Someone who posted a new story after you watched the rest opens at the new one too. Facebook starts at the first card its servers think you haven't seen, and they never hear about these views, so the phone keeps the cards you watched for 48 hours and Facebook's pick skips past them. Your views still aren't sent, so you stay off the viewer lists (issue #218). Checked in tests, not yet on a phone.

- `Turn off HDR brightness` no longer makes the phone's own video service crash and restart on a Samsung phone with a Snapdragon chip. HDR reels set off a tone-mapping step in that chip's video decoder, and that step is what crashed, so the decoder isn't asked to tone-map anymore. HLG reels still go over at the usual brightness, and PQ videos on that decoder play as Facebook set them up. Checked in tests, and on a phone over 30 reels with two HLG ones and no crash.

- With Debug logging on, Marketplace's report reads a whole page of search results again. Pages of 27 and 48 listings carried ads nested deeper than the report would follow, so it stopped early and called them incomplete. It follows more than twice as deep and reads four times as much of a page now, and when it does have to stop, it says whether the page was too deep or too big. Checked in tests, and on an emulator where both pages now read in full.

- With `Don't save search history` on, a search no longer sits at the top of search's Recent list until Facebook restarts. It already stayed out of your saved history, but Facebook still kept it in Recent for the rest of that session. Checked in tests, not yet on a phone.

- With `Don't save search history` on, a page or profile you open from a search doesn't show up in your search history as "You visited" anymore (issue #221, requested by @itsmenewbie03). Facebook builds that entry from the visit report a profile sends as it opens, not from the search itself, so that one report isn't sent while the switch is on. The page opens the same as before. Checked on an emulator, where a page opened from its search result left nothing in the history.

- `Hide the reaction preview on posts` also takes away the "Name and 55 others" line beside the reaction faces, or the plain number Facebook puts there on some layouts. Only the faces went before. TalkBack still reads it. The number on the Like button stays until `Hide counts on posts` is on too, as its description says (issue #158). Checked in tests, not yet on a phone.

- The `Mark as seen button` also shows when Facebook opens a story in one of its other story screens. Facebook 584 has three more besides the usual one, and the button only looked for that one. Checked in tests.

- A copy of Facebook made with `Clone app` could close right after it opened when the regular Facebook was installed beside it. It was asking the regular app for a saved value instead of asking itself, and Android doesn't let one app into the other's storage like that, so it closed the copy. Now every one of those requests goes to the copy's own storage (issue #16). Checked on an emulator.

- With `Material You theme` on in dark mode, the sheet that slides up when you tap the arrow beside your name in the Menu, the one for switching profiles, takes the theme's colors now. It stayed Facebook's own flat gray while the Menu behind it turned blue-gray. That sheet's gray comes with the screen from Facebook's server, paired with a light one, so no theme color ever reached it. A dark gray there now becomes the theme's gray at the same brightness, and the AMOLED theme keeps the sheet as it was (issue #37). Checked on an emulator, where the sheet went from #1F1F20 to the theme's #1E1F25.

- With `Picture-in-picture` on, leaving Facebook while the Hushfacebook settings were open over a reel floated the settings page in the small window. The reel kept playing under the page, so Facebook still opened its window on the way out. While the settings show, leaving Facebook doesn't open the window anymore, and once you close them it works the same as before. Checked on a phone, where leaving with the settings open over a reel opened no small window, and after closing them the reel went into the window as before.

Other changes

- Patching takes about a third of the time on a phone. Most patches used to read through all 215,000 of Facebook's classes to find the few they change, dozens of full passes in one patch. Now a single pass at the start notes what each class refers to, and a patch only reads the classes that mention what it's looking for. With the recommended patches on Facebook 584, a patch in Morphe Manager on a phone went from a little over 3 minutes on 0.17.0 to just under 1 minute, and on a desktop held to two cores from 54 seconds to 28. It still fits in the memory it needed before, and the patched app comes out the same as before, class for class (issue #216, reported by @AbdulrahmanAlamodi).

- `Use the system font` patches faster. It used to read through Facebook's code four separate times to find the places it changes, and it built the full name of every call and field along the way. It now makes one pass and only builds a name when the class matches one it cares about. On Facebook 584 with the recommended patches, `Use the system font` went from about 5.9 seconds to 1.5, and the whole patch from 51 seconds to 45 on a desktop. It still changes the same places in Facebook (issue #216, reported by @AbdulrahmanAlamodi).

Behind the scenes

- The device audit no longer refuses to start when the phone holds a settings backup from an older audit or the settings tool with no locale and theme saved beside it. It copies that folder off the phone first, takes the locale and theme the phone has now, and puts the backup's switches back at the end, the same as for a run that never finished. Twice on 2026-10-22 that backup had to be fixed by hand before a walk could run. Checked in tests, and the folder copy on a phone.

- A focused test run that names fixture tests after `:patches:fixtureTest` runs them again. Those filters used to be dropped, and the run passed without running a single fixture test.

- A push or a fixture check with a morphe-desktop CLI on the wrong patcher stops right away now. The 0.17.0 push ran its whole 17-minute gate with an old 1.18.1 CLI still set in the shell and only failed at the last step, because a bundle built on the 2.0 patcher won't load in a 1.x CLI. `scripts/pre-push.ps1` and `scripts/verify-all-patches.ps1` read which patcher the jar carries before anything heavy runs, and the message names the jar, both versions and, when it applies, the newer jar your user settings already point to.

The [changelog](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/Hushfacebook/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) has every earlier release too.

How to update

1. Update Morphe Manager to 2.0.0 or newer, then refresh the Hushfacebook source.
2. Patch Facebook `584.0.0.51.56`. On most phones that's build `475817393`, the arm64-v8a one.
3. Install over your current patched Facebook with the manager's existing signing key. Keep that key so updates keep working.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a Facebook APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/Hushfacebook#install).

Look over a diagnostic report before you share it. The filter can still miss private text it doesn't recognize.

What was checked

Local checks passed: 3718 runtime tests and 1181 patch tests with no failures, plus both Android lints and the release-script checks. All 102 patches applied without forcing to Facebook 584.0.0.51.56, the 64-bit build, and a second build of the same commit matched this bundle entry for entry. I patched Facebook with this exact bundle and walked the whole app with every switch on, on an emulator signed in to a full account. 76 of 103 hook families ran there, the new Home header text, Double tap to skip, Hide profile notes and Pinch to zoom among them. All 23 settings pages opened in dark and in light, and Facebook didn't crash once. Android's verifier raised nothing on the patched build, the same as on Meta's own. The walk doesn't reach downloads, chats or the story viewer, so those are covered by the patch tests alone this time.

Hushfacebook moves to Facebook 584 and Morphe's new 2.0 patcher, so update Morphe Manager to 2.0.0 or newer before you patch. It's 64-bit only for now, since Facebook hasn't put out a 32-bit 584 yet. New switches can close Facebook when you leave it, hide the video comment box and draw thin lines between posts on the black theme, and a new patch keeps feed videos muted. Black cards buttons, the comment gestures in clean mode and Menu promotions in the side panel work again too.

New in this release

- New switch under Privacy, `Close Facebook when you leave it`. Three seconds after you leave Facebook it closes all the way and drops out of your recent apps, so nothing of it keeps running in the background (issue #202, requested by @M7amma). It holds off while an upload, a call or a Hushfacebook save is still going, or while a file picker or camera Facebook opened is on screen, and turning the screen off with Facebook in front doesn't count as leaving. Notifications can come late, or not until you open Facebook again. It starts off. Checked on a phone.

- New switch under Comments, `Hide the video comment box`. The Add a comment box under a full-screen video goes away, outline and all, while comment boxes on posts stay (issue #213, from a patch by @dijitalcozum). The Comment button beside the video still opens the comments, with their own box. It starts off. Checked on a phone.

- New switch under Appearance with the AMOLED black theme, `Lines between posts`. Facebook leaves a thin gap between posts that shows the page behind them, and on a black page that gap went black too, so a post without a photo ran straight into the next one (issue #206). With the switch on, that gap shows as a thin dark gray line in Facebook's dark mode, while the page and the cards stay black. It starts off. Checked on a phone, with the switch on and off.

- New patch, `Keep feed videos muted`, under Playback. Videos in the feed start with the sound off every time you open Facebook, even after you've been away a while, and Facebook doesn't turn it back on by itself. A video you open from the feed starts muted too. A tap on a video's speaker or the volume up key still turns it on. It starts off, and takes effect after the restart its switch offers. Checked on a phone.

Fixes

- With `Black cards` on, buttons like Log out in the side panel and Edit profile keep their dark gray fill again. In 0.16.0 and 0.16.1 the AMOLED theme's sweep for leftover dark colors also caught Hushfacebook's own colors, so those buttons went black on a black page and only their text showed (issue #191). Checked on a phone.

- `Open comments with a gesture` works with `Always use clean mode` on. Clean mode hides a reel's sidebar, Comment button and all, and the gestures pressed that button, so a long press fell back to Facebook's menu and a double tap did nothing (issue #179). A reel without the button now gets its comments from what its long-press handler keeps, on the same sheet the button opens. Checked on a phone, long press and double tap both.

- With `Leave calls and chats to Messenger` on, a message sent to you in Facebook's own Chats no longer shows up twice, once from Messenger and once from Facebook. Those messages reach your phone as Facebook's regular notifications rather than through its chat notifier, so they slipped past the switch. Facebook now leaves them to Messenger as well, while every other notification posts as before (issue #193). Checked in tests, not yet on a phone.

- `Hide Menu promotions` now holds in the side panel Menu for accounts Facebook gives its server-drawn Menu. 0.16.0 put Facebook's own Menu in that panel, but the Menu page inside it asks Facebook's server the same question again, and those accounts got the server's Menu right back with Upgrades and Also from Meta still in it (issue #184). Hushfacebook answers that second question too now. While any Menu switch is on, the panel and the Menu tab both show Facebook's own Menu with your hidden sections and shortcuts gone. Checked on a phone with Facebook's answer forced to the server-drawn Menu.

- `Block Instant Games ads` now covers games that open inside Facebook's main screen too. Those games talk to Facebook through a bridge of their own, so their ad requests went around the patch and some showed ads between levels anyway (issue #168). They get the same no-ad answer now, and with `Answer rewarded game ads as watched` on, a rewarded video still counts as watched. Checked on a phone with a game played to its map.

- `Disable Audience Network` stays off now. Facebook switched those parts back on after an install or update, and one of its startup tasks lets the server turn three of them on again (issue #168). Both are held off, and any an earlier install left on go back off when Facebook starts. Checked on a phone.

Other changes

- Hushfacebook now targets Facebook 584.0.0.51.56 only, the newest stable release. That's build 475817393 for 64-bit phones (the arm64-v8a 480dpi Android 11+ bundle). Facebook hasn't released a 32-bit build of 584 yet, so none is declared for now. If you're on 583.0.0.39.55, update Facebook to 584 before you patch.

- You need Morphe Manager 2.0.0 or newer now. The patches are built on Morphe's new 2.0 patcher, which Manager 1.x can't load (it asks you to update instead), so update Manager first. Desktop patching needs morphe-desktop 1.19.0 or newer for the same reason.

- The description of `Hide the reaction preview on posts` now says where the number on the Like button goes. That count belongs to `Hide counts on posts`, so the preview switch alone leaves it showing (issue #158).

- A settings file can now be up to 96 KB, up from 88 KB, so a file with every list full still fits now that there are more switches.

Behind the scenes

- The device audit can now put back the switches from a backup an older Hushfacebook build left on the phone. Switches added after that build weren't in the backup, so they kept the audit's all-on values, the restore never matched, and the audit folder stayed behind. Those switches go back to their defaults first now, and everything else comes from the backup. Checked on a phone.

- The device audit gets its report and opens the settings pages even when the walk ends on a reel or another full-screen page, and the phone smoke walk reaches the settings there too. Android dropped those requests without saying so, and the audit stopped with no report. The audit was checked on a phone, the smoke walk by its tests.

- The device audit no longer stops halfway when another tool reads the phone's lease file at the same moment. It waits a few seconds and tries again. A missing lease or one held by someone else still stops it.

- A baseline the device audit writes on Windows now has the same line endings as the copy in the repo, so promoting one doesn't leave the file looking half changed.

- No release goes out now until the whole app has been walked, on a phone or an emulator, with the exact bundle being published. `scripts/device-audit.ps1` leaves a `walk-receipt.json` saying how the walk ended, where it ran and which patch build the app reported, and the release script's publish step takes it as `-Walk`. Anything short of a full pass with no crash on that same bundle stops it before the tag.

- A release now also waits on Android's own code check, run on a phone or an emulator. The 0.16.0 comment crash was a method that phones refuse to load, and only the phone half of `scripts/verify-injected-registers.ps1` would have caught it, but the release check ran without a phone. With `-Serial` and `-ReceiptPath` it now leaves a `verifier-receipt.json` that names the phone, the patch build read out of the checked APK, and every message where the patched app and Meta's own build differ. The publish step takes it as `-Verifier` and stops before the tag unless it's a pass for that same bundle with no differences. When it stops, it names the methods that failed.

- The device patch scripts read morphe-desktop 1.19.0's results. That CLI renamed its list of patching steps, so every device patch read an empty list and counted as failed. Both names work now, and a result with no steps or a failed one is still refused.

- The source ledger asks an adopted source for proof on every Facebook build the patches declare, and on two builds whenever two are declared. With 584 out for 64-bit phones only, two fixtures of one declared build couldn't exist, so the old rule stopped every release.

A quick fix for 0.16.0, which closed Facebook whenever comments opened on a lot of phones, posts opened from a notification included. Comments open normally again with `Comment sheet options` patched in, so there's no need to leave it out anymore. Instant games also download through Facebook itself now, since Google Play can't deliver them to a patched Facebook.

Fixes

- Opening comments doesn't close Facebook any more. In 0.16.0, tapping a post's comment button, or the comments on a reel, crashed Facebook when `Comment sheet options` was patched in, even with every switch off or Hushfacebook paused. Phones and accounts that get Facebook's newer comment list hit it, opening a post from a notification included (issues #203, #204, #208, #209 and #210). Android's own check of the patched app passes on a phone now, where 0.16.0 failed it. The phone I check on gets Facebook's older comment list, so it never crashed either way.

- Instant games download with Facebook's own downloader now. When Google Play had installed Facebook, Facebook could hand the game download to Play, which can't serve a patched build, so the game's loading screen closed right away. With Debug logging on, the report's module download line says when Play was skipped (issue #168). Checked in tests, not yet on a phone, since mine already had its games downloaded.

Reported issues

- #203, #204, #208, #209 and #210 Facebook closing when comments open, a post from a notification included: fixed, with nothing to turn on or leave out.

- #168 Instant games closing on their loading screen: games download through Facebook itself now. Please say on the issue whether yours opens.

Behind the scenes

- The patch check that runs before a release now catches the mistake behind 0.16.0's comment crash without a phone. A hook that hands back the extension's answer without casting it to the type Facebook's method returns gets refused, naming the method. Run against the published 0.16.0 build, it flags exactly the comment method that crashed.

What was checked

Local checks passed: 3430 runtime tests and 1095 patch tests with no failures, plus both Android lints and the release-script checks. This release is mostly your requests again. You can keep your searches out of Facebook's history, hide posts from groups you haven't joined, take the For you list off search and hide the Find friends card where your friends' posts run out. Reels get switches for the audio line, Save and the speaker button, and a long press on a feed post can open its comments. Kept reel speeds now last through a restart, Black cards make the AMOLED theme fully black, and a Free stuff shortcut opens Marketplace's free listings. On the fix side, Hide Menu promotions reaches the side Menu, Default comment order works on a post's own page and the logo long press works in Arabic.

New in this release

- New patch, `Don't save search history`. With its switch under Search on, what you search for isn't added to your Facebook search history, so there's nothing to clear by hand later. Searches already there stay until you delete them. It starts off (issue #196).

- New switch under Reels and Watch, `Hide the audio line on reels`. It takes the "Original audio" or song line off the bottom of reels, and the other info there stays. It's part of `Clean up Reels` and starts off (issue #200).

- New switch under News feed, `Hide the Find friends card`. The "Want to see more posts from friends?" card with its Find friends button stops showing where your friends' posts run out, and the "You're all caught up with friends" line above it goes too, since Facebook builds them as one block. It starts off (issue #187).

- New switch under News feed, `Hide posts from groups you're not in`. Posts from groups you haven't joined, like a friend's post in a public group with a Join button next to its name, stop showing on Home. Posts from your own groups stay, and so does a friend sharing a group post to their profile. While it's on, Home always asks Facebook whether you're in each group, since some accounts don't get that by default. It's part of `Hide suggested and promoted posts` and starts off (issue #195).

- New switch under Search, `Hide For you in search`. When you open search, the For you list of searches Facebook suggests, with its Refresh button, doesn't show. Your recent searches stay, and so do the suggestions while you type. It's part of `Hide suggested and promoted posts` and starts off (issue #80).

- New switch under Downloads, `Convert to keep the full size`. With `Save videos other apps can open` on, a full size video Facebook only has as VP9 or AV1 gets converted to H.264 on your phone, so it isn't saved at a smaller size any more. It's slower, videos over 10 minutes still save smaller, and it starts off (issue #189). Checked in tests, not yet on a phone.

- New switch under Reels and Watch, `Hide Save on reels`. It takes the Save button off the side of reels, and the buttons above it move down. It's part of `Clean up Reels` and starts off (issue #190).

- New switch under Reels and Watch, `Hide the speaker button on reels`. It takes the speaker button off the bottom of the side of reels, and your phone's volume buttons still turn the sound on. It's part of `Clean up Reels` and starts off (issue #190).

- `Long press opens comments` works on feed posts now, not just reels. Hold a post's photo or the line with its name and that post's comments open, ready to read, without the keyboard popping up. That includes the photo inside a post someone shared. When the bottom of a long post is still off screen, the feed scrolls up just enough to bring it in first. Holding the post's text (a text post on a colored background too), a profile picture or one of the buttons under the post does what it always did, and nothing opens if a call or another app takes the screen before you let go. The switch still starts off (issue #179).

- New switch under Appearance, `Black cards`, for the AMOLED black theme. Cards, comments, menus, the Create story tile and the strip behind the Menu's Log out button go fully black like the page instead of the near black that sets them apart, and buttons like See more and Log out keep a dark gray fill so they still show. It starts off and needs a restart (issue #191).

- `Menu tiles to hide` lists the rows under Help and support and Settings and privacy too, so Orders and payments or Report a problem can leave the Menu (issue #153). They show up in the list once you've opened those groups in the Menu, and the rows Hushfacebook adds there always stay.

- New switch under Marketplace, `Free stuff shortcut`. Facebook's app has no Free category in Marketplace, so this adds Free stuff to the menu you get by holding Facebook's icon (right after the Hushfacebook entry, if there's room) and a Free stuff row to the Menu's Settings and privacy. Both open Marketplace's free listings, the same ones the website's Free Stuff category shows. It starts off (Discussion #52).

- With `Skip silent parts` on, a reel's More menu and a video post's three-dot menu get a `Skip silent parts` row. Tap it and that one video plays its quiet stretches again, right away, while every other video keeps skipping them. Tap it again to go back to skipping. The row needs `Resume long videos` patched in too, and the post menu one needs `Download any video` (issue #144). The reel row is seen on a phone, the post menu row so far in tests.

Fixes

- Back on App Lock's locked screen sends Facebook to the background again on Android 16. Facebook now targets Android 16, so Back reaches the locked screen through a different path there, and it did nothing at all.

- `Hide Menu promotions` now reaches the Menu that slides in from the side, the one some accounts open with the three lines button next to the Facebook logo (issue #184). Facebook can fill that panel with a second Menu drawn by its server, which nothing in Hushfacebook touched, so Upgrades and Also from Meta stayed put. While any Menu switch is on, the panel gets the same Menu the Menu tab shows, with your hidden sections gone and the Hushfacebook row under Settings and privacy.

- A copy made with Clone app looks up its own resources and app info where Facebook's code spells out its package name (issue #16). Morphe renames a clone's resource table along with its package, so the lookups Firebase's notifications make for their text, icon and sound found nothing in a clone, and the login and consent links, device login and Xiaomi's icon badge were pointed at the stock app. They go to the clone now. Where Facebook means Meta's own app, like handing a link to an installed Facebook, nothing changes. Checked against Facebook's code, not yet on a phone.

- With `Picture-in-picture` on, a Facebook link you open from another app while a reel floats in the small window opens its page full screen, and the reel keeps playing in its window (issue #126). Before, the link just brought the floating reel back to full screen, or opened Facebook's Home instead of the page.

- With `Keep the progress bar` and its time on, swiping to the next reel shows 0:00 and that reel's length right away (issue #120). Before, the time went missing until the reel started playing, about a second on a slow connection.

- The Saved and Watch history entries you can add to the menu you get by holding Facebook's icon now sit right after the Hushfacebook entry, ahead of Facebook's own. Samsung phones show only the first four, and with Facebook's Notifications, Friends and Reels behind the Hushfacebook entry, yours got added but never showed. Facebook's entries just move down one.

- With `Keep the progress bar` on, a reel Facebook doesn't hand a bar to no longer shows the last reel's frozen spot and time (issues #90 and #120). They stay hidden until you're back on that reel or the next one takes the bar.

- `Default comment order` applies on a post's own page too, the one a link, a notification or a post's date opens (issue #192). That page asks Facebook for its comments another way than the comment sheet does, so Most relevant or Newest only took hold in the sheet and the page kept Facebook's order.

- `Hide the new comments pop-up` takes away the newer pop-up as well, the one with the commenters' pictures on it (issue #185). Facebook has two of them now and the switch only knew the older one. Checked in tests, not yet on a phone.

- With `View stories anonymously` on, a story you watched to the end stays grey through the feed's refreshes (issue #165). Facebook rebuilds the story tray a dozen times a second when it opens and again with each refresh, and only the first eight copies in a minute got marked, so a ring could turn back blue moments after it went grey.

- `Leave calls and chats to Messenger` works with a Messenger installed under another name beside Meta's apps, the way HushMessenger's "install beside" option makes one (issue #193). Facebook only counted Meta's own Messenger package, so with a renamed copy it kept ringing and posting the same chat notification Messenger posted. The Messenger icon at the top and the Get Messenger card already counted such a copy.

- `Hide the notes and active now row` takes the whole row away now. Your own "Your note" tile used to stay behind and keep the row at full height.

- With `Save videos other apps can open` on, a long video Facebook only has as VP9 or AV1 keeps its full size when it's made H.264. A thin four minute 1080p reel used to run out of the room set aside for the conversion and save at 720p instead (issue #189).

- With `Save videos other apps can open` on, a video over 10 minutes that Facebook only has as VP9 or AV1 goes straight to its smaller H.264 file. Before, it downloaded the full size first, gave up on converting it and showed two error messages on the way.

- `See-through bars` keeps its blur on Home after you've been to Reels. Before, a trip to Reels could leave the bars plain see-through until Facebook restarted (issue #188).

- `Menu tiles to hide` now hides Feeds, Reels, Memories, Birthdays, Dating and Pages, which it missed on 583, and tiles you ticked before carry over. The list shows the tiles your own Menu has, by the names Facebook gives them, so Crisis response, Community Notes, Pokes and the rest can go too (issue #153).

- A video whose best file is over 512 MB saves the next smaller one instead of nothing, and the message at the end says which quality you got. A two hour reel's 720p file was 645 MB and the save just failed, though Facebook also had it at 480p. Checked in tests, not yet on a phone.

- A long press on the Facebook logo opens the Hushfacebook settings with Facebook in Arabic too. In some languages Facebook gives the logo nothing to do when it's tapped, and the long press never got set up there (issue #12).

- Where a reel's More menu opens the gear menu's speed sheet, the sheet marks the speed the reel really plays at, so you can pick `1 (Normal)` to drop a kept speed (issue #199). Facebook couldn't find the reel's player there and always marked Normal, and a tap on the marked row does nothing, so a kept speed stayed until you turned `Keep the reel speed` off.

Other changes

- `Hide the search pill on reels` also takes the search suggestion off the top of a reel's comments. Comments start right at the top of the sheet, and the one under the caption stays hidden like before (#197).

- `Hide the search pill on reels` also takes the search bar off the top of reels you open from a profile, along with the paper plane button next to it that searches the suggested words. The back arrow stays (#201).

- `Keep the reel speed` and `Keep the video speed` remember the speed you picked after Facebook or the phone restarts, so the first reel or video you play starts at it. Pick normal speed and it's gone for good (#199). Seen on a phone with reels, and checked in tests for feed videos.

- `Turn off screen transitions` also skips the zoom a photo opens and closes with. Tap a photo in the feed and it's full screen right away, and Back puts it away without shrinking it into the post. Dragging a photo away still follows your finger.

- `Turn off screen transitions` also skips the slides of screens Facebook opens inside the app, the ones that slide in from the side and back out to the right when you press Back. They just appear and go now.

- `Turn off screen transitions` also covers posts with several photos. Tap one of the photos and its page is there right away, without the photo growing out of its tile or the gray background fading in. Back closes it just as fast, with no shrink into the tile or slide off the screen.

- `Turn off screen transitions` also stops the single-photo viewer from sliding. A photo that opens without its spot in the feed used to slide up from the bottom, and one that can't shrink back into the post slid off the screen on Back. Both just appear and go now.

- `Stop link history in Facebook's browser` also stops the request that saves a page you opened to your Facebook link history, its address, title and times, from either place in the browser that asks for it. Before, it only stopped the two parts that record pages, and Facebook's browser has a second way in to that save.

- `Stop link history in Facebook's browser` also stops the two reports Facebook's browser logs when you fill in a form on a page. One of them names the page's address, the form's fields and the ad the page came from. Autofill itself isn't touched, so it fills forms and remembers what you turned down the same as before.

- The `Home shows` row and the `Following feed on Home` description say what the filter really does: Home asks Facebook for that filter's posts, and when there's nothing new Facebook can still fill Home with suggested posts and reels. Both now point to `Hide "Suggested for you" posts` and `Hide Reels in the feed`, which take those out. A Home set to Friends got 39 suggested posts, 21 ads and 2 friends' posts in one test, so the old wording promised more than Facebook gives.

- With Debug logging on and `Clean up Reels` patched in, a report says whether a reel that just ended is the one Facebook's Reels auto-advance is following, or one it let go of after a swipe. An option to go to the next reel on its own needs that answer first. Only fixed labels and counts are written, nothing about the reel itself.

- A report counts each press held on a feed post with `Long press opens comments` on, and when the comments didn't open it says why: the post text's own long press, a hold on the buttons under the post, a list that doesn't scroll, the screen losing focus, or a lift that came before the timer ran. With Debug logging on, the line also names the kind of view under your finger and its size. Nothing about the post goes in (issue #179).

- With Debug logging on, a report says more when a game's download screen closes right away. Next to the module and the error, its line lists the steps Facebook's downloader took for that module in the last 30 seconds and what the download task ended with, so one report can show where a game that won't open stopped (issue #168).

- With Debug logging on, a report gets a line for Bengali text the first time each part of Facebook lays it out. It lists the font's line height at that size, how high and low the letters really reach, and how much room Facebook left them, so a report can show where captions lose the tops of their letters (issue #96). The text itself isn't logged.

- With Debug logging on, a report lists what each kind of feed request asked Facebook for, like its feed style and ordering. That lets Home with a `Home shows` filter be compared with the same filter on the Feeds tab, since Home with Friends still comes back full of suggestions for some accounts. Ids, page cursors and anything that isn't a plain one-word value are left out.

- With Debug logging on, each feed post's line in a report ends with a short code, and the same code comes up again when Facebook counts that post as seen. Lining the two up shows whether a post at the top of Home came from that run's request or from what Facebook kept from an earlier one. The code is six characters cut from a one-way hash of Facebook's id for the post, so it can't be turned back into the post.

- With Debug logging on, Marketplace's report lines name a listing's price, title, photo, delivery and seller fields when Facebook sends them, where before they only counted as other fields. They also name its place, its sold or pending state, the parts of the price and place, and whether the seller is a person, a page or a business. A long page of search results is read to the end now, where it used to stop partway and mark the capture incomplete. A listing's own page is read too, and so is a search page Facebook sends as one big block, which used to stop the capture before it read anything. The lines also say whether a listing came with a description, a posting time, a map point or an inventory kind. When a capture is incomplete, the report says why, so one that only ran out of room for new lines can be told from one that stopped reading. Only the field names and their kinds go in, never prices, titles, links or ids.

Local checks passed: 3429 runtime tests and 1093 patch tests with no failures, plus both Android lints and the release-script checks. Most of this release comes from your requests. A video you tap in the feed can open on its own now, so a swipe up doesn't drop you into an endless reels feed, and the comment sheet can open at full height or from a double tap on a reel. There are new switches to hide the status bar, the Messenger button, the counts under posts and reels, reaction previews and the people row in the share sheet. Settings come in Simplified Chinese, new ones carry a small dot, and Remember what you watch keeps a list so a reel that vanished on refresh is easy to find again. On the fix side, Tap the bar to seek works on 583 again and stories you finish stay watched with View stories anonymously on.

New in this release

- New switch under Comment sheet options, `Hide the new comments pop-up`. The "3 new comments" bubble stops popping up over the comments while you read them, and new comments still land in the list. It starts off (issue #185).

- New switch in Clean up Reels, `Open feed videos on their own`. A video you tap in the feed opens full screen by itself, and no more reels load after it, so a swipe up can't lead into an endless reels feed. The Reels tab, the Watch page and a reel you open from a link keep scrolling as before. It also catches a reel someone shared to your feed, which some accounts open straight in the reels viewer, and a swipe past that video no longer lands on a loading circle that never ends. It starts off (issue #161).

- New switch, `Hide the status bar`, under Appearance with the other bar switches. The phone's status bar with the time and battery goes from Facebook's main screen, so the feed gets the whole screen, and a swipe down from the top edge shows it for a moment. It starts off (issue #124).

- New patch, `Open comments at full height`. With its switch under Comments on, the comment sheet opens all the way up instead of stopping part way, on posts, videos, reels and stories. On reels and videos, the Comment button opens that sheet instead of the split view with the video on top, and the reel Facebook keeps showing above the comments, on the Reels tab too, is hidden so they get the whole sheet. It starts off (issue #179).

- The settings now come in Simplified Chinese when Facebook runs in it. Every row, switch name and description is translated, and Facebook's own feature names follow the words its Simplified Chinese app uses. Traditional Chinese still gets English for now. If a line reads oddly, a better wording is welcome on the issue tracker.

- Settings added since you last looked now carry a small dot, on the switch and on its section's row on the home page. A switch's dot goes once you've left its page, and a section's dot once you've opened that section. Nothing shows on a fresh install or in search results.

- `Remember what you watch`, a new switch under Playback, keeps a list on your phone of the reels, videos and stories you watch, so one that vanished when the feed refreshed is easy to find again. `Recently watched`, the row right under it, shows them newest first with a chip for each kind, and a tap opens one in Facebook. Clear empties the list. A video you watched as a reel and again in the video player shows up once, as whichever you watched last. A reel or video counts once it's played for about three seconds, and the list keeps the last 500. Stories are listed when the `View stories anonymously` patch is in your build, with its switch on or off. Nothing on the list leaves your phone, and it starts off. Part of `Resume long videos` (issue #183).

- `Open videos in another app`, a new switch under Downloads, adds Open in another app to the menu of a feed or Watch video, beside Download to phone. It hands the video's file to whatever player or casting app you pick, like VLC or Web Video Caster, so you can watch it elsewhere or send it to a TV. A video with no single file to hand over says so, and it starts off (issue #182).

- `Menu tiles to hide`, a new list under Menu, takes the tiles you tick out of the Menu's shortcut grid, Marketplace and Gaming for example. Tiles are matched by where they open, not by their name, so it works in any language. The next tile moves up, and See more and the sections above the grid stay. Pull to refresh the Menu after you change it (issue #153).

- `Download first in post menus`, a new switch under Downloads, moves Download to phone and Save photo from the end of a post's three-dot menu to the start of its options list. Facebook's own top rows stay above them, and on photo posts that list is the More options page. The row under a post only has room for icons and counts, so the menu is where a post's download lives. A post with nothing to save gets no row, and it starts off (issue #151).

- New patch, `Open comments with a gesture`. Two switches under Reels and Watch let a double tap or a press and hold on a reel open its comments instead of liking it or holding it. The sheet is the one the Comment button opens. A double tap that opens comments doesn't send a like, and `Turn off double tap to like` and `Hold a reel for 2x` keep working as they did when this is off. Both start off. It covers reels, not feed posts (issue #179).

- Three new switches under Appearance clean up the top bar on Home: `Hide the Messenger button` takes the button out and the buttons beside it close up, `Hide the Messenger count` keeps the button but drops its unread count, and `Hide the Facebook logo` leaves an empty spot of the same size that still opens Hushfacebook settings when you press and hold it. They start off, and the button and logo need a restart. Part of `Tab bar at the bottom` (issue #181).

- `Hide people to send to in the share sheet`, a new switch under Share sheet items, takes the row of profile pictures off the share sheet, so it doesn't keep showing people you've lost touch with (issue #169). The search box and the other ways to share stay. It starts off.

- `Hide who is typing in comments`, a new switch under Comment sheet options, takes away the line that says someone is typing a comment (issue #170). Your own typing stays a separate switch under Privacy. It starts off.

- `Hide the search pill on reels`, a new switch under Reels and Watch, takes the search suggestion out from under a reel's caption (issue #173). It starts off and shows from the next reel. Part of `Clean up Reels`.

- `Hide counts on posts`, a new switch under News feed, takes the numbers off the Like, Comment and Share buttons under posts, so each button shows just its word. `Hide counts on reels`, a new switch under Reels and Watch, takes the numbers away from under a reel's Like, Comment and Share icons, and the icons stay put. Both start off and show on what's drawn after the change. They're part of `Hide post prompts` and `Clean up Reels` (issue #180).

- `Hide the reaction preview on posts`, a new switch under News feed, stops drawing the stacked reaction icons at the end of the button row and the reactions count under a post (issue #158). The space stays where it was. It starts off. Part of `Hide post prompts`.

- `Hide the reaction preview on comments`, a new switch under Comments, stops drawing a comment's reaction icons, whether they sit in the corner of the comment or next to its reaction count on Facebook's newer comment layout (issue #158). The space stays, so a tap where they were still opens the list of reactions. It starts off and shows on the comments drawn after you change it. The switch for posts leaves comments alone, and this one leaves posts alone. Part of `Hide post prompts`.

- An empty `hushfacebook-safe-mode` file in `Android/media/com.facebook.katana` now pauses Hushfacebook too, like the one in `Android/data`. Android 11 doesn't let adb write in `Android/data`, and the media folder is the way around that. The settings name whichever folder the file is in, and `Resume` deletes both.

- Two new switches under Menu, `Open settings from the logo` and `Settings row in Menu`, sit next to `Settings shortcut on the app icon`, so you pick which ways into the settings stay (issue #146). Both start on. The last one still on stays on and greys out, so there's always a way back in.

- `Picture-in-picture button`, a new switch under Playback, floats a small button at the left edge of a reel or video that has the window ready. Tap it and the window opens right away, the same one the More menu row opens (issue #44). It starts off, needs Picture-in-picture on, and goes away while the window is open.

- With Debug logging on, the diagnostic report says why a game didn't open. When Facebook's download screen for a game closes, the screens list gets what it was downloading and the error Facebook kept, so a game that shuts right away can be traced from one report (issue #168).

Fixes

- With a reel floating in the `Picture-in-picture` window, opening Facebook again from the home screen no longer lets a video playing on Home take the window over. The window stays with the reel that's floating.

- `Hide Upgrades` and `Hide Also from Meta` now bring up the restart button when you flip them (issue #184). A Menu Facebook already built kept both sections on screen until Facebook started again, so turning either switch on looked like it did nothing.

- `Tap the bar to seek` jumps to where you tap on Facebook 583 again (issue #120). Facebook now starts a scrub a moment after the drag begins, and the tap's seek landed before that start, which put the video right back where it was.

- With `View stories anonymously` on, a story you watched to the end now stays watched when Facebook restarts or reloads the story tray (issues #61 and #165). Facebook builds the tray a few times over as it starts, the last time from its servers, and only the first of those got marked, so the ring came back blue.

- `See-through bars` work with the tab bar at the top now (issue #171). Facebook stacks the top bar and the tab bar in one holder there, and neither bar's color was big enough to count. The blur behind a bar also stays inside the bar on phones whose tab bar holder reaches above the tabs, where it showed as a blurred strip of the feed. Pages that play video on their own surface skip the blur and keep just the see-through color, since drawing that video a second time could turn the Reels tab black.

- Coming back from the `Picture-in-picture` window no longer puts a purple button over the top right of the reel (issue #126). That was Facebook Flex's switch button. Facebook hides everything on the screen while the window is open, then shows all of it again on the way back, even parts that were never meant to show, and that built the switcher bar and a few other pieces in the reel viewer. Now everything comes back the way it was before the window opened.

- The diagnostics report keeps every Picture-in-picture count again. It had room for 16 named counts per feature, and Picture-in-picture has more than that, so whichever came last in a session were left out. It keeps 24 now.

- A saved video whose sample description gives its size as 0 now gets the description's real size. Read on its own, 0 means "to the end", but players reading the box it sits in take it as no size and refuse the whole file. The parser fuzzer found this on its third MP4 hour.

- Picking an app icon no longer replaces the Facebook wordmark at the top of Home (issue #172). `Use the icon at the top of Home`, a new switch under Appearance, puts your picked icon there instead. It starts off and needs a restart.

Behind the scenes

- The source ledger is settled for 2026-10-18: new pins for the moved Facebook sources, Messenger-Z and Messenger-Pro, the NexAlloyNext port and five new forks recorded, and the deleted anemia004 repository and Shuhaib's removed Lite patch marked unavailable and retired. The audit now reads the Morphe Patch Tracker's mixed-case keys and Jman's new registry API, retries a request that times out, waits out a rate limit for longer (as long as the server asks, up to 15 minutes), and checks release fixtures by build and version code. GitLab sources are now read from a local mirror that keeps commits and folder names but no file contents, so a census sends gitlab.com a handful of requests per source instead of a few hundred. A repository an index files under a Facebook package it doesn't patch stays settled once its record names that package, and comes back up if the index names another one.

- A source audit that skips GitLab's global code search can stamp the census again. GitLab.com doesn't offer that search at all, so since 2026-10-03 no census could ever be refreshed and every release would have stopped at the 14-day check. The census still lists `gitlab-code-search` under skipped each time, the report keeps the reason, and a search that runs and gets refused, or any other gap, still fails the audit.

- The device audit now checks its device lease and input window before sending input. Failed imports, missing pages and unproved destinations fail the run. Settings, language and theme restore independently, with recovery files kept if anything fails. A baseline is replaced only after the full run and recovery pass.

- The device audit starts Facebook through the launcher entry the phone has turned on, so a run, and the phone smoke walk, still work after you pick another app icon. They read the entry from the phone, never change a component, and stop before touching any setting if they find none or more than one.

- The device audit's walk gets through a test account with no profile picture and the pages Facebook's links open now. Notifications restored partway down, the profile's Add profile picture button and the Menu opened as a page of its own all count as arrived. A row that repeats its label on a part inside it, like the Menu's Settings and privacy, can be tapped, and the tap still has to land inside that row.

- The device audit's Watch and Shorts stops no longer hang on a playing reel. The phone can't read a screen while a video plays, so the walk now proves the reel viewer from Facebook's own screen state: the right screen in front and the reel page showing, with nothing hiding it. A reel stop still takes swipes and Back but never a tap, since a second tap likes the reel.

- The device audit's walk no longer types stray letters into Facebook search. Search opens with the keyboard up, and the walk's swipes across it were typing into the search box. The walk now sends no swipe or tap while a keyboard is open. A new search step types one fixed word and submits it, so the search hooks run on purpose instead of by accident. Typing anything else, or typing at any other step, is refused.

- The script contract tests pass on a published index again. Their check that the release facts refuse a second Facebook build swapped one into the CHANGELOG part of the index, which the facts check skips on purpose, so it failed as soon as a changelog bullet named the target build. It now swaps it into the facts.

This release moves Hushfacebook to Facebook 583.0.0.39.55. There are new patches to skip the quiet stretches in videos and to post Stories in HD, plus switches that put the tab bar back at the top, keep a reel's original sound instead of a Meta AI dub, give tablets the phone layout and hide the Meta AI shortcut in the Menu. Picture-in-picture got a round of fixes, and dark mode with Material You shouldn't crash Facebook on Android 12 and newer anymore.

New in this release

- `Settings shortcut on the app icon`, a new switch under Menu, takes Hushfacebook settings out of the menu you get by holding Facebook's icon (issue #146). It starts on. The Menu row and the logo long press open settings either way, and Pause leaves the choice alone.

- New patch, `Hide carrier data banners`, for carriers with Facebook Flex (issue #70). `Hide the Data mode banner` takes away the Data mode bar and its buy mobile data button, and `Hide the Free mode banner` takes away the purple Free mode bar. Both switches are under Appearance and start off.

- `Picture-in-picture` puts a `Picture-in-picture` row in a reel's More menu, so a reel can float in the small window without leaving Facebook (issue #44). The new `Only from a reel's More menu` switch under it starts off. Turn it on and leaving Facebook no longer opens the window, so the row is the only way in.

- `Material You theme` colors Facebook's light mode too (issues #141 and #65). In light mode the grays, the blues, the pale blue highlights and the selected tab take your wallpaper's colors at the same lightness, so text stays as easy to read. White stays white, and dark mode looks as it did. There's no new switch.

- New patch, `Skip silent parts`, plays videos, reels and stories past the quiet stretches in their sound, so talks and how-tos get to the point sooner (issue #144). Its switch is under Playback and starts off. A change takes effect from the next video or the next seek.

- `Load whole reply threads` under Comment sheet options keeps loading an open reply thread as you scroll, so you don't have to keep tapping View more replies (issue #140). It starts off.

- New patch, `Upload Stories in HD`, makes videos you post to your Story ask Facebook for its high upload quality instead of standard, so they can come out sharper (issue #123). Its switch is under Stories and starts off. Facebook's servers still pick the final quality.

- `Keep the original audio`, a new switch under Reels and Watch, plays reels and videos with the sound they were made with instead of a Meta AI dubbed track (issue #148). It starts off and takes effect from the next video.

- `Save photo on more stories`, a new switch under Stories, adds Save photo to photo stories with music, which Facebook plays as videos (issue #38). Save photo also takes the story's photo at the biggest size Meta serves, on Android 12 and newer. It starts off.

- `Phone layout on big screens`, a new switch under Appearance, gives tablets and unfolded phones Facebook's phone layout, so the tab bar switches work there too (issue #149). It starts off, needs a restart, and drops Facebook's wider big screen layout while it's on.

- `Play SDR versions of HDR videos`, a new switch under Playback, plays the regular copy of an HDR video when Facebook sends one at the same size, so the screen doesn't brighten and the picture stays as sharp (issue #66). It starts off.

- `See-through bars`, a new switch under Appearance, lets the feed show through the top bar and the tab bar as you scroll, frosted on Android 12 and newer (issue #124). It starts off. The status bar strip above Facebook's top bar stays solid.

- A `Restart Facebook` row now sits at the end of the settings home page, just above Support Hushfacebook, so you can restart Facebook from settings whenever you like (issue #155). It steps aside while a changed switch is waiting for its own restart row.

- The settings now come in Vietnamese when Facebook runs in Vietnamese (issue #152). Every row, switch name and description is translated. Some of Facebook's own feature names may read a little differently from the app's, and a better wording is welcome on the issue.

- `Hide more posts under notification posts`, a new switch under News feed, opens a post from a notification without the "More from your friends" list Facebook adds under it, which can carry ads (issue #163). It starts off and takes effect from the next post you open.

- `Tab bar at the top`, a new switch under Appearance, puts Facebook's tab bar back at the top, under the search row, as older Facebook had it (issue #166). It starts off and needs a restart. With `Tab bar at the bottom` on too, the bottom one wins and this one greys out.

After a restart the tab bar keeps Events, Notifications and Profile/Menu, and Facebook opens on Events. Pin Events under Settings, Tab bar, Customize the bar first if your bar doesn't show it. It starts off. If Marketplace only is on too, that one wins and this one greys out. Return to regular Facebook turns both off.

Fixes

- `Hide GIF and sticker buttons` now also clears those two buttons from the comment bar under a video in the full-screen video viewer. Before, it only reached the comment box in the comment sheet.

- A switch that another one overrides now says which one to turn off, the way rows that need another switch already said which one to turn on. That covers `Events only` under `Marketplace only`, `Tab bar at the top` under `Tab bar at the bottom` and `Keep the tab bar on screen` under `Hide the tab bar while scrolling`. `Loop stories` and `Lock after` now grey out while `Stop Story auto-advance` or `Lock Facebook` is off, since they do nothing without them. With `Events only` on, the `Marketplace only` row no longer reports Events' state as its own, and the other way around. On Opening Facebook, `Marketplace only`'s two follow-up switches now sit right under it. Each thing set when you patched has one name across the Pause page, `Set when you patched` and the ads list under Privacy, so "Ad tracking blocked" and "Block ad telemetry" no longer read like two different things.

- `Leave calls and chats to Messenger` no longer leaves incoming calls silent in both apps (issue #157). When the switch is on and Messenger is installed and enabled, Facebook stops registering itself for Messenger calls at its next start, so the call reaches Messenger instead. Facebook's local call blocks stay as a fallback for calls already sent its way. Restart Facebook after changing the switch or installing, enabling or disabling Messenger.

- `Keep the top bar on screen` no longer leaves the top bar sitting over the Reels tab (issue #159). Facebook hides its bars itself as it opens Reels or a full-screen page and brings them back on the feed, and the kept bar now goes along with that. On the feed it stays put as before.

- With `Material You theme` in your build, dark mode no longer crashes Facebook as the feed loads on Android 12 and newer (issue #154). The likes line under a post reads its text color as a plain number, and the theme had turned that color into a day and night pair it couldn't read. The colors Facebook reads that way now get the nearest plain wallpaper tone instead. Light mode and the rest of dark mode look as they did.

- A copy made with Clone app builds Facebook's rich notifications from its own layouts, so a notification no longer closes the clone (issue #36). Tapping a push or chat notification opens the clone instead of the stock app, and the notification's icon and color come from the clone. There's no switch.

- A copy made with Clone app no longer closes when you tap the chat icon at the top (issue #113). Facebook's chat backup looks for the app among Meta's own by its package name and gave up on the clone's renamed one. The clone now answers to Facebook's name there.

- `Turn off HDR brightness` no longer leaves HLG reels bright and warm (issue #93). HLG video reaches the decoder at the usual range in its own colors, the way HDR10 reels already did.

- With `Tap to play` on, tapping a reel in the Reels row on Home plays that reel right away, since the tap already asked for it (issue #106). Reels sitting in the feed still wait for a tap.

- Home keeps loading posts when Hushfacebook hides most of a page. Once the end of the list is on screen, it asks Facebook for the next page again, at most every 2 seconds, and stays stock while paused.

- Home no longer stops showing new posts while it keeps loading them after the phone's accessibility state changes, for example when a screen reader or another accessibility service turns on or off. The diagnostic report counts the rows and layouts Facebook would have held back after such a change.

- Picture-in-picture no longer opens on the reel next to the one you were watching (issue #126). Facebook gets the next reel ready by playing it for a split second off screen, and the window used to follow it there. It now stays with the reel on screen.

- Picture-in-picture no longer opens on Facebook's whole screen with a purple block where the reel should be, which could happen after you'd opened the window back up full screen (issue #126). Facebook doesn't always get the window ready again after that, so when it doesn't, the patch does it for the reel you're watching.

- Picture-in-picture opens each reel in its own shape after a swipe, so a landscape reel no longer opens a tall window around a wide video (issue #126). Like Facebook's own window, it opens none for a reel wider than square.

- With `Keep the progress bar` on, a reel's bar and time don't stay frozen on the last reel when Facebook moves on without handing the bar over, and they no longer read 0:00 over the old length (issues #90 and #120). The bar hides until the new reel takes it, then comes back with that reel's own time. After a fast double swipe, the bar no longer sits at the start with no time while the new reel plays. When Facebook's update stops before it has drawn the new reel, the patch starts it again until it does.

- The Mark as seen eye on a story shows with the story's header right away, instead of half a second later, and hides with the header while you hold the story (issue #150).

- With `AMOLED black theme` or `Material You theme`, the ring between a post's overlapping reaction icons shows the page through it, so it can't come out as white boxes on a dark page (issue #147). In dark mode the discs behind the reaction icons under a post, in the likes line and in the reactions header take the page color too.

- Turning `Keep the progress bar` on or off while Reels is open changes the reel you're watching right away (issue #73). The bar used to stay thin after turning it on, or stay full size with its time stuck after turning it off, until you touched it or restarted Facebook. Turning it on also lifts that reel's caption above the bar, so the time no longer covers it. That now also works when the reel plays on or loops right after you close the settings, and for the next reel Facebook had already laid out.

- The README's Help entry on Facebook links now names the Messenger setting that stops Messenger claiming facebook.com links: Open supported links, or In your browser on newer Android (issue #111).

- `Hide Meta AI questions under posts` also takes away the row of Meta AI question chips Facebook puts under some photos and captions (issue #48). Those chips came through a different part of the post than the questions the switch already caught. It's under News feed and starts on.

- With `Use the system font` on, a font that draws past its own line box keeps its extra room in Reels captions and other text with a set line height, so letter tails and Bengali vowel signs aren't cut off (issue #96).

- With `AMOLED black theme` or `Material You theme` in your build, the time on Facebook's older comment row (left of Like and Reply) can't come out too dark to read on a dark page anymore (issue #138). It falls back to Facebook's own gray, themed like the rest. Light mode looks as it did.

- With `Material You theme`, the box under a link post (the site and title) takes your wallpaper's colors when Facebook doesn't send that box a color of its own (issue #37). Light mode stays as it was.

How to update

1. Update Morphe Manager to 1.34.0 or newer, then refresh the Hushfacebook source.
2. Patch Facebook `583.0.0.39.55`. On most phones that's build `475614366`, the arm64-v8a one. Phones with a 32-bit processor take build `475614365`, the armeabi-v7a one.
