What was checked

Local checks passed: 3003 runtime tests and 1007 patch tests with no failures, plus both Android lints and the release-script checks. All 91 patches applied without forcing to Facebook 583.0.0.39.55, both the arm64-v8a and the 32-bit build, and a second build of the same commit matched this bundle class by class. I patched 583 with a development build of these patches and installed it over the build already on an Android 16 emulator. Facebook opened signed in with no crash, took a profile with every switch on, and the whole-app audit saw the same hook families run as it did on 582. The Hushfacebook row at the end of the Menu's Settings and privacy group opened the settings. That emulator runs the 64-bit build, so the fixes only the 32-bit build needed were checked by the patch tests alone.

This release gathers everything since v0.12.0 and still brings 88 patches for Facebook 582.0.0.50.54. New switches hide reposts, save the picture behind a photo Story with music, take the Meta AI button out of Chats and keep saves quiet. With Picture-in-picture on, a link that opens while a reel floats brings Facebook back full screen. Link posts leave Home on 582 again, the kept top bar stops fading, and a reel waiting to play starts its bar at the beginning. A failed save says why, Morphe Manager shows this release's whole list of changes, and the Reported issues list below maps each report this release touches.

New in this release

- `Hide posts by words` has a new switch under News feed, `Hide reposts` (issue #133). With it on, a post that shares someone else's post stays out of the feed, whether the person sharing it wrote anything above it or not. Posts people write themselves stay, and so does any post Hushfacebook can't read. The diagnostic report counts how many it hid and keeps nothing a post says. It starts off, and a change applies to the posts Facebook loads next.

- A photo Story with music gets `Save photo` in its menu next to Save, with `Save any story` on (issue #38). Facebook plays that kind of Story as a video made from the photo, so Save keeps the video. Save photo keeps the picture it was made from, at the size Facebook serves it. Video Stories and plain photo Stories still get just Save. It hasn't been tried on a real music photo Story yet.

- `Clean up Facebook's chat list` has a third switch under Chats, `Hide the Meta AI button in Chats`. It takes the Meta AI button off the search row at the top of Chats and off Chats' search screen, and the search box gets the room. Your chats with Meta AI stay, and the diagnostic report counts how often it kept the button out. It starts off and takes effect the next time Chats opens.

- A new switch under Downloads, `Quiet saves`, turns off the toasts a save shows when it starts, finishes or is canceled (issue #142). A save that fails still tells you why, and the WhatsApp warning still shows when no notification carries it. It starts off.

Fixes

- A save that fails now says why. The toast and the `Last save` row under Downloads used to give the same "try again" whatever went wrong. No connection, an expired link, a download cut short, too little free space, a video the phone couldn't put together and a gallery that wouldn't take the file each get their own message now. Anything else still gets the plain "Download failed" one.

- Export settings saves one whole set of choices, even when you change something while the file is being written. It used to read your settings one by one in the background, so a Quick setup tapped at that moment, or a change to both word lists, could leave the file with some settings from before and some from after. That was a mix you never picked. Now it takes all of them the moment you choose where to save, and the file holds your settings as they were then. Exporting while paused still saves what you chose, and import works as it did.

- If the settings screen is rebuilt while you're typing in its search box, the box keeps what you typed and gets the cursor back, and the screen asks for the keyboard again. Android 17 stopped bringing the keyboard back by itself after a change like a rotation, and the box never got its focus back on any version, so you had to tap it again.

- A saved video whose track holds only empty samples now gets a size table other players can read. When every sample had the same size and that size was 0, the join wrote just the 0, which in an MP4 means "the sizes follow", and none did. An hour of fuzzing the joiner found it.

- A video manifest that gives a track an empty type no longer lists it as a track. The track now takes its adaptation set's type, or is skipped when there's none to take. The parser fuzzer found this one too.

- A saved video now carries only the sample descriptions its track counts. A few stray bytes after the last one used to be copied into the saved file, where players that read that box to its end could take them for another description. The fuzzer turned this one up on its second hour.

- With `Default comment order` on All comments, a post's comments that come back as Most relevant or Newest after a refresh get All comments picked again (#110). The first pick held, but a reload Facebook built from the post's first request came back in its own order with nothing to pick it. It's picked once per answer, so a post where Facebook won't give All comments isn't asked over and over. A link to one comment still opens in Facebook's own view.

- `Keep the top bar on screen` now keeps the bar from fading out too. Facebook fades the top bar as it scrolls away on some phones and accounts, and only the slide was held before, so the bar could stay put and still disappear.

- With `Picture-in-picture` on, opening a Facebook link, a notification or a settings shortcut while a reel floats in its window brings Facebook back full screen on that page. The page used to open inside the little window and stay there until you tapped the app icon.

- `Hide link posts` hides website links on 582. Facebook sends their preview card with a template style first and the plain link style second, and only the first one was checked, so these posts stayed in Home. A post goes now when its card lists the link style anywhere and the link leads off Facebook. Shared events and shared reels stay, and so does a photo post with a web address typed in its text.

- With `Hide the Meta AI button in Chats` on, the box on Chats' search screen stops short of the screen's right edge again. Hiding the button took the box's end margin with it, so the box ran all the way to the edge. It now keeps the same gap as the search box at the top of Chats.

- Morphe Manager lists every change of the release your Facebook was patched with, not just a short summary (issue #143). For that one release Manager shows the patch bundle's description instead of the changelog, and the description was a paragraph while every older release listed its changes. It now goes on with the release's changelog groups and bullets after the summary, starting with this release.

- A reel that's waiting to play no longer shows where the last reel stopped (issues #90 and #120). Facebook moves one Reels progress bar from reel to reel, and only a playing reel updates it. So a reel held by `Tap to play`, or one whose video was slow to start, showed the last reel's bar position and, with `Keep the progress bar`, its time too. With either switch on, each reel's bar now starts at the beginning, and the time stays hidden until the reel plays and can show its own.

Other changes

- Quick setups can be hidden from the settings home with a long press on its row, and its help line now says so. The `Quick setups on the home page` row on Pause, backup and diagnostics brings it back. Settings files and the Quick setups choices leave it alone.

- The README's two settings screenshots come from 0.12.0 now, so the overview shows the Quick setups row.

- The README's Facebook keeps closing section no longer says adb can make the pause file on Android 11. Android 11 refuses it with "Permission denied", so the section now points there to patching again without the suspect patch, signed with the same key, which keeps your sign-in and settings.

- The release receipt records what each native library says about 16 KB pages in separate parts now (ZIP offsets, LOAD segments and RELRO ends, each library with its hash). It used to keep one flag that only spoke for the ZIP.

- The `Support Hushfacebook` row at the bottom of settings is just its name now. The "Buy me a coffee on Ko-fi" line under it is gone, and a tap still opens the Ko-fi page.

- A release now builds its commit a second time, in a fresh worktree, and compares that bundle with the staged one before anything is tagged. Every class, DEX file, extension payload and resource has to match by name and SHA-256, whatever the ZIP order or the timestamps say. What a bundle records about its own build used to be taken on its word. A checkout with other line endings still passes when the classes come out the same. `scripts/release/release.ps1 -Stage rebuild` runs it, `publish` won't go ahead for a bundle that wasn't compared, and it adds one build to a release.

- The source census has a tested prototype for covering GitLab, which has no code search across every project to lean on. `scripts/scan-gitlab-coverage.ps1` lists public projects up to a highest id it fixes at the start, pins each branch at its commit, reads each tree at that commit and keeps a ledger of every result, including the ones it couldn't read. It can stop anywhere and carry on from the ledger. A check that reads only the ledger says whether coverage is complete or lists what's still open, and a few known projects are checked a second way against GitLab directly. When GitLab says to slow down, every later run keeps to the wait it asked for, even when that came before a ledger existed or during the second check. It has only read those few projects so far, so the GitLab part of the census still isn't counted and the census still lists it as skipped.

- Parser fuzzing runs build on each other now. `scripts/fuzz-parsers.ps1` keeps the inputs Jazzer finds for each target under `build/fuzz/corpus/`, up to 4096 files and 64 MB, and starts the next run from them along with the seeds and the saved findings. Every run, clean or not, leaves a record of its seed, tool versions, commit, time, executions, coverage and corpus size, plus its full log. A clean run used to delete all of that. It only runs between 19:00 and 07:00 unless you pass `-AllowDaytime`, and exits 3 when it skips a run for the hour. A setup problem such as a JDK without javac now exits 2, like any other failure of the fuzzer itself. It could exit 1 before, which means a finding. Saved findings in `tools/fuzz/regressions/` are marked binary for git, so a line ending conversion can't change the bytes they replay.

- `Block background ad prefetch` now says which jobs it stops, the background ad downloads and the ad-ranking model, instead of promising data and battery savings. Short runs with and without it couldn't tell the two apart on data used, so that promise is off the README and the patch list until a longer measurement backs it.

This release gathers everything since v0.11.0 and still brings 88 patches for Facebook 582.0.0.50.54. New switches leave calls and chat notifications to Messenger, keep the top bar and the tab bar on screen while you scroll, let a tap on a reel's progress bar seek, and take Muse out of the share sheet. The settings home page gets Quick setups and a Report a problem row, and a setting that needs a restart now shows a row that restarts Facebook and brings you back to the same page. You can name the patched app when you patch, and `Pick an app icon` opens Facebook's App icon page on accounts where Facebook doesn't list it. The kept progress bar shows on every reel and stays where you drag it, and the Reported issues list below maps each report this release touches.

New in this release

- A new switch under Chats, `Leave calls and chats to Messenger`, stops Facebook ringing and notifying beside Messenger when you have both (issues #39 and #100). With it on and Messenger installed, Facebook doesn't ring for incoming calls and doesn't post notifications for new messages, reactions, message requests or missed calls, so you only hear them once, from Messenger. Without Messenger, or with Messenger turned off in Android's settings, the switch does nothing and Facebook rings and notifies as before. Hushfacebook can't tell whether you're signed in to Messenger, so if you're signed out you'll miss calls and messages. It comes with `Open Messenger from the top bar`, starts off and needs no restart.

- Two new switches under Appearance keep the bars on screen while you scroll, each on its own (issue #132). `Keep the tab bar on screen` stops the bottom tab bar from sliding away on accounts where Facebook does that by itself. It greys out while `Hide the tab bar while scrolling` is on, and needs a restart. With the bar kept, the bottom of every page stays above it, so a reel's progress bar isn't hidden behind the tabs. `Keep the top bar on screen` holds the top bar with search and Messenger in place as you scroll down, with the tabs too when they sit at the top. It works on the next scroll, no restart needed. Both start off.

- `Keep the progress bar` has a new switch under Playback, `Tap the bar to seek` (issue #125). Facebook's bar on reels and videos only moves when you drag its dot, and a tap anywhere else on it did nothing. With the switch on, a tap jumps to that spot, and a drag can start anywhere on the bar. It works with or without `Keep the progress bar`, starts off and needs no restart.

- `Hushfacebook settings` has an `App name` option (issue #105). Type a name in Morphe Manager when you patch, and it's what shows under the app icon, in App info and on the recent apps screen instead of Facebook, so a patched copy is easy to tell apart. It stays when you pick another app icon. Leave it empty and the labels stay exactly as Facebook ships them. It only changes the name. `Clone app` is still what lets a copy install next to the official Facebook.

- The diagnostic report has a Network section with how much Facebook downloaded and uploaded since it finished starting up, and since it last came back on screen. Android already keeps those counts for every app. Hushfacebook just reads them when Facebook starts, when it comes back on screen and when you save the report, and nothing gets sent anywhere. The count covers all of Facebook, Hushfacebook's own saves included. It's there so a copy patched with `Block background ad prefetch` and one patched without it can be compared with real numbers.

- A running save now says how fast it's downloading and how long it's been going, in its notification and on the Downloads page, like "1.3 MB a second, 0:42 elapsed". The speed covers about the last five seconds, so it drops when the connection stalls instead of showing the old number. Joining the picture and sound and copying to the gallery show the time only, since nothing's coming over the network then. The time keeps going once a second until the save ends.

- Change a setting that only takes effect after a restart and a `Restart Facebook to apply this change` row shows up at the top of the settings page right away. It counts the changes when more than one is waiting. Tap it and Facebook closes and opens again on the same settings page, so you don't have to find your way back. Before, a change like that only got a short message.

- `Report a problem` sits just above Support Hushfacebook at the end of the settings home page. It opens the GitHub bug form with your Hushfacebook and Facebook versions, your phone and the switches you've turned on already filled in, and all that's left is saying what happened.

- `Hide Meta upsells` has a new switch under Meta's other products, `Hide Muse in the share sheet`. Muse is Meta's AI agent app, and Facebook lists it among the ways to share a post. With the switch on it's left out, and every other way to share stays in the same order. It starts off and needs no restart.

- `Quick setups`, near the top of the settings home page, flips a set of switches in one tap. Quiet hides ads, suggestions, promos and prompts and stops the nagging notifications. Privacy holds back usage reports and camera roll scans, removes tracking from shared links and hides your typing and screenshots. Back to defaults puts every feature switch except Lock Facebook back the way it started. A message says how many settings changed, and the restart row comes up when one of them needs it.

- `Unlock app icons` has a new `Pick an app icon` row right below it that opens Facebook's App icon page (issue #122). Facebook lists that page in Settings and privacy only on some accounts, so on the rest there was no way to get to the icons.

Fixes

- With `Keep the progress bar` on, every reel in the Reels tab keeps its bar. Reels under a minute showed it on every other reel only (issue #73), because the Reels tab answers Facebook's minimum length check with its own version and the hook that gives a short reel its bar never ran there. A reel could also come up without the bar right after a swipe, when the hide Facebook meant for the reel leaving the screen landed on the next one.

- With `Keep the progress bar` on, a reel no longer picks up the last one's "most replayed" graph or chapter marks. Facebook takes the graph away when the bar thins out, and a kept bar never does, so one reel's graph sat over the next one's bar until you dragged it. After a reel with chapters, the next one could also come up with no bar at all. Both get cleared as each new reel loads now, and the graph shows while you drag, the way Facebook shows it.

- After you pick an app icon, the long press on the new icon lists Hushfacebook settings again right away. Android takes an app's shortcuts off when its launcher entry changes, and since Facebook keeps running after an icon change, the shortcut stayed gone until Facebook was closed and opened again (issue #119).

- With `Debug logging` on, the report's list of screens opened no longer carries the id from a Facebook app link. A link like fb://profile/1234567890 is written as profile/#, since the report's redaction only caught ids of 15 digits or more and older accounts' and most Pages' ids are shorter. Addresses on Instagram, Threads, WhatsApp and m.me are now cut from the whole report the way facebook.com ones already were.

- `Default comment order` set to All comments now picks the unfiltered row on posts whose sort menu doesn't list the usual All comments row. A diagnostic report on issue #110 showed menus like that, and those posts stayed on Most relevant. Where a menu has both, the usual row is picked, even if Facebook opened the post on the other one.

- With `Use the system font` on, a phone font that draws Bengali or Devanagari itself and hangs the vowel signs past its own line box now gets the extra room too (issue #96). Only Latin letters were measured before, so a font like that could fit y and g and still cut the bottoms off its captions. Text the phone's usual fallback font draws keeps Facebook's layout.

- `No time limit` is greyed out while `Keep feed position on return` is off, and says to turn that one on first (issue #130). It looked like it worked on its own, but with the switch above it off, Facebook refreshes the feed as usual. What you picked for it stays saved while it's greyed out, and settings search shows the same note.

- `Share sheet items to hide` no longer loses a ticked item when the list runs out of room. A settings file can fill it with item names this build doesn't know yet, and Save used to keep what fit and quietly drop the rest. Now Save leaves the list open with a note that it's out of room, and nothing changes until you untick something. When the phone doesn't store the change, the list stays open with your ticks and says so, where it used to close as if the save had worked.

- A real crash's report, and its file in Download/Hushfacebook, can't be wiped by an exception Facebook swallowed on another thread a moment earlier. Hushfacebook puts the report back as it was once Facebook swallows an exception, and it used to do that even when a newer crash had been written in between, deleting whichever file was written last. Each exception now takes back only what it wrote.

- `Hide posts you've already seen` keeps its list through a restart when Facebook is busy. A save that came up while all of Facebook's background workers were taken was dropped and never tried again, so the posts seen after it showed up again after a restart, and `Forget seen posts` could leave the old list on the phone to come back the same way. A save the phone's storage turns down is tried again now too, and the list already saved stays whole until a new one is written in full.

- `Clear diagnostic data` stays cleared when an exception Facebook swallowed just before the clear finishes after it. Hushfacebook used to put the crash report from before that exception back, with no Undo tap. Undo still brings back what was cleared, and a crash after the clear keeps its place. When that crash turns out to be one Facebook swallowed too, the report Undo brought back takes its place again.

- `Font file` and `Use your phone's font` no longer stay greyed out when the app holding a picked font stops answering. After 30 seconds the rows come back, the font you had stays, and a note says Hushfacebook stopped waiting. If that app finishes later, nothing changes. The font it was copying isn't saved and doesn't replace yours. Picking another font waits until that app lets go, while `Use your phone's font` works right away.

- A save that converts a video's picture or sound keeps to the space set aside for it. The conversion used to write whatever the encoder made, which could take room other saves running alongside were counting on, or the 128 MB every save leaves free. Now it stops at that limit and the save falls back to the plain video file. Sound that comes as xHE-AAC also gets room for the AAC it turns into, worked out from how long it runs. Three times the original file, the old guess, fell short on tracks over a few minutes. A photo that comes as AVIF becomes a JPEG only when the JPEG fits in its own set-aside space and under the size cap, and otherwise it's saved as the AVIF.

- Tapping `Download to phone`, `Save photo` or `Save all photos` in a post's menu while three saves are already running now says there are too many saves at once. It used to say the video couldn't be found and to play it first, which didn't help. A copied video link waiting to save says the same thing instead of doing nothing.

- Importing or exporting settings now gives the real answer when the file's app replies right as the 30 second wait runs out. A file turned down at that moment used to get "taking too long" instead of the reason, and a good file's preview never showed.

- With `Debug logging` on, `Hide sponsored profile posts` no longer writes a line each time it draws a post on a profile. Scrolling a long profile could fill the log with them and push everything else in a diagnostic report out. It only logs the posts it hides now, and the report's counts still cover every post.

- Individual photos, videos and photo chains share one three-save limit. Cancelling a save keeps its slot occupied until cleanup finishes, and a failed worker start gives the slot back.

- The people, Pages and sites editor keeps rejected drafts open and shows its count and capacity as you type. Single-line editors keep Save and Cancel with the keyboard in landscape, as the word editors do. Search no longer matches the word null for rows without a summary.

- Font file feedback distinguishes a selected file from an enabled font override. Replacing or removing a font file also keeps the restart reminder visible, including a replacement with the same name.

- Push diagnostics keep newer observations when another Facebook process writes while a record update is delayed. The clock is sampled under the shared lock, so the delay is no longer mistaken for a restart.

- With `Keep the progress bar` on, a reel goes where you drag it again (issue #120). Keeping the full-size look ran Facebook's time writer, which put the bar back at the player's old spot right before Facebook read it to seek. On reels that show preview frames while you drag, that sent the reel back to where the drag began. The same writer sent the bar to the start when the reel's length wasn't known yet.

- With `Show a reel's time` on, the time comes back on its own after a reel ends or after a drag with preview frames (issue #73). Facebook hid it at those moments and only showed it again on the next drag, so a reel could play on with the bar but no time.

- With `Keep the progress bar` on, reels Facebook gave no bar at all get one too (issue #73). Facebook decides per reel whether it has a bar before any of the patch's other checks, and says no for ads and for some reels it flags on its servers. Now any reel whose length is known gets the bar.

Other changes

- The patch list now describes the separate Leave calls and chats to Messenger switch under `Open Messenger from the top bar`, including that it starts off.

- Settings pages have larger headings and connected navigation lists, with more consistent spacing in dialogs. Search and saved choices work as before.

- `Use the system font`, `Use the phone's emoji`, `Text size` and `Accent color` bring up the restart row when you change them. Each one only shows fully after Facebook restarts, and their summaries already said so. A page no longer opens with a line saying a change there applies after a restart, since the row says it and does it.

- Settings search uses the same matcher as the other Hush apps. It finds the same rows as before: every word you type, in any order, with accents and capitals ignored.

- A saved diagnostic report now goes in Download/Hushfacebook, the same folder as the crash files, so everything for a bug report is in one place. Reports saved before this stay in Download/Morphe.

- `Reels quality` and `Stories quality` say how each choice relates to `Playback quality` (issue #90 asked). Their first choice is now called Same as Playback quality, and a quality of their own reads like "Highest for reels, whatever Playback quality is set to." instead of a bare "Highest".

- The `Unlock app icons` summary names the `Pick an app icon` row that opens the App icon page, so it reads right in search results and in every language, and the hint in the list editors writes ID in capitals like the rest of the settings.

- The README is a lot shorter. It sticks to installing, the settings, the patch table and fixes for the errors people run into, and it now lists the SHA-256 of the two Facebook bundles the patches are checked against. The long version, with every switch's fine print, is still in the repository history.

- The install guide now points desktop-browser users to HushFacebook Web and its separate userscript instructions.

- Settings controls have visible focus boundaries and distinct disabled actions in black, Material dark and Material light. Switches and button feedback follow the same small corner scale, and recovery spacing adapts to shorter screens and large text.

- Downloads keeps the last generic save result until Facebook closes, including when notifications are off. It contains no filename or media address. Joining and gallery-copy notifications now match the phase shown in settings.

- Diagnostic export shows copying or saving in its row, disables repeat actions while working, and leaves a readable result. Reopening the page keeps that state.

- With Debug logging on and Hold back analytics uploads off, reports count when Analytics2 requests a retry or finishes without one. This observes the stored retry flag without changing uploads. A job finishing without a retry is not reported as successful delivery.

- Diagnostic reports have a PUSH section for server registration outcomes and timing (issue #83). Separate lines cover FBNS transport readiness and FCM receive callbacks. Records survive process restarts, retain no tokens or message contents, and distinguish an unavailable observer from a route not observed in the window.

- With Debug logging and reel downloads on, a reel missing both known sidebars can add a small layout sample to the report. It keeps actual native view class paths, without reading names, captions or count values, to help identify layouts whose Download button is missing (issue #18). Deeper component paths aren't available.

- Playback quality has now been checked on a Page video story with anonymous viewing on. The 480p ceiling selected 360p from the available qualities, and Highest selected 1080p on the same story.

- The known-issues notes now reflect reporter confirmations for Reels saving and ads. The original Xiaomi Gallery reporter also confirmed full-quality saves play with sound with Save videos other apps can open off.

- The settings pages have larger headings and blue navigation icons, with more space between category links. Controls stay grouped, and the version and build details sit below the current status with a quieter appearance. Pause, Resume and Undo have outlined buttons.

Behind the scenes

- `patch-for-device.ps1 -PatchOptions` hands option values to a patch, like `@{ 'Hushfacebook settings' = @('appName=HushBook') }`. It stops before patching when the patch isn't in the build or an entry isn't key=value.

- `scripts/fuzz-parsers.ps1` fuzzes the DASH manifest reader and the MP4 joiner with Jazzer, locally and only when you run it. It has to find a bug planted in a test-only reader before it trusts a clean run, keeps every input inside set limits, and minimizes what it finds. The seeds and any saved findings run with the ordinary unit tests. CONTRIBUTING.md has the setup. Its first seeds turned up one thing: a manifest's negative width, height or bitrate went through as a negative number. It reads as unknown now, the same as a missing one.

- The release check refuses any change to a published patch's name or default, removals included, unless `scripts/patch-catalog-compatibility.json` records it with a migration note the CHANGELOG repeats word for word. Morphe Manager keeps patch choices by name, so those changes quietly reset what people picked. The baseline is the catalog at the published tag, read only after the hosted receipt matches `SHA256SUMS.txt`, and the check runs with or without a local receipt or bundle. New patches need nothing.

- The fingerprint calibration reads the retired 577 and 580 from a folder of their own, `HUSHFACEBOOK_FINGERPRINT_HISTORY_DIR`, now that the fixture folder only keeps 582. Each bundle has to match the SHA-256, version, ABI and Meta signers `scripts/fingerprint-history.txt` pins, or the run stops and says what's off. It doesn't skip. Two new lists hold the ranker to nine feed, Reels and story menu targets each from 580 to both 582 builds. CONTRIBUTING.md has the one-time setup.

- The fingerprint ranker reads back strings Redex moved into a string table, where the call proves which case it asks for, and counts them as the method's own. The report and the saved signature say which table and case each came from. Signatures saved before this are version 1 and get refused, so capture them again. A build with more tables than the ranker reads makes a signature that counts these strings fail closed, since its true match could be missing them. The ranker also stops counting the case number such a call asks for as one of the method's own numbers, since Redex renumbers those cases from build to build.

- The build moves to Gradle 9.8.1, Kotlin 2.4.21, commons-lang3 3.21.0 and androidx.annotation 1.11.0. They're patch and minor releases, nothing in the patches changes, and the dependency checksums cover the new artifacts.

- Settings previews are refreshed from both Android SDK capture runs, with focus, disabled, validation and export-result states checked in all three themes.

- The source ledger now includes FacebookGoodies, current NexAlloy branches and ten reviewed duplicate ReVanced forks. Pinned source and license records are updated; global GitLab coverage remains incomplete.

- The release receipt has been checked against retained, unforced patch runs for both supported 582 variants. It read all 88 patch results per input without running the patcher again or changing the retained files.

- Settings captures keep separate copies for each Android SDK and include the end of every category, so long pages are checked below the first screen too. Marketplace previews use the current page layout as well.

- Corrected the origin record for the download-speed helper so the source checks pass.

- A fixture test follows the top bar's scroll-away name from where Facebook sets it into the field `Keep the top bar on screen` reads. A future build that moves the name now fails the test, where before the switch would have quietly done nothing with every test passing.

- The release script's publish step now checks that the receipt was made for the commit it's about to tag. It read the commit from a field the receipt doesn't have, so the check never ran.

- The release script's index step stops when it can't read the repository description. It used to leave the description as it was and still say the index was done.

- The patch, receipt and register scripts read the Android SDK path the way Android Studio writes it in local.properties, with the drive's colon escaped (`C\:\\Users\\...`). That form used to leave a path Windows couldn't open.

- `patch-for-device.ps1 -Replace` and the phone smoke test treat a phone without Facebook as not installed. `pm path` answers that with exit code 1 and no output, which the scripts took for an adb failure, so a replace install on a clean phone stopped before installing.

- The translation generator refuses a row for an extra plural form (like "|few") when its table lacks the row that form belongs to. Both checks used to pass, and every other count would have stayed in English.

- The two Python harnesses that copy the whole checkout delete the copy after a passing run. A failing run still leaves it in the temp folder to look at.

- `patch-for-device.ps1` holds the bundle to the sources it was built from instead of to file times. A deleted or renamed source, or an edit left with an older time, used to get through, so a phone could get a bundle that didn't match the checkout. The script now works out the same input digest the build stamps into the bundle and stops when the two differ. `-AllowStaleBundle` still patches anyway, and the output says it did.

- The release receipt builder holds the bundle to the same input digest. It went by file times too, so a source deleted, renamed or put back with an older time since the build got past it. A bundle with no recorded inputs, like the ones published before the build started stamping them, gets the old checks.

- A kept gate run counts toward the release receipt only while it still holds the files the gate checked. `verify-all-patches.ps1 -KeepIn` now stamps the SHA-256 of the patched APK, its report and the merge once every check has passed, and the receipt builder hashes them again before reading the run. A patched APK changed afterwards could keep its manifest and alignment and pass the checks the receipt repeats, while the resource table and register checks it skips had only seen the old one. A changed output, a missing hash or a stamp from before this gets the fixture patched again.

- The release script's publish stage checks the staged release before it tags anything. It takes a copy of the five assets, holds `SHA256SUMS.txt` to exactly the four files it lists and their hashes, and holds the receipt to the bundle, SBOM and tooling report beside it and to the source commit. Then it uploads that same copy. Before this it only looked for the files, so a bundle or evidence file changed after the bundle stage could go out with checksums and a receipt that no longer matched, and comparing the downloads against the changed files didn't catch it.

- The publish stage also holds the staged bundle to its source. The bundle has to carry an intact build identity naming the release commit, built clean, and the input digest of the checkout, which has to be that commit with nothing changed. A bundle with its identity taken out used to pass as one from before bundles carried one, once the receipt and checksums were rewritten to match. The checked copy now stays open for reading only until the downloads are compared, so no file in it can be swapped between the check and the upload. The receipt builder reads a kept gate run from its own copy too, and hashes it there.

- The receipt check holds the receipt's list of extension payloads to the bundle it's checked with. Each payload the bundle carries has to be listed once, with its exact size and hash, and nothing else can be. Only their form was checked before, so a receipt could name payloads the bundle doesn't carry while the SBOM beside it named the right ones.

- The publish stage won't tag a release whose checked copy holds a link. A link could be pointed somewhere else after the check, and gh would upload whatever it pointed at. The copy's folder and each file in it are held from before the check until the download back is compared, and each hold is checked against the path's own file ID, so a link put there before the open is caught too. The download back goes to a folder with a fresh random name each time. Every cleanup now removes links as links at any depth, so it never empties what one points at. The receipt builder holds its copy of a kept gate run the same way from the hash until that fixture's checks are done, and a copy it turns down is cleaned up without following links either.

- Four settings files say where they came from. Quick setups, the settings search, Report a problem and the return to settings after a restart were brought over from [HushPinterest](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushPinterest) at `c5be4d9`, but their headers named only this project. The headers, `provenance.json`, `NOTICE` and the README credit it now, and the app's Licenses page shows it with the rest. The check that holds every source file to its rule in `provenance.json` caught it, along with one download file that had no rule yet.

- Linux codec checks clean up their tool processes even if the private launcher is terminated. A separate guard keeps ownership of the process group, so cleanup doesn't send a terminating signal through a group number that could have been reused.

The [changelog](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/Hushfacebook/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) has every earlier release too.

How to update

1. Update Morphe Manager to 1.34.0 or newer, then refresh the Hushfacebook source.
2. Patch Facebook `582.0.0.50.54`. On most phones that's build `475417104`, the arm64-v8a one. Phones with a 32-bit processor take build `475417036`, the armeabi-v7a one.
3. Install over your current patched Facebook with the manager's existing signing key. Keep that key so updates keep working.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a Facebook APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/Hushfacebook#install).

Look over a diagnostic report before you share it. The filter can still miss private text it doesn't recognize.

What was checked

Local checks passed: 2757 runtime tests and 932 patch tests with no failures, plus both Android lints and the release-script checks. All 88 patches applied without forcing to Facebook 582.0.0.50.54, both the arm64-v8a and the 32-bit build, and the only manifest changes are the four permission renames that let it install beside Meta's apps. I also patched 582 with this bundle and installed it over the build already on a phone. Facebook opened signed in on the first and second launch with no crash, and Hushfacebook settings showed 0.12.0. Pause and Resume each took effect through the new restart row, which brought Facebook back to the same settings page. A full diagnostic report saved to Download/Hushfacebook, and a reel saved at 1080p with sound. The same build opened signed in on an Android 16 emulator too.

This release gathers everything since v0.10.0 and brings 88 patches for Facebook 582.0.0.50.54, up from 87. The new one is `Frame step`, which moves a paused reel or video one frame at a time. New switches hide comments with shop links or with words from your News feed list, let Home show just Friends, Favorites, Groups or Pages, and save crashes to Downloads so they can go with a bug report. The kept reel progress bar no longer jumps back on the first reel or sits under the caption, Material You reaches the Menu's top card and Log out strip, and the Reported issues list below maps each report this release touches.

New in this release

- New patch, `Frame step`, under Playback (issue #95). With it on, pause a reel or a video and tap the right third of the picture to move one frame forward, or the left third to move one frame back. The middle third plays it again, and taps on a playing video work as before. It starts off, and the report counts the steps each way.

- Two new switches under Comments in `Comment sheet options`, `Hide comments with shop links` and `Hide comments with your words` (issue #118). The first leaves out comments that link to Shopee, Lazada, Tokopedia, AliExpress, Temu, Shein, TikTok Shop or Amazon's short links, replies and all. The second leaves out comments holding something from your News feed `Words to hide` list, unless they also have something from `Words that keep a post`, so the one list now covers posts and comments. Both start off, and the report counts what each one hid.

- `Following feed on Home` has a new row under it, `Home shows`, for people who want Home to be just their friends. Pick Friends, Favorites, Groups or Pages and Home asks Facebook for that filter's newest posts, the same ones the Feeds tab shows under it. All, the default, keeps Home as it was. If your Facebook doesn't have the filter you picked, Home shows All, and the diagnostic report counts which feed Home asked for. The choice travels in an exported settings file.

- New switch under Privacy, `Save crashes to Downloads`, in every build and on from the start. When Facebook crashes, the error goes in a text file in Download/Hushfacebook, so it can go with a bug report even when Facebook won't open far enough to reach the settings. It holds the diagnostic report's crash section, with links and IDs left out, and the newest five are kept. Nothing is written while Hushfacebook is paused. The bug form now says where to find it.

Fixes

- A link to a site that isn't Meta's shows up in the diagnostic report's list of screens opened as "(outside link)" and nothing more. The list used to keep the site and the page's path, so a report could name a page you read in Facebook's browser or a file you opened from it.

- Finished-save cards don't pile up any more. The shade keeps the newest twenty "Video saved" and "Photo saved" cards and lets the oldest go. Android stops an app at about fifty notifications and drops the next without a word, which could leave the next save's progress card, Cancel button and all, with no room to show.

- When the phone's decoder gives no sample rate for a reel's xHE-AAC sound, or changes its format part way through, the save falls back to Facebook's single file where there is one and the log says why. The first case used to end in a division by zero. The second would have gone on into sound that comes out wrong.

- Cancel, Pause, Resume, Undo, Add a topic pack, Back and Clear search in the settings show a ripple when tapped. They showed nothing before.

- `Turn off HDR brightness` also asks the phone's video decoder to bring an HDR video down to the usual range on Android 12 and newer (issue #93). Until now only the window was told to stay in the usual range, and a video the phone's own decoder plays, like a VP9 HLG reel, could still light the screen up. A decoder that turns the request down is set up again without it, so the video still plays, and the diagnostic report counts which way each decoder answered.

- With `Tap to play` on, a reel that's waiting for your tap no longer goes into picture-in-picture when you leave Facebook (issue #90). The window used to stay armed from the reel before, so going home opened a floating player for a reel you hadn't started. Once you tap play, leaving works as it did. A reel you were watching in the floating player also keeps playing when you open it back up into Facebook. Facebook pauses it on the way back and starts it again, and Tap to play used to hold that start, so the reel sat with its play button over the time you'd already watched.

- Facebook's push service no longer turns down a patched Facebook (issue #112). On a re-signed build it checked Facebook's certificate, didn't recognize it, stopped and got started again, over and over, and each round could leave threads running, which can drain the battery. It now gets Facebook's original certificate for that check, the same fix HushThreads got for Threads. It's part of every build, whichever patches you pick.

- A save WhatsApp may refuse shows one card in the shade. It has Open and Share like any finished save, says why the video may be refused and adds an `Open the setting` button. It used to post a second card next to the finished-save one.

- Two saves finishing in the same moment keep twenty finished-save cards. Each one trimmed the shade on its own, so they could both let a card go and leave nineteen.

- The Messenger link test under Links writes its result into its own row, where it stays readable. It used to show as a long toast that some phones cut short.

- With `Keep the progress bar` and `Show a reel's time` on, the first reel's bar no longer jumps back to the start while it plays (issue #120). The time above the bar was refreshed before Facebook had checked that the reel's player was ready, and the code that writes the time moves the bar too, so each refresh could put the bar back at 0:00 until the player caught up. The time is now refreshed only after Facebook has moved the bar itself.

- After you pick a different app icon, the `Hushfacebook settings` shortcut on a long press of the icon opens the settings again (issue #119). Picking an icon switches Facebook's usual launcher entry off and the icon's own entry on, and the shortcut still pointed at the one that was off, so tapping it did nothing. It now points at whichever entry is on, and so do the buttons on a notification that open a setting and the Open and Share buttons on a saved file's card. The shortcut catches up the next time Facebook starts.

- With `Default comment order` set to All comments, a friend's post no longer opens with no comments (issue #110). Asking for All comments up front got some posts an empty answer, while Newest and Most relevant got their comments. Comments now open in Facebook's order first, and when the post's sort menu offers All comments, it's picked there the same way a tap does. A post without that choice keeps Facebook's order.

- With `Keep the progress bar` on, a playing reel's caption no longer sits on top of the bar and its time (issue #73). Facebook moves the caption up only while a reel is paused, so it now keeps that paused layout while the reel plays too. Short reels whose bar showed for a moment and then faded out keep it as well. The diagnostic report counts any reel whose bar Facebook still hides.

- With `Material You theme` in dark mode, the card at the top of Menu with your name and picture takes your palette, and so does the strip behind Log out at the bottom (issue #37). Facebook's server sends the card's gray along with the Menu's layout, and the strip loads the gray Facebook keeps for cards as a picture, two paths the theme didn't reach.

- With `Material You theme` in dark mode, the Create story tile at the start of the stories tray takes your palette under your picture (issue #37). Facebook writes that gray straight into its code for dark mode.

- With `Material You theme` in dark mode, the box under a link post's picture takes your palette in the feed as well (issue #37). The 0.10.0 fix waited for Facebook to say dark mode was on, and Facebook lays out the first posts of a cold start before it says so, so those boxes could stay gray.

- In Indonesian and Turkish, the Following feed on Home summary and the Feeds header call the Feeds tab by the same name as the rest of those settings ("Feed" and "Akışlar"). They said "Feeds".

Other changes

New in this release

- New patch, `Unlock app icons`, under Appearance (issue #109). Facebook already carries every icon on its App icon page and keeps most of them for Facebook Plus. With the switch on you can pick any of them, and Facebook switches your home screen icon to it and keeps it when it restarts or you update Hushfacebook. Facebook puts its own icon back on the first start after an update, and the switch stops that. Turned off, your pick stays until the next update, so pick the blue icon first if you want it back sooner. It's in Manager's default selection with its switch off.

- `Stop link history in Facebook's browser`, a new switch under Privacy that comes with Open links in external browser and starts on. Links that still open in Facebook's own browser, like Facebook's pages or any link on a phone with no other browser, aren't recorded for your link history or sent to Facebook as pages you visited. The browser just never builds its two link recorders, which is what it does when Facebook turns the feature off. Login, checkout and autofill keep working, and your Enhanced browsing setting stays as it is.

- `Hold back camera roll processing`, a second switch in Hold back analytics uploads under Privacy, which starts off. The processing behind camera roll sharing suggestions goes through your photos and videos, runs Facebook's models on them and uploads photos with what it found, and another job tells Facebook how many photos and videos you have. Facebook's server decides whether they run, and the app asks one check before it schedules or runs the work. With the switch on that answer is no, so Facebook cancels the work it scheduled, and the count job is cancelled too. Photos you pick to post go another way and never ask it.

- `Show a reel's time`, a new switch right below Keep the progress bar that starts on (issue #73). While the bar is kept, a reel's elapsed and total time stay above it and keep counting. Turn it off to see the time only while you drag, as before.

- `Watch history shortcut`, a new switch under Menu that starts off (issue #114). Turn it on and holding Facebook's icon offers Watch history, the videos and reels you've watched, when there's room next to Facebook's own shortcuts. The Menu's Settings and privacy group gets a Watch history row too. Both open Facebook's Videos you've watched page.

Fixes

- Open and Share on a finished save only answer their own buttons now. Another app on the phone could send Facebook the same request with a guessed file address and get it to open or share a video or photo Facebook had saved, with no tap from you.

- When a piece of Hushfacebook fails to load, Facebook keeps running. An error like that at app start or while opening a screen used to close Facebook every time, and pausing Hushfacebook didn't help.

- The `Share sheet items to hide` list closes with the settings page when you rotate the phone or Facebook closes the screen. It used to stay up over a window that was already gone, and it now follows the page's colors too.

- On a Facebook build that reads the loop setting in a way the reel hook can't use, the play reels once switch is refused while patching. Before, that build's reel player would fail to load.

- `Share sheet items to hide` calls Facebook's Muse item Muse. It showed up as "Share to hatch", Facebook's name for it inside the app.

- A reel's link from Copy link loses the `s=yWDuG2&fs=e` Facebook 582 adds to every copied reel, as long as Sanitize sharing links is on. Those two only say the link was copied.

- `Open on a chosen tab` set to Feeds opens the Feeds page again on Facebook 582 when your tab bar has no Feeds tab. The page showed for a moment and then Facebook jumped back to Home, because 582 treats its own Feeds links as links to Home. It now opens the page the way the Menu's Feeds row does.

- With `Material You theme` in dark mode, the comments under a post take your palette on Facebook 582. Each comment row draws its own gray box there, which the theme didn't reach, so the list stayed Facebook's gray while the rest of the sheet changed (issue #37).

- With `Material You theme` in dark mode, the box under a link post's picture, where the site name and title sit, takes your palette too. On some accounts Facebook sends that box a gray of its own, which the theme didn't reach, so it stayed gray in the middle of an otherwise themed post (issue #37).

- `Accent color` reaches the blues Facebook's server picks for a screen. A profile's Add to story, Message and Sign up buttons, links in a profile's bio and Marketplace's For you tab and location name now take your color in light and dark mode. They stayed Facebook's blue before, while the tab bar and the chips around them changed. Facebook blue and Pause leave them as Facebook draws them.

- In light mode, `Accent color` now tints the pale blue behind a selected chip, like Marketplace's For you pill. That fill stayed Facebook's light blue while the text on it changed, so a teal label sat on a blue pill. It's now a light shade of your color at the same brightness, and the label stays at least as readable as Facebook's own.

- After you update Hushfacebook, the settings page no longer shows a line like "Hushfacebook 0.7.1 targets Facebook 581" left over from the last release check. That line came from a check made before the update and named the older release's Facebook build. It now waits for the next check.

- The `Mark as seen button` eye sits in a story's top row now, next to the arrow and the three dots, instead of floating over the picture (issue #117). It also hides while you swipe to the next person's stories or drag a story down to close it, and comes back once the story stops moving. Before, it stayed put at the top of the screen through both.

- `Keep the progress bar` works on every reel now (issue #73). Short reels, which Facebook gives no bar at all, get one too, and their caption moves up to leave room for it like a longer reel's does, so the bar no longer sits on the caption. The bar also moves smoothly. Facebook only moved it about ten times a second, so it crept along in little jumps.

- `Open the Messenger app` finds a Messenger installed under another package name, like a copy made with Clone app, and the Get Messenger card stays hidden for it (issue #116). The top bar's Messenger icon used to look only for Meta's own package, so with a renamed copy it fell through to Facebook's Chats.

Hushfacebook turns that sound into AAC-LC while it saves, also with Save videos other apps can open off, as long as your phone has an AAC encoder, and the picture keeps its full quality.

The job that posts it with your limit-tracking choice is stopped, and so are the launch event that carries it next to your device id, the GraphQL report of it and the install event sent from the first login screen. Other apps on your phone that ask Facebook for the ID get the empty answer Facebook gives when Google Play services has none, and Facebook no longer logs which app asked. The code that registers ad views and clicks with Android's own ad measurement returns right away, and so do the check of that measurement's status and the test ad audience job. A Facebook build that moved one of these still gets the rest, and the patch log says which one kept running.

Behind the scenes

- The contributor guide maps patch sources, runtime extensions, and the patch workflow. The Facebook 581 audit traces ad delivery and tracking controls, records the signed-in stock screens, and measures foreground, background and screen-off activity. It includes network metadata, two settings screenshots and code search targets for browser history, camera-roll processing and the Facebook Plus icon screen in #109. It separates observed behavior from paths that still need a device check.

- `scripts/phone-smoke.ps1` walks a patched Facebook on a phone through the feed, Watch, Reels, notifications and Marketplace, saves a full diagnostic report from Hushfacebook settings and pulls it. It fails when a hook family reports anything missing, ambiguous or thrown, when a family you name with `-ExpectInvoked` never ran, or when Facebook crashed during the walk. A crash the report kept from before the walk doesn't count. `scripts/test-phone-smoke.ps1` checks the report reading without a phone.

- Settings tests now match the current patch list, switch defaults and supported-link explanation. Story privacy tests clear shared diagnostic counters before each case so an earlier test can't change their results.

- The desktop CLI runs, bundle merges and the resource, register and fingerprint checks now wait for a slot of the machine's build queue when `BUILD_QUEUE_SCRIPT` names one, and run straight away when it doesn't. Before, they started beside whatever builds were running and the queue never saw them.

- The patch tests that read the Facebook fixtures run as their own Gradle task, `:patches:fixtureTest`, with each fixture's path and SHA-256 as its inputs. A change to the fixtures reruns only those tests, and a fixture swapped for another of the same size and date still counts as a change. Each fixture's dex is now read and parsed once per test run rather than once per lookup. `:patches:test` still runs every test, and refuses a run where a fixture test skipped with the fixture folder set.

- The pre-push gate runs Gradle twice. Everything but the fixture tests goes first, so a failing quick test or lint stops the push in minutes, and the full run with the fixture tests comes second. `scripts/release/release.ps1 -Stage preflight` runs the quick checks a release needs in about five minutes: the script contracts, that same quick patch run, the translation and release-check tests, both lints and the release facts.

- `tools/release_text.py` writes a release's text. `cut` turns Unreleased into the dated section with a Facebook summary first, `bump` moves the version and the README badge, `check-translations` holds every table to the same strings and `L10nTranslations.java` to the tables, `github-notes` writes the notes with every bullet kept and checks that the app's update check reads the newest declared build from them, and `index` writes `patches-bundle.json`, the README's latest-release sentence and the bug form. Its tests run with `py -3.13 -I -m unittest discover -s tools -p "test_*.py"`.

- A release patches each Facebook fixture once instead of twice. The pre-push gate now patches the fixtures with the release bundle from `build/release` when the patch sources or the version change, and keeps each passing run with a stamp naming the bundle, APK, patch list and CLI. `build-release-receipt.ps1 -AppliedDir` reads a kept run whose stamp matches and runs every check on it, and patches any other fixture as before.

- `scripts/release/release.ps1` runs the whole release in five stages, each refusing to start until the one before it is done. `source` cuts the CHANGELOG, bumps the version, writes the patch list and checks the translations, and puts the tree back if a step fails. `preflight` adds the release text tests, the translation check and a draft of the GitHub notes to its quick checks. `bundle` builds from the pushed source commit and writes the receipt from the gate's kept runs plus `SHA256SUMS.txt`. `publish` tags, creates the release and downloads every asset back to compare it. `index` writes `patches-bundle.json`, the README and the bug form from the published release and the gate's test counts, then updates the repository description. The pre-push gate now runs the release text tests and the script contract tests when only `tools/` changes, and the phone smoke report checks when `phone-smoke.ps1` changes.

- The marketing script no longer writes `assets/readme-hero.png`, which has been separate artwork since the quieter hero. The social preview it still builds says "Safe mode built in" in place of "Recovery built in", which people read as a promise about Messenger's chat backup PIN.

- Every patch finds its places in Facebook 582. That build moves more text into lookup lists, reads its config flags through new helpers or straight from the config, and folds some classes into their parents or into one shared object, so the patches and their fixture checks now accept each of those forms.
