HushThreads v0.0.16 has 20 patches for Threads 452.0.0.50.64 (`com.instagram.barcelona`), and it patches that version only. It's built on Morphe patcher 2.0.0, so you need Morphe Manager 2.0.0 or newer. Update Threads to 452 before you patch.

Hide ads now also goes after the ads Threads fetches for the replies under an opened post. There's a new `Disable swipe to Search` patch too, for accounts where a sideways swipe on the feed slides into Search.

**Your reports in this release**

- [#12](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads/issues/12) found ads among the replies when you open a post. Those come with the post rather than through the feed, and Hide ads now empties that list as well.
- [#13](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads/issues/13) asked for a way to stop the feed sliding into Search on a sideways swipe. Turn on `No swipe into Search` on the Feed page and restart Threads. The Search button still works.

## Threads

- HushThreads now patches Threads 452.0.0.50.64 only, the newest stable version, and drops 451.0.0.51.80. Update Threads to 452 before you patch. The bundle is built with Morphe's 2.0 patcher, so you'll need Morphe Manager 2.0.0 or newer.
- Hide ads now also takes out the ads that show up among the replies when you open a post. Threads sends those with the post instead of through your feed, which is how they slipped past before. Turn Hide ads off, or pause HushThreads, and they show the way Threads draws them. The Hide ads switch says so in all six languages.
- New `Disable swipe to Search` patch. On accounts where a sideways swipe on your feed slides into Search, the swipe stops and your feed stays put. The Search button still opens Search. Only some accounts have the swipe, and on the others nothing changes. The `No swipe into Search` switch is on the Feed page of HushThreads settings and starts off. Restart Threads after you flip it.
- A download that runs out of its ten minutes now always says it was too slow. Every so often its last wait ended a fraction of a millisecond early, and you were told the network failed instead.

## Tooling

- A release can't go public until the whole app is walked with that exact bundle on a release phone or an emulator. The publish stage now takes the walk's receipt as `-Walk` and stops before the tag or GitHub if the walk wasn't a full pass, saw a Threads crash, ran on some other device, or patched with a different bundle.
- `scripts/walk-app.ps1` does that walk. It patches Threads from the release bundle and installs it, opens the feed, Search, Activity, a profile and a post by their links, then goes in through the Profile tab, the profile's Settings button and the HushThreads row in Threads' settings and opens every HushThreads settings page. A screen only counts when Threads shows that screen's own view, since a link Threads doesn't handle still opens Threads, on the feed. Any Threads crash or ANR since the walk began fails it, and the receipt it writes is the one publish asks for. Its only taps are those three steps and the settings rows, each checked on its own screen, so it can't follow, block or message anyone, or like a post.

## Update

1. You need [Morphe Manager](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-manager) 2.0.0 or newer. If HushThreads is already one of your patch sources, Manager shows 0.0.16 once it refreshes. If it isn't, add it: https://morphe.software/add-source?github=SysAdminDoc%2FHushThreads
2. Get Threads 452.0.0.50.64 (arm64-v8a, version code 512207626) and patch that. v0.0.15 was the last release for Threads 451.
3. Manager's default selection has every patch except `Change version code`, `Remove share targets` and `Trust user-added certificates`. Turn on Expert mode if you want any of those.
4. Patch with the Morphe Manager signing key you used last time. That's what lets the update install over your patched Threads and keep your data and your login. Coming from the stock Threads, uninstall it first.
5. On a fresh install, sign in with your Instagram username and password.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a Threads APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads#install).

## Validation

1004 runtime tests and 287 patch tests passed locally, along with both Android lints and the release script checks. All 20 patches applied without forcing to Threads 452.0.0.50.64, and the release receipt records the run. The dependency advisory check passed.

HushThreads v0.0.15 has 19 patches for Threads 451.0.0.51.80 (`com.instagram.barcelona`), and it patches that version only. It's built on Morphe patcher 1.15.1, so you need Morphe Manager 1.34.0 or newer.

Copy text is back on opened posts, and Open links in browser now catches ad links and lead form links too. Settings got Quick setups for changing several switches in one tap, a Report a problem row that fills in your versions for you, and they stay open now when Threads redraws itself. Saving photos and videos got a lot of fixes, the biggest one for phones with smaller screens, where Save photo saved nothing.

**Your reports in this release**

- [#9](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads/issues/9) found that Copy text didn't do anything on an opened post. Pressing and holding the post's text brings up Copy text again, and the new `Copy text on long press` switch under Posts turns it on or off.
- [HushFacebook#146](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushFacebook/issues/146) asked for a way to keep HushThreads settings out of the menu you get by holding Threads' icon. The new `Settings shortcut on the app icon` switch on the Pause, backup and diagnostics page does that, and the Threads logo still opens settings with a long press.

## Threads

- Don't want HushThreads settings in the menu you get by holding Threads' icon? Turn off the new `Settings shortcut on the app icon` switch on the Pause, backup and diagnostics page and it leaves that menu right away, while Threads' own shortcuts stay. A long press on the Threads logo and the HushThreads row in Threads' settings still open the settings, and Pause leaves the switch as you set it.
- Pressing and holding the text of an opened post brings up Copy text again, the same as in your feed, so you get the whole post with its links. It had stopped doing anything on 451. A new `Copy text on long press` switch under Posts in HushThreads settings turns this on or off. It starts on and comes with every build.
- Open links in browser now also covers the places on 451 that used to skip it. An ad's link button and a swipe up on an ad in the media viewer send the ad's web link to your browser the same way post links go, and so do the privacy policy and disclaimer links on a lead form. Meta's own pages still open in Threads.
- Search's Follow suggestions row is gone too. It has its own switch, `Hide follow suggestions in Search`, right under Hide suggested users on the Feed page, and it starts on. Nothing takes the row's place, and search results and topics stay as they are. Turn the switch off, or pause HushThreads, and Search looks the way Threads draws it.
- Save photo and Save all work on phones with smaller screens again. On a 720 px wide screen Threads only keeps a photo at up to 750 px, and HushThreads took every one of those for a thumbnail and saved nothing. It now saves the largest copy there is, still prefers a full size one when Threads has it, and still never saves an avatar-sized copy.
- Disable video autoplay now also tells Threads' video prefetcher to hold off. The switch only held a feed video at its cover frame, so Threads could still start downloading a held video ahead of time. The patch now answers the prefetcher's autoplay-off question itself, only where the prefetcher asks it, so Instagram's older autoplay checker is left alone. With the switch off, paused or in safe mode, Threads' own answer goes back as before. Checked on a Galaxy S22 with Threads 451. The prefetcher got the hold answer with the switch on and Threads' own with it off, and a tapped video still played full screen.
- The HushThreads settings home page has two new rows. `Quick setups` changes a set of switches in one tap: Quiet hides ads and suggested accounts, Privacy stops most usage reports, takes tracking off shared links and hides your screenshots from Threads, and Back to defaults puts every feature switch back. A toast says how many changed. `Report a problem` opens a new GitHub bug report with your HushThreads and Threads versions, your phone and the switches you have on already filled in.
- More settings is now a heading on the HushThreads settings home page, with Appearance, Links, Updates, Set when you patched, Pause, backup and diagnostics and About listed under it. Every page is one tap from home and Back always goes home. Report a problem and Support HushThreads are still the last two rows, and the patch descriptions and bug report form point to the shorter paths.
- Don't use Quick setups? Press and hold its row on the settings home page and it's gone, and its help line says so. To bring it back, tap the Quick setups row on the Pause, backup and diagnostics page. Screen readers get the same press and hold on that row, and no other row offers one.
- HushThreads settings stay open when Threads redraws itself, after you change the font size or switch dark theme from the quick settings, or when Android closes Threads in the background and you come back. They used to close. They now come back on the page you were on. That holds with the settings open over two Threads screens and one of them closed, and on Android 9 in split screen when the Threads side sits for more than 30 seconds before you tap back into it.
- A settings file you pick for Import or Export isn't lost anymore when Threads redraws itself while the file picker is open, after a font size or dark theme change, or when Android closes Threads in the background to make room. The settings came back as if you hadn't picked anything. The file picker now opens through a small invisible screen of HushThreads' own, which keeps your pick until the settings are back. Access to the file ends once it's read or written. If Android closes Threads before that, it ends the next time Threads starts. Two quick taps on Import or Export open one picker, not two.
- After an export or import, the Export settings or Import settings row says how it went, in full, until you run another. That message used to show only in a pop-up, and newer Android versions cut those off after two lines, so a refusal like a damaged file lost its "Nothing was changed."
- Save's messages are short enough to read whole on Android 12 and later, which cut a message after two lines. On an S22 the proxy message stopped mid-word, and the slow-download one was just as long. A carousel's result now shows each line as its own message, so a line under the counts, like a proxy asking for a password, isn't lost. The German, Spanish, Indonesian, Portuguese and Turkish wording was shortened to fit too.
- A download that only trickles in now stops after ten minutes per file and says it was too slow, instead of holding one of the three save slots for as long as the server likes. A host lookup that never answers gives up after 20 seconds, and Cancel now ends a save that's still waiting on one.
- Cancel and the download time limit now end a save even when the phone's proxy service stops answering. Waiting proxy calls share the fixed limit on background network checks, so repeated attempts can't keep creating threads.
- A save's download now has a connection of its own that never asks Threads' cookie store or sign-in prompts for anything, so it can't send a cookie or a password, and it drops every cookie a server or a redirect sets. It still goes through the proxy your Wi-Fi or phone settings name and checks the server's certificate the same way. If that proxy asks for a password, the save stops and tells you, since it never sends one.
- On Android 9, a save without Threads' Storage permission now stops before it downloads anything and tells you where to turn the permission on. A carousel stops fetching its remaining pages if the permission is taken away partway through.
- Joining the picture and sound of a VP9 save (or AV1 before Android 14) now stops before it would take more than 24 MB of memory, and the save falls back to the single file. A file built from millions of tiny parts can't run Threads out of memory that way anymore. Cancel is also noticed while the join is still reading the tracks.
- When a save finds no picture or video it can keep, the diagnostics report now lists the kind and size of every address it looked at, so a bug report shows why. It never includes the addresses themselves.
- When the regular Instagram app from Meta sits beside your patched Threads, the Links page in HushThreads settings says Instagram won't open Threads posts or profiles here. That's Instagram's own check, and it's why Instagram says it couldn't load the website.
- When the settings list can't be put on the HushThreads screen at all, the screen shows Retry and Back instead of staying blank. Retry opens the page you were headed to, with your switches as you left them.
- When Threads rebuilds its screen with the settings open (after a text size change, say, or when Android closed Threads in the background), a settings page that fails to come back now gives way to a fresh page. Before, that failure would have crashed Threads, since it happens where the settings' own Retry and Back can't catch it.
- TalkBack now reads the Threads logo at the top of the feed as "Threads". Before, it stopped on the refresh spinner inside the logo and said "Progress bar". The README also says the logo ignores taps and holds while the feed loads or refreshes.
- TalkBack no longer stops on the HushThreads settings list as a whole to offer a long press that does nothing there. Quick setups, the one row with a long press, still offers it.
- HushThreads now keeps a note of how each switch starts in the build you patched. When a later build changes how a switch starts, one you never changed keeps the setting it had. Earlier builds left no such note, so this starts working with the update after this one.
- Settings file access stays tracked when a disk write or Android's permission service fails. Cleanup retries after a restart, and retrying the same file can't keep lasting access without a saved cleanup record.
- Morphe Manager lists every change of the release your Threads was patched with, not just a short summary. For that one release Manager shows the patch bundle's description instead of the changelog, and the description was a paragraph while every older release listed its changes. It now goes on with the release's Threads bullets after the summary. You'll see it from the next release on.

## Tooling

- A GitHub description that names no release, patch count or Threads build now passes the release facts check and stays as written when a release publishes. Both used to refuse it, though a description like that has nothing a release can leave out of date. One that names any of those is still held to this release's and rewritten as before.
- The release cut now moves the release check test's User-Agent from whatever version it names. The v0.0.14 prep left that test on 0.0.13, so the next cut found nothing to move and stopped.
- The file picker behind Export settings and Import settings now has its own entry in the source ledger. Its two classes never had one, so the provenance test failed on every full run since they were added.
- When the final APK check catches the direct browser hook overwriting something Threads still needs, it now says which case it found. The register can be past the method's own locals, or Threads reads it right where the hook goes in, or Threads reads it once the link has opened. Each test build has to fail for its own reason, so one that trips the wrong part of the check doesn't pass anymore.
- Save's contract tests now cover the two other ways into Copy link's row call that would skip the Save row, a switch case and an exception handler aimed straight at it. The patch and the final APK check already refused both, but only a plain jump had a test, so losing either refusal would have gone unnoticed.
- The final APK check now holds Disable video autoplay's prefetch hold to its contract. Where Threads' prefetcher asks Instagram's autoplay-off question, the answer has to go through the extension right after it's read and come back in the same register, and every jump to the test that reads it has to pass through that call too. Nothing else may make the call. The question itself, its Olympus twin, Instagram's older autoplay checker and the prefetch dispatcher have to stay as Threads wrote them, and a build without the patch leaves every one of them alone. Each rule has a test build that only it refuses.
- The final APK check's browser guard has a test build only its completion half can catch: a link hook on a register that's free where the hook goes in but read again once the link has opened. No test build failed that half alone before, so losing it would have gone unnoticed.
- Save's final APK contract got stricter. A branch inside the post menu's Copy link case that jumps straight to the row call would skip the Save row, so the patch and the check both refuse one now. Share's jump onto Copy link's row still works. Every static method on the media bridge class has to be a bridge the patch writes, and written, so one left empty or one the patch doesn't know fails. A build without Save has every bridge and the activity reader checked as shipped, and a changed menu is reported at the first instruction that differs.
- The final APK check now holds Save photos and videos to its own contract. The post menu's Copy link path has to carry exactly one Save row, drawn with the calls Copy link's own row is built from and handed the menu and its composer, while every other menu item still reaches Copy link as before. The row's readers, its click and all fifteen media bridges have to point where the patch found them. A build without Save has to leave the menu and every stub as they shipped, and a bundle from before Save had a status reads as leaving it out.
- The build classpath inventory refuses to write when a project's buildscript graph is missing, instead of quietly leaving it out. That happens when a build doesn't evaluate every project, as under configure-on-demand, and the refusal names each one. Its Guava probe also stopped failing every Gradle command when it can't find one of the two plugins. It records no jar for that plugin now, and only the inventory refuses. A refused run also deletes the previous inventory, so nothing reads an old one as this run's.
- The same classpath now resolves commons-lang3 3.18.0 instead of the 3.16.0 the Morphe plugin asks for, which is inside GHSA-j288-q9x7-2f5v (CVE-2025-48924, 3.0 to 3.17.0). That was the last advisory OSV reported for the build's 114 plugin components, and the build advisory gate now finds none. It's a floor too, so it goes quiet once the plugin asks for 3.18.0 or later.
- The classpath the build plugins run from now resolves Guava 33.7.2-jre instead of 33.5.0-jre, which is inside GHSA-xxph-c9ww-hj94 (CVE-2026-102554, 4.0 to 33.7.1). It's a floor, so a plugin that later asks for a newer Guava still gets it. The build classpath inventory also records which jar the Morphe and Android Gradle plugins really load the advisory's three classes from, and it refuses to write when that isn't the Guava the classpath resolved. The bundle build and the focused registry tests pass with it.
- The source census now waits out a rate limit for as long as the answer says. GitLab throttles unauthenticated reads and answers 429 with the time its limit resets, and the census used to wait a flat 61 seconds, so a long reset used up its three tries and failed the run. It waits until the reset that Retry-After (seconds or a date), RateLimit-Reset or X-RateLimit-Reset names, plus a second, capped at 15 minutes by `-MaxRateLimitWaitSeconds`. An answer that names no reset still waits `-RateLimitWaitSeconds`, and a fourth limit in a row still fails the source. The run log also says whether GitLab was read with a token, since a token raises the limit.
- The source census reads the Morphe Patch Tracker again. Its list now carries a couple of bundles twice under keys that differ only in case (immortalzeus:dev and ImmortalZeus:dev), and the census refused the whole file as unreadable JSON. It reads those keys as they are now and counts each repository once, in PowerShell 7 and Windows PowerShell 5.1 alike.
- The final APK check now holds Hide suggested users on profiles to its own contract. It finds both places from the clean DEX alone: the profile screen's suggested accounts carousel, which has to hand its list to the extension right before Threads' own null check and cast the answer back, and the header row, which has to ask first thing on its path and leave by its check's other side through a local nothing reads. A build without the patch has to leave both as Threads wrote them, with no call to the extension anywhere.
- The final APK check now holds Copy text on long press to its own contract whenever Settings is selected. Every override check in the post row has to carry the patch's hook, which hands the override and its own action to the extension in a free local and casts the answer back, and PostText has to ask about its selection switch first thing. A build without Settings has to leave both exactly as Threads wrote them.
- The build classpath inventory now records a SHA-256 of settings.gradle.kts, patches/build.gradle.kts, gradle/libs.versions.toml and gradle/verification-metadata.xml, and the release receipt refuses an inventory whose hash for any of them differs from the checkout, naming the file. Before, only the settings script was checked, so a changed plugin version or dependency pin could leave an old inventory standing for the new build. Each hash is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the file's raw bytes.
- The source census reads Jman's Patch Bundle Registry now, through its registration file and the paged Threads list, because the old bundle files there answer 404. It follows the list's own total across short pages within a request and row budget, reads renamed repositories under their current names, and counts a repository as a Threads bundle only for a current release with verified metadata. History, unverified entries and a bare registration are reported but not promoted, and a list it can't finish reading fails the census. The source ledger points its Jman entry at the registry too, with HushThreads' registration there as the listing's evidence.
- Updated the build wrapper to Gradle 9.8.1, which fixes three high security advisories. The build advisory check now checks the recorded Gradle distribution separately from component libraries and refuses missing or unreadable version evidence, including when online component checks are skipped.
- A fixture test checks on 451 that both of the post row's long press override checks and PostText's selection flag go through the extension, and that a jump straight to an override check or a selection flag written over before PostText copies it stops the patch.
- The release receipt now asks OSV about the plugin classpath that builds and signs the bundle too, from an inventory settings.gradle.kts writes after each bundle build, and reports it apart from what the bundle carries, with its own exception list. A version that was only asked for and resolved to another is listed as a request, and a missing inventory or a dependency that didn't resolve stops the release instead of reading as clean.

## Tooling

- Settings and Turkish translation tests now match the wording shipped in HushThreads.
- The desktop CLI runs, bundle merges and the resource, register, signing and fingerprint checks now wait for a slot of the machine's build queue when `BUILD_QUEUE_SCRIPT` names one, and run straight away when it doesn't. Before, they started beside whatever builds were running and the queue never saw them.
- The device scripts no longer cut a longer device lease down to 20 minutes when they renew it, so a lease taken for a long check can't lapse in the middle of it and hand the device to someone else. They also read a lease's end time in UTC under PowerShell 7. A lease written with a `Z` used to read back as local time, which west of UTC kept an expired lease looking valid for hours.
- The patch tests that read the Threads fixtures run as their own Gradle task, `:patches:fixtureTest`, with each fixture's path and SHA-256 as its inputs. A change to the fixtures reruns only those tests, and a fixture swapped for another of the same size and date still counts as a change. Each build's dex is now read and parsed once per test run rather than on every lookup. `:patches:test` still runs every test, and refuses a run where a fixture test skipped with the fixture folder set.
- The pre-push gate runs Gradle twice. Everything but the fixture tests goes first, so a failing quick test or lint stops the push in minutes, and the full run with the fixture tests comes second. `scripts/release/release.ps1 -Stage preflight` runs the quick checks a release needs in about five minutes: the advisory comparator, the script contracts, that same quick patch run, the translation and release-check tests, both lints and the release facts.
- A release can patch each Threads fixture once instead of twice. `verify-all-patches.ps1 -KeepIn <folder>` keeps a passing run with a stamp naming the bundle, APK, patch list and CLI by SHA-256, and `build-release-receipt.ps1 -AppliedDir` reads a kept run whose stamp still matches and runs every check on it. Any other fixture is patched as before.
- The release check accepts `* **Docs:**` bullets in the section being released, the way it accepts `* **Tooling:**` ones. Morphe Manager shows neither, and neither counts as a Threads change. Before, a release whose section held a Docs bullet was refused.
- A release now runs in five stages from `scripts/release/release.ps1`, one command each, in the order `prepare`, `preflight`, `build`, `publish` and `index`. Prepare makes the version and changelog edits for you to review and commit. Preflight now runs the release text tests too, then pushes the prep commit through the gate. Build patches each fixture once for the receipt and tags the commit only after everything passed. Publish checks every hosted asset against the built one before it changes the repository description, and index writes the index commit and pushes it. A stage won't run before the one it follows, and one that stopped part way can be run again.
- Release preflight clears the test results its filtered extension run leaves behind. Gradle keeps only the classes a run touched, and the push right after read that partial set for the commit it carried and stopped there, so preflight's own push failed every time before the gate ran a test. Build still reruns every test before anything is counted.
- The register check accepts the version code `Change version code` writes. `verify-all-patches.ps1` applies every patch, that one included, and the check refused the build because its version code no longer matched stock. With the patch selected, the patched build now has to carry exactly the raised code, and without it the codes still have to match.
- The final APK check now holds `Block background-return feed refresh` to its own contract, the way it already holds `Hide ads` and five other patches. It finds Threads' four return checks in the stock build by what they log and how they decide, and the patched build has to ask the extension once at each: first thing in the hot-start decision, right before the reset to main feed returns, right before the warm-start check stores its answer, and where For you's swap joins its two answers. Left out, the patch has to leave those four methods as Threads wrote them. Before, a hook that still landed but no longer saw the answer it's there to change would've passed.
- The final APK check now holds `Disable video autoplay` to its own contract too. It finds PostVideo and its playback effect in the stock build by the notes Compose leaves in them and works out which of PostVideo's booleans decides whether its video plays (the fourth on 450). The patched build has to ask the extension about that flag right before every call a single post or a carousel makes to PostVideo, with any branch to the call landing on the question, and PostVideo and the effect have to stay as Threads wrote them, so the full-screen viewer plays as it always has. Left out, nothing may ask and those methods stay stock. Before, a build that dropped the hook or put it on the wrong flag passed this check, and only the fixture tests would've caught it.
- That `Disable video autoplay` contract now covers the calls an Instagram post, a trend preview and an ad card make to PostVideo as well. It reads which bit of PostVideo's default mask stands for the play flag. Where a call sets that bit (the trend preview and the ad card on 450), PostVideo ignores the flag it's handed, so the hook has to clear the bit and load the default into the flag before it asks, and nothing may read either register after the call. The full-screen viewer has to stay as Threads wrote it. The register check gains test builds that skip the Instagram post, ask without clearing the bit, load the wrong default, change the viewer or read the mask again after the call, and only this contract refuses each one.
- The final APK check now holds `Pure black dark mode` to its own contract as well. It finds Threads' theme in the stock build by the note Compose leaves in it, along with the helpers the theme builds its colors in (on 450 the #101010 gray is loaded in one of those, not in the theme), and it finds the dark and light color schemes the theme reads by their colors. Every #101010 load there has to hand the gray to the extension right after, on its own register, and each of the dark scheme's #101010 backgrounds (two on 450) has to ask right before the scheme is built. The light scheme keeps its own #101010 untouched, so light mode looks as it always has. Left out, nothing may ask and those methods stay stock. Before, a build that dropped a load hook or the dark scheme's background hooks passed this check, and only the fixture tests would've caught it.
- The final APK check now holds the HushThreads row in Threads' own settings to a contract too. It finds Threads' settings list, its settings row and the row it draws Accounts Center with in the stock build by the notes Compose leaves in them, and it reads which case of the list draws More settings from the entry names Threads keeps. The patched build has to ask the extension for the HushThreads row once, right where that case ends, on the composer the case draws with. The extension's row has to call Threads' Accounts Center row with its own title, subtitle, icon and click, and the click has to be a kind Threads' row can take. Every other patch depends on `HushThreads settings`, so the check expects the row in any build with a patch selected. Before, a build that dropped the row or drew it in the wrong place passed this check, and only the fixture tests would've caught it.
- The final APK check now proves the spare registers `Sanitize sharing links` borrows are really free. Each of its link hooks puts the post's code and its author's name in registers of its own, and the hooks in Copy link and the resumed shares load the post into one as well. The check walks the stock method from the spot each hook goes in, down every branch and into the catch blocks around it, and refuses a build whose hook writes a register Threads still reads there. Before, it only checked that those registers didn't clash with each other, so a hook that wiped out a value Threads still needed passed, and only the fixture tests would've caught it.
- The final APK check now makes sure `Restore screens on re-signed builds` only borrows registers that are really spare. The patch writes three registers at the top of Threads' signature wrapper before the stock code runs, and the check requires all three to be locals of that method, below the register `this` sits in. Before, a build whose wrapper had fewer registers than the patch assumes could have the patch overwrite `this`, and it passed because the check only compared the register numbers to the ones the patch expects. Only the fixture tests would've caught it.

- New Remove share targets patch, not selected by default. Threads stops showing up in the share sheet other apps open, so it isn't offered when you share a link, a photo or a video from somewhere else. The patch takes Threads' share entries out of its manifest, and any direct share contacts Threads might list there go too. Sharing from Threads to other apps still works. HushThreads settings list it under Set when you patched.
- New Change version code patch, not selected by default. It raises the patched Threads' version code to the highest Android allows, so Google Play stops offering Meta's updates over it. Every build with the patch has that same code, so an older Threads patched with it installs over a newer one too. Threads' own checks of its version code, at start and in its job scheduler, still see the code Meta built. Going back to stock Threads afterwards means uninstalling first, which deletes Threads' data, and later HushThreads builds need the patch too.

The Hide ads switch covers both checks.
- New Max image quality patch, off by default in Manager. Threads gets every photo in several sizes and normally loads the one closest to your screen's width. With this on it loads the largest size it has, so photos look sharper and each one is a bigger download. Square crops stay square and nothing changes size on screen. The switch is under Feed in HushThreads settings as Full size photos, and turning it off or pausing HushThreads gives Threads its own choice back.
- New Disable screenshot detection patch, off by default in Manager. Threads isn't told when you take a screenshot. It stops looking through your photos for new screenshots, and on Android 14 and newer it doesn't ask Android to report screenshots of the feed. Your screenshots are still saved. The switch sits in HushThreads' Privacy settings, and turning it off or pausing HushThreads gives Threads its own behavior back.
- Restore screens on re-signed builds now also covers FBNS, the push service Meta's apps share. FBNS checks the app's own signing certificate before it hands it pushes, and on a re-signed build it now gets Threads' original certificate there too, the same way Threads' other security checks already did. Refs #6.
- New Save photos and videos patch, selected by default. A post's menu gets a Save row right under Copy link, with Threads' own download icon. It reads Save photo, Save video or Save all, depending on what the post holds, and posts without a photo or video don't get it. This patch is experimental and needs device testing. The existing Hide app posts and NSFW mode patches are unchanged. Select the built-in Morphe source alongside this source, as before.

Removes the post-render early return, which could leave Compose feed row state stale after navigation. NSFW and non-NSFW filtering still happens before posts are rendered. Both custom patches and upstream Morphe Reddit patches apply successfully to Reddit 2026.14.0.

The NSFW button now filters incoming feed posts in both directions. Turning mode off immediately removes NSFW posts even if Reddit returns them in a refresh before its account setting catches up. The bottom bar refresh behavior from v0.2.4 remains.

# Gemini microG patches 0.1.1

バージョンごとのフック定義を導入しました。

## 変更内容

- Google 17.54.18.ve.arm64 / Gemini 1.0.958859967のフック情報を別ファイルで管理。
- クラス・メソッド・フィールド・探索文字列・レジスタ条件・期待する変更数・APKハッシュ・検証結果を記録。
- パッチとDEX検証コードが同じ定義を参照。閲覧用JSONとの整合性をCIで検証。
- 未登録のversionNameや異なるversionCodeへの適用を停止。
- 古いトランポリンの記録を実際のaiwk.fへ修正。新バージョンの追加手順を整備。

## 検証

Googleの15 DEX、Geminiの4 DEXと各AndroidManifestが変更前とバイト単位で一致しました。全APK再ビルド、MPP構造・読み込み、未登録版拒否、定義とJSONの整合性、GitHub CIを確認済みです。

## インストール

MorpheのSourcesからこのリポジトリを更新するか、Assetsの `gemini-microg-patches-0.1.1.mpp` をLocal sourceとして追加してください。

対象はGoogle 17.54.18.ve.arm64 / Gemini 1.0.958859967、microG 7.0.0。新しいGoogleバージョンへの対応を追加したリリースではありません。

従来どおり公式Morphe patches 1.41.0のClone appと `updatePermissions=true`、`updateProviders=true` が必要です。Googleのxxhdpi splitの変換と同一キー署名はREADMEのローカルスクリプトを参照してください。Android版Managerでの一連のAPK作成操作は未確認です。

# Gemini microG patches 0.1.0

初回のMorpheパッチバンドルリリースです。

## ダウンロード

Assetsの `gemini-microg-patches-0.1.0.mpp` を使用してください。JVMクラスとAndroid用DEX、Morpheのバンドル情報を含みます。元APKや署名キーは含みません。

## Morpheへの追加

Morpheの「Sources → ＋ → Remote」で以下を登録します。

`https://github.com/ryuya0124/gemini-microg-patches`

または `.mpp` をダウンロードし、Localから追加します。

## 修正内容

- microGのアカウント同期・ログイン・初回権限要求
- クローンのプロセス名不一致とアカウント同期ループの修正
- Geminiランチャーの呼び出し先をクローンGoogleへ変更
- Secure FolderでのWeb転送と利用不可エラー(19)の回避

## 対象と使用条件

- Google `17.54.18.ve.arm64` / Gemini `1.0.958859967`
- microG `app.revanced.android.gms` 7.0.0
- Morphe Patcher 1.12.0向けにビルド
- 独自パッチに加えて、公式Morphe patches 1.41.0の **Clone app** を有効にし、`updatePermissions=true` と `updateProviders=true` を設定してください。ManagerではExpert modeで複数ソースから選択します。
- Googleのxxhdpi splitのパッケージ変更と同一キー署名も必要です。3つのAPKを再現する手順はREADMEの `scripts/build-all.sh` → `scripts/sign-apks.sh` を参照してください。
- Account Switch Lock Bypass / Account Sync Binder Loop Fix / Account ID Fallback for Cloneは無効のまま使用します。

通常領域とSamsung Secure Folder（user 150）でログイン・利用成功を確認済みです。MPPの構造・全クラスのDEX収録・Desktopからの読み込みを検証します。Android版ManagerでのインポートからAPK作成までの一連の操作は未確認です。

HushTelegram v0.0.20 has 67 patches for Telegram 13.1.0, on both telegram.org's build (`org.telegram.messenger.web`, version code 72299) and the Google Play build (`org.telegram.messenger`, version code 72291). It's built on Morphe's 2.0 patcher now, so update Morphe Manager to 2.0.0 or newer before you patch. Sixty-three patches are selected by default, and every new switch starts off. Four of those new switches came from your reports: a red label on kept deleted messages, hiding the new message button, full screen videos that turn to either side, and saving files from chats that don't allow saving. A settings lock you didn't mean can be undone for 10 minutes now, and the settings home page takes less scrolling. ## What's new

* **Telegram:** Moved to Telegram 13.1.0, both telegram.org's build (version code 72299) and the Google Play build (version code 72291). Every patch carried over as it was.
* **Telegram:** HushTelegram now builds on Morphe's 2.0 patcher, so this release needs **Morphe Manager 2.0.0 or newer**. Update Manager first, then patch. On a computer, use morphe-desktop 1.19.0 or newer. The patch count is the same, and every patch still applies to both 13.1.0 builds.
* **Telegram:** The HushTelegram settings home page gets you to the settings sooner. The seven pages of switches now sit right under the status card, and the header, the gaps between cards, the section titles and the page rows all take less room. **Quick setups** moved to the Settings backup page and **Lock HushTelegram settings** to the Pause page under More settings. Search finds both, and they work like before. The long press that hid Quick setups is gone, and so is its **Quick setups on the home page** row.
* **Telegram:** Locking the HushTelegram settings by mistake no longer costs you a day. For 10 minutes after you lock them, the row reads **Unlock now** and one tap opens them again. After that, unlocking takes the usual 24 hours. Changing the phone's clock or restarting the phone ends those 10 minutes early. (#23)
* **Telegram:** Save downloaded files has a new switch under it, **Also save from chats that don't allow saving**, and it starts off. With it on, files and songs from chats whose owner turned off saving get a copy in Download/Telegram too. That's for chats where the owner doesn't mind you keeping things. Secret chats and self-destructing media still stay inside Telegram. (#29)
* **Telegram:** Save downloaded files now covers the files and songs Telegram downloads on its own, too. Before, a file that auto-download fetched while its chat was closed stayed in Telegram even with the switch on, and only files downloaded in an open chat got a copy. Those now go to Download/Telegram under their own names, and chats that don't allow saving follow the same switch as everything else. (#29)
* **Telegram:** Keep deleted messages gets a second switch, **Show deleted in red**. Off by default. Turn it on and the word "deleted" next to a kept message's time turns red, so those messages stand out while you scroll. The time keeps its usual color and the bubble stays the same size. (#25)
* **Telegram:** **Hide Contacts tab** has one more switch on the Chat list page, **Hide new message button**. It hides the round pencil button on the chat list. The story camera button, the archive, your folders and search all work as before, and you start a new chat from the menu or from search instead. It's off until you turn it on, and the change shows after a restart. (#22)
* **Telegram:** **Keep videos muted on volume keys** has a second switch on the Playback page, **Full screen videos turn either way**. Telegram puts a full screen video on one landscape side and leaves it there, so turning the phone the other way shows the picture upside down. With this switch on, the video follows your phone to either side, even with auto-rotate off. It starts off. (#27)

### Tooling

* **Tooling:** A release can't go public until the whole app has been walked with that exact bundle on a release phone or an emulator. The publish stage now takes the walk's receipt as `-Walk`, and it stops before the notes, the tag or GitHub if the walk wasn't a full pass, saw a Telegram crash, ran on some other device, or patched with a different bundle. `scripts/walk-app.ps1` runs the walk. It patches Telegram from the bundle and installs it on a leased phone or emulator without touching the app's data, then opens Telegram's own screens and every HushTelegram settings page and reads the crash log. `patch-for-device.ps1 -CliDefaultKeystore` signs with a keystore the desktop CLI made.
* **Tooling:** The release and patch selection scripts read morphe-desktop 1.19.0's results as well as 1.18.1's. The new CLI renamed its list of patching steps, lists applied patches without the rest of their details, and writes a failed patch as just its name and error. It also skips the result file when it can't read the options file. A result with no steps, or with a failed step, is still refused.

## Install

1. Install [Morphe Manager](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-manager) 2.0.0 or newer. This release needs 2.0.0, so update Manager before you patch.
2. Add HushTelegram as a patch source: https://morphe.software/add-source?github=SysAdminDoc%2FHushTelegram
3. Get Telegram 13.1.0. Two builds work: telegram.org's [Download button](https://telegram.org/android) (`org.telegram.messenger.web`, version code 72299) and the Google Play build (`org.telegram.messenger`, version code 72291), the one most people already have, which [APKMirror](https://www.apkmirror.com/apk/telegram-fz-llc/telegram/) and Uptodown also carry. The patched app needs Android 9 or newer.
4. Coming from an earlier HushTelegram? Patch the 13.1.0 APK of the same build you're on and install it over your current HushTelegram with the same Morphe Manager signing key. New to HushTelegram? Uninstall the stock Telegram first, since Android won't put a patched app over one signed with a different key. Your chats come back when you sign in, but secret chats don't. Back up Morphe Manager's signing key after your first patch. You'll need it for every update.
5. If Telegram turns down your login code with `API_ID_PUBLISHED_FLOOD`, that's Telegram refusing the public API ID that ships with any patched build, the Play one included. Register your own app at [my.telegram.org/apps](https://my.telegram.org/apps), using only letters and numbers in the short name. Then select `Use registered Telegram API credentials`, fill in `apiId` and `apiHash`, and patch again. The result installs over your current HushTelegram build. Keep both values private.
6. Want HushTelegram's own icon, or Telegram's logo in white on the black launch screen? Turn on Expert mode in Morphe Manager and pick `HushTelegram icon and name` or `Black and white launch logo` before you patch.
7. For notifications, open Telegram's Settings, tap Notifications, and turn on `Keep-Alive Service` and `Background Connection` under Other, near the bottom of the page. Phones where Firebase notifications don't come through can also try the `UnifiedPush notifications` switch on HushTelegram's Notifications page with a UnifiedPush app like ntfy.
8. To change HushTelegram's switches, open Telegram's Settings and tap HushTelegram settings, or press and hold the Telegram title at the top of your chat list. The side menu is the `Side menu` switch on the Chat list page.

Write how you want things translated in your own words (keep it casual, leave names alone, a word list) and it goes to your AI service along with each message, up to 1,000 characters. It's optional and stays on this phone with your key. Google's web translate doesn't use it, and it's still there if you switch back to an AI service later. Asked for in #6.
* **Telegram:** **Hide messages by keyword** turns away an expression whose count only makes work, like `/(?:(?=x)){16777215}(?!x)/`, with the same "may be slow" note it gives other slow lines. Large counts are refused now, and so is a count on a look-ahead or right after an open-ended repeat. Short ones like `\d{4}` still work. The lines of one list also share a single budget, so a hundred heavy lines can't add up to a slow chat. A line like that from an older list or a settings file stays in the editor and in backups, but the chat skips it without running it. A repeat that can only stop in one place, like the spaces in `/airdrop\s+0x[a-f0-9]{40}/`, isn't counted as many ways into the count after it, so filters for wallet addresses work. That shortcut isn't taken for a letter written by its number, like `\x61`, or one that matches two letters when case is ignored, like ß or ẞ, so `/\x61+a{1000}!/` is turned away like `/a+a{1000}!/`. Checking that shortcut reads each pair of characters once and keeps the answer, so a list of a hundred wallet lines is ready in a moment instead of holding up the first message after it's saved.
* **Telegram:** A switch you flip while a settings import is running stays the way you left it. Before, the switch and the setting Telegram was running could snap back while your change was still saved, so the next start disagreed with what you saw. Only the switches the file names wait for the import now, and every settings page that's open shows how it ended.
* **Telegram:** A settings import that changes **Use system font**, **AMOLED black**, **Disable pull to archive**, **Hide Contacts tab** or the **Emoji next to the chat list title** now brings up the Restart Telegram row, just like flipping one of them by hand. A file that sets a switch back to what Telegram is running clears that one, and an import that fails doesn't add any.
* **Telegram:** Saving a filter list, the translation service, the sticker size or the emoji next to the chat list title no longer freezes the settings screen while the phone writes it. The dialog dims its buttons until the save is done, so a second tap doesn't start another, and it only closes once the save worked. If it didn't, what you typed stays and the list goes back to the size that's saved. Chats keep using the old value until the new one is actually saved. A save you make while a settings import is still running waits with a short note and keeps what you typed.
* **Telegram:** **Clear diagnostic data** and its undo do their file work in the background now, so slow storage doesn't hold the settings screen. The row waits while it works and ignores extra taps. If putting the data back fails, the row still offers to try again. Whatever HushTelegram records in the meantime doesn't wait for the files either.
* **Telegram:** Patching is faster. Most patches used to read every instruction in Telegram on their own to find the few methods they change. Now the app is read once per patching session, and each patch only looks inside the classes that mention what it's searching for. On a PC, the default patches for Telegram 13.0.2 took about 32 seconds instead of 52, and the patches themselves went from about 34 seconds to 15. In Morphe Manager on a two-core Android 14 emulator, 67 patches on the same Telegram took about 51 seconds instead of 111 to 116. What each patch changes stays the same, and so does every check that makes it refuse a build it doesn't recognize.
* **Telegram:** Searching HushTelegram settings for "null" no longer turns up rows that just don't have a line under their title.
* **Telegram:** **Notification status on this phone** now gives Telegram's reply to each account's push sign-up on its own line, with Firebase and UnifiedPush apart and how long ago the reply came. Before, it kept only the newest reply, so one account's refusal could hide behind another account's success. Accounts show as 1, 2 and so on, never by name or number, and a reply that can't be tied to one account isn't shown as anyone's. The diagnostic report carries the same lines.
* **Telegram:** **Play voice messages one at a time** has a second switch on the Playback page, **Keep voice messages quiet while locked**. With it on, voice and round video messages don't start, resume or skip to the next one while your phone is locked, whether the tap comes from headphones, a car, the notification or the lock screen, and a short note says to unlock first. One that's already playing finishes. Music and other videos play as usual. It starts off.
* **Telegram:** **Faster downloads** has a second switch on the Playback page, **Hold automatic downloads on Data Saver**. With it on, while Android's Data Saver is on and the network is metered, Telegram doesn't start photos, videos, files, voice messages, music or stories downloading on its own, and the next song and upcoming stories aren't loaded ahead. Automatic downloads in Telegram's download queue stop when the hold starts and pick up again once it lifts, though one a chat had already started as it showed the message gets to finish. What you tap still downloads. A video you open streams without being saved for later, so it doesn't land in Telegram's Downloads, and a download from Telegram's in-app browser asks first. Both work that way when automatic downloads are off, too. With Data Saver off, Telegram allowed to use data freely, an unmetered network or no network, Telegram's own rules apply. The hold notices the switch, Data Saver or the network changing right away, and the row shows what Android reports when you open the page. It starts off, and it doesn't hold anything while HushTelegram is paused.
* **Telegram:** Settings say which account they work on. **Folders by chat type** works on the account you have open. A chat or message you turn on for outside translation stays on only in the account you turned it on in. **Keep drafts on this phone** covers every account. **Export settings** lists what a settings file leaves out in your build, the translation service and its key, the settings lock and a hidden Quick setups row among them, and says your chats, drafts and kept messages aren't in it.
* **Telegram:** The **Hide messages by keyword** list editors have a **Try** button. Type or paste a message under the list and it tells you which line would hide it, numbered the way you see the lines, or that none would. It reads the list the way a chat does, unsaved changes included, so the first line that matches is the one named. A line that can't be used gets the same note Save gives. The message you try isn't saved, logged or sent, and it's gone when the editor closes. Autofill doesn't see it either. **Try** waits for its answer before it takes another tap, and when the phone is too busy to check, it asks you to try again in a moment rather than freezing the screen. A check that fails says the same instead of showing nothing.
* **Telegram:** The settings home page has a **Changed switches** row just above More settings. It counts the switches that aren't the way they started and opens a page with only those, each under the name of its page, including ones that start on and were turned off. Flip one there and it's back the way it started and off the list. The settings lock and a change that needs a restart work there just like on the switch's own page.
* **Telegram:** After a **Quick setups** choice changes switches, its note says you can undo it, and Quick setups shows an **Undo the last setup** card. The card names what the choice turned on and off, and how many switches were already set or couldn't change. Undo puts back only the switches you haven't touched since, through the same steps as a tap, so the lock and restart notes still apply. It only moves switches, so the chats' translate choices a switch cleared stay cleared. A settings import ends the undo. If an undo couldn't put everything back, the card lists only what's left.
* **Telegram:** **Notification status on this phone** splits its details into three parts, each with its own fix. The first is what Android allows, now including whether it restricts Telegram in the background and whether battery optimization is on. The second is the push service, with the UnifiedPush app's state when your build has it. The third is what Telegram answered each account, and an APP_PUSH_APIKEY_MISSING refusal now explains that it's set up on Telegram's side, not on your phone. When Android holds Telegram back, a button takes you to where that's changed. That's App info, or before Android 12, Android's battery optimization list when battery optimization is all that applies, since App info only reaches it a few taps in there. Nothing gets changed for you, and anything that can't be read says Unknown.

### Tooling

* **Tooling:** Every build graph this repository owns uses Guava 33.7.2 now, the release that fixes CVE-2026-102554. That includes the lint and annotation tools the Android plugin loads on its own. The patcher's classpath still says 33.5.0, because that's what Morphe Manager and the CLI run with, and the dependency report keeps it that way.
* **Tooling:** The selection check lets a selection with `Black and white launch logo` rewrite exactly the two values it changes in Telegram's dark launch theme, the splash background to black and the splash icon to the logo it adds, and checks the icon names that logo. Every other selection still has to leave Telegram's values as they were.
* **Tooling:** The selection check expects the UnifiedPush receiver's fifth action, `TEMP_UNAVAILABLE`, which the patch has declared since it started following the connector contract. Every selection with UnifiedPush in it was failing that check, the default one included.
* **Tooling:** The build runs on Gradle 9.8.1 now. 9.7.1 was inside three of Gradle's own high severity advisories, and 9.8.1 is the release that fixes them.
* **Tooling:** The pre-push hook now stops a push whose ref lines aren't what git sends, instead of reading them as nothing to check.
* **Tooling:** The advisory gates stop when OSV sends back something that isn't a real answer. An error object used to read as "no advisories", and the gate passed without checking anything.
* **Tooling:** The build advisory scan now holds the Gradle version to Gradle's own published advisories, so a wrapper inside a known high severity range is refused. OSV doesn't cover the build tool, which is why a clean library scan said nothing about it.
* **Tooling:** Two device builds can run at once without stepping on each other. Each works in its own folder, so a second run can't overwrite or delete the first one's files.
* **Tooling:** A device install only goes ahead under a lease in the machine's shared lease folder. A lease kept somewhere else doesn't count anymore.
* **Tooling:** A device build now waits its turn in the machine's build queue before it starts patching, and the patcher runs with a capped heap and two processors so it doesn't crowd out builds already running.
* **Tooling:** A release can't skip the build advisory scan anymore. Release preflight and the build stage both generate the dependency report under strict checksum verification, run the scan, and stop on a build tool or library it refuses. The release gate also reads the Gradle version recorded in an SBOM and holds it to the same advisory list, even when the OSV check is skipped.
* **Tooling:** Patching now checks each extension stub it writes the way Android's verifier will, and stops with the stub's name if one would be turned down. The side menu's name stub was: one register held your user on one path and your name on the other, so Android refused the whole side menu and Telegram closed on the first swipe.
* **Tooling:** Morphe Manager now lists what changed in the release your Telegram was patched with, the way it does for older ones. The release's index stage puts every bullet but the Tooling ones under What's new in the bundle description, and the release facts check reads only the text above that list.
* **Tooling:** A release no longer stops when the GitHub description names no version, patch count or Telegram build. That description is left as written, and one that names any of them is still kept current.
* **Tooling:** A device build now clears out what a killed one left behind. When `patch-for-device.ps1` starts, it deletes any `run-` folder in the output folder that no running build owns, the argument file with the signing password included. Each build records its process and start time in its folder, so a build that's still running is never touched. One whose process can't be read, such as a build started as administrator, is left alone too.

## Install

1. Install [Morphe Manager](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-manager) 1.34.0 or newer.
2. Add HushTelegram as a patch source: https://morphe.software/add-source?github=SysAdminDoc%2FHushTelegram
3. Get Telegram 13.0.3 from telegram.org's [Download button](https://telegram.org/android). The [official beta](https://telegram.org/dl/android/apk-public-beta) 13.0.3 works too, and both have version code 71839. The patched app needs Android 9 or newer.
4. Coming from v0.0.17? That one was built for 13.0.2, so patch the new 13.0.3 APK and install it over your current HushTelegram with the same Morphe Manager signing key. New to HushTelegram? Uninstall the stock Telegram first, since Android won't put one over the other. Your chats come back when you sign in, but secret chats don't. Back up Morphe Manager's signing key after your first patch. You'll need it for every update.
5. If Telegram won't send you a login code, register your own app at [my.telegram.org/apps](https://my.telegram.org/apps). Use only letters and numbers in the short name. Then select `Use registered Telegram API credentials`, fill in `apiId` and `apiHash`, and patch again. The result installs over your current HushTelegram build. Keep both values private.
6. Want HushTelegram's own icon, or Telegram's logo in white on the black launch screen? Turn on Expert mode in Morphe Manager and pick `HushTelegram icon and name` or `Black and white launch logo` before you patch.
7. For notifications, open Telegram's Settings, tap Notifications, and turn on `Keep-Alive Service` and `Background Connection` under Other, near the bottom of the page. Phones where Firebase notifications don't come through can also try the `UnifiedPush notifications` switch on HushTelegram's Notifications page with a UnifiedPush app like ntfy.
8. To change HushTelegram's switches, open Telegram's Settings and tap HushTelegram settings, or press and hold the Telegram title at the top of your chat list. The side menu is the `Side menu` switch on the Chat list page.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a Telegram APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushTelegram#install).

## Validation

1360 runtime tests and 487 patch tests passed locally, along with both Android lints. All 68 patches applied without forcing to Telegram 13.0.3 and to the 13.0.3 beta, both version code 71839. The release receipt checked each patched app's manifest, native libraries, resources and alignment.

On a Samsung phone running Android 16, a 13.0.3 build from the same patch code installed over the 13.0.2 one and stayed signed in. A swipe on the chat list's title bar opened the side menu, its HushTelegram settings and Settings rows opened their pages, and Back closed it. The patched 13.0.3 beta started and opened HushTelegram settings on an Android emulator.

HushTelegram v0.0.17 has 68 patches for telegram.org's Telegram 13.0.2 (`org.telegram.messenger.web`, version code 71759) and the official Telegram beta 13.0.2 (`org.telegram.messenger.beta`, 71809). Sixty-four are selected by default, and every new switch starts off. This release moves to Telegram 13.0.2 and fixes patching on a phone when `HushTelegram icon and name`, `Black and white launch logo` or `Use registered Maps API key` is picked. HushTelegram settings has a new look, a Restart Telegram row that shows up when a switch needs one, and Quick setups for turning on the Quiet or Privacy switches in one tap. You can also open the settings by pressing and holding the Telegram title on your chat list. There are four new privacy switches. Drafts and searches can stay on your phone. Links to Telegram's own sites can open without signing you in, and with `Don't share my number by default` on, adding a contact doesn't share your number unless you tick the box.

## What's new

* **Telegram:** Leaving the optional Maps key blank now keeps Telegram's key, as the option says. Spaces around a valid key are ignored. Invalid keys still stop patching without printing the key.
* **Telegram:** The HushTelegram row in Telegram's Settings now sits at the top of the account settings, right above Account, instead of below Language. While Telegram's new Wallet row is showing at the top, HushTelegram comes just under its divider. Asked for in #14.
* **Telegram:** The Telegram app reference for contributors now points to where the current target builds are declared, and marks what it recorded from 12.10.6 and the 12.10.7 beta as observations of those builds rather than of today's targets.
* **Telegram:** **Disable draft link previews** has a second switch on the Privacy page, **Keep drafts on this phone**. With it on, a message you start typing and leave unsent stays on this phone, and Telegram gets an empty draft in its place. Your other devices drop any copy of that chat's draft they had, and an older copy on Telegram's side can't come back over the one on this phone. Emptying the text box still clears it everywhere, in a channel's direct messages too. Turn the switch off and a draft goes up again the next time you change it. It's off unless you turn it on, and drafts sync as usual while HushTelegram is paused.
* **Telegram:** **Disable draft link previews** has a third switch on the Privacy page, **Keep searches on this phone**. With it on, what you type in search's Chats tab isn't sent to Telegram. It still finds the chats and contacts stored on this phone, along with your recent searches. Messages and public accounts or posts don't show up there while it's on, and an empty result says that only this phone was searched. The other search tabs, search inside a chat and the contact pickers work as usual. It's off unless you turn it on, and search goes back to normal while HushTelegram is paused.
* **Telegram:** **Strip link tracking** has a second switch on the Links page, **No automatic sign-in on Telegram's sites**. Telegram quietly adds a sign-in token for your account when you open a link to one of the websites its server lists for automatic sign-in. With this on, those links open without it, so the site doesn't know who you are until you sign in there yourself. Where the link opens doesn't change, and it works with or without Open links externally. It's off unless you turn it on.
* **Telegram:** **Hide phone number** has a second switch on the Privacy page, **Don't share my number by default**. When you add someone as a contact from their chat, Telegram ticks the box that shares your phone number with them. With this on, that box starts clear. Tick it and your number goes with the contact like before, and the tick stays put if the screen redraws (after a theme change, say). It's off unless you turn it on, and the Privacy quick setup turns it on too.
* **Telegram:** **Folders by chat type** waits for Telegram's answer before it says anything. A new folder goes into your list once Telegram's server says yes, and if it says no (its own folder limit, or anything else) you're told which and the switch goes back when nothing was made. The tab order is sent once the folders are in, and a refused order gets its own note. Turning the switch off removes a folder only once Telegram agrees. If it keeps any, the switch goes back on, and turning it off again asks for just those without making the others again. If Telegram takes a moment (offline, say), a short note says it's still being asked, and the switch waits for those answers before it can be flipped again. Folders made from now on remember the tag color Telegram's server gave them, so a color you pick later keeps the folder too. If Telegram closes before it answers, the next flip goes by what your folder list actually has, and answers that arrive after you've opened another account settle quietly without moving the switch. Folders made by earlier versions are still found and removed the same way.
* **Telegram:** **UnifiedPush notifications** follows the current UnifiedPush rules more closely, so stricter push apps work with it. On Android 14 and up, Android tells the push app who's signing up. A new address is acknowledged right away (some apps drop one that isn't). If the push app's server goes down for a while, the sign-up and its address stay and the Push app row says the server is down. A sign-up the app turned down gets a fresh start next time, and a late refusal after a working address came in no longer counts. An address without https is turned away with a note in the row, since Telegram's servers only call https. If it replaces a working address, Telegram lets go of the old one and goes back to Firebase. A sign-up goes to the push app only once it's saved on the phone, and the same goes for an address before Telegram gets it.
* **Telegram:** **Translate with an outside service** keeps up with fast scrolling instead of piling up work. At most 24 texts wait for an answer at once. Where you stop scrolling, the messages on screen are asked for next as answers come in, and a short notice says there's a backlog (once a minute at most). A message redrawn while it waits doesn't line up a second time. Failures while you're offline no longer pile up in memory, and a request still trickling in after 20 seconds (90 for an AI service) is closed so the next one can go.
* **Telegram:** **Save downloaded files** tells files apart by the document they came from instead of their name and size. Two different files that happen to share both now each get a copy, and the same file downloaded again still lands only once. Files saved before this update are matched by name and size one time each, the way they were before, so updating doesn't copy them all again. If you delete a copy from Downloads, it comes back the next time that file downloads. Turning the switch off or pausing HushTelegram also stops copies still waiting their turn, and one caught halfway is removed.
* **Telegram:** **Keep deleted messages** doesn't lose track of what it kept anymore. A message only counts as kept once the list naming it is saved, and if that save fails Telegram deletes it as usual. **Clear kept messages** does its work away from the screen, says "Removing" right away and "Removed" once Telegram has actually deleted them. If Telegram closes partway through, the rest goes the next time that account gets a deletion or you tap Clear again. An account slot that now holds a different account never deletes the first one's messages.
* **Telegram:** **Translate with an outside service** checks again right before a message's text is sent. If you turned the chat off, turned the feature off (from its row or with a settings file), paused HushTelegram, signed out of that account or changed the translation service while it waited, nothing goes out. Waiting text always goes to the service that was set when the message was opened. Text already on its way can't be called back. Its answer stays hidden while that chat is off or HushTelegram is paused, and if the service fails you won't get a notice for a chat you've turned off.
* **Telegram:** With more than one account signed in, **Translate with an outside service** keeps each account's chats to itself. A chat you turn on in one account no longer sends messages from the chat with the same ID in another, and a different account you sign in later doesn't pick up the old one's choices. Chats turned on before this update didn't record which account chose them, so they're cleared once with a short notice. Turn translation back on in the chats you want.
* **Telegram:** Flipping **Repair Firebase push registration** now shows the restart row right away. Firebase only signs up when Telegram starts, so the change never took effect until the next launch anyway.
* **Telegram:** The settings home page has two new rows. **Quick setups** turns on the Quiet or Privacy switches in one tap, or puts every switch back the way it started, and tells you how many settings changed. **Report a problem**, just above Support, opens a GitHub bug report with your HushTelegram and Telegram versions, your phone and the switches you have on already filled in. It doesn't include anything about your account.
* **Telegram:** Press and hold the Telegram title at the top of your chat list to open HushTelegram settings. Telegram's chat list has no logo, so its title stands in. A tap on the title still scrolls the list back to the top, and it works while HushTelegram is paused.
* **Telegram:** Flip a switch that needs a restart and a Restart Telegram row shows up right away at the top of the settings page, counting the changes waiting. Tap it and Telegram closes, then reopens on the same settings page. Before, a toast said to restart and there was nothing to tap.
* **Telegram:** All 15 settings pages now share blue-black cards and cyan controls on an AMOLED background. Editors and dialogs use the same restrained corners. Switch explanations keep their full width at larger text sizes.
* **Telegram:** Closing settings also closes the diagnostic report chooser. Dialogs on wide displays reserve enough space for their actions at the actual dialog width.
* **Telegram:** Moved to Telegram 13.0.2, telegram.org's build (version code 71759) and the official beta (71809). The beta added an audio recorder settings entry, and HushTelegram leaves it alone.
* **Telegram:** The New Year look switch now says what the snow needs. Telegram only draws it while `Wallpaper rotation` is on under Power Saving, in Effects in Chats, and it leaves that off on most phones that aren't high end. Seen on a phone: the snow stops the moment that option goes off and comes back with it. Refs #14.
* **Telegram:** When your UnifiedPush app is uninstalled or ends the sign-up itself, Telegram is told to ask Firebase for a token again, the same way turning the switch off does. Before, Telegram's servers could keep sending to an address nothing answered. A phone without Google services has no Firebase to fall back on, so pick another UnifiedPush app there.
* **Telegram:** An API ID or hash pasted with a stray space or line break is trimmed, and two empty fields keep Telegram's own pair instead of stopping the patch.
* **Telegram:** When translation keeps failing, for example offline, old failures are forgotten once their one-minute wait is over instead of piling up until the service changes.
* **Telegram:** HushTelegram's startup hook goes in at each return's own label in Telegram's app start, so a branch that jumps straight to a return still runs it.
* **Telegram:** Settings controls share visible focus outlines, readable disabled text and 48dp touch targets. Cards, switches and dialogs use the same corner scale. Dialog headings are exposed to accessibility services. Search updates its heading as you type and keeps the keyboard open when you clear it.
* **Telegram:** Filter and translation editors keep labels visible and show errors beside the field that needs attention. Validation scrolls its explanation into view, without a second popup covering the form. Dialog actions stay visible at the largest text size. Translation fields share one style, the keyboard's Done action saves, and API keys are masked and stay out of saved view state. Failed sticker-size saves keep the picker open.
* **Telegram:** Notifications show a compact local status with a button for the full details and Android's notification settings. Import previews name changed filter lists and show the old and new sticker size. Both backup actions explain when they're busy, and cleared logs offer Undo while recovery is available.
* **Telegram:** Quick forward destinations wrap long names inside a scrollable dialog. Clipboard and message actions explain failures, and pending actions respect Pause. Whole-chat translation now changes its menu label when you switch it on or off. Refs #8.
* **Telegram:** Patching on a phone no longer stops with a `disallow-doctype-decl` error when `HushTelegram icon and name`, `Black and white launch logo` or `Use registered Maps API key` is picked. All three asked Android's XML reader for safety switches it doesn't have, so they only worked when patching from a computer. They now check each file for DTDs, XInclude and outside entities themselves before anything is written. Seen patching both Telegram builds in Morphe Manager on Android 14. Refs #6.
* **Telegram:** Settings now mirror correctly in right-to-left languages, including Back and the preference list. Telegram's host layout settings stay unchanged.

### Tooling

* **Tooling:** Quick setups now builds against Android's public preference API. Each switch still runs its change listener and keeps its value when that listener refuses a change. The accessibility check now finds the heading and Ads row by name after Quick setups moved them down.
* **Tooling:** The draft fixture checks compile again after two mask assertions reused one local variable name. Both checks remain in place.
* **Tooling:** Chat-list title fixture checks now recognize method calls by their reference type. The previous uppercase opcode check missed every call because the bytecode library uses lowercase instruction names.
* **Tooling:** The source ledger now covers the files behind the new privacy switches.
* **Tooling:** The native library check now reads each library's GNU_RELRO segment, the part Android makes read-only after loading. On arm64 and x86_64 it fails a library whose RELRO shares a 16 KB page with writable or executable memory, since a 16 KB phone would make that memory read-only too. Receipts record where each RELRO ends and whether that's on a 16 KB boundary, the rule Google's page-size guide states. Telegram's own language-ID library ends mid-page with nothing else in that page, so it passes and the receipt says so. Older receipts without these facts still validate.
* **Tooling:** Build notes now name both the source and published catalog APKs required by the push checks.
* **Tooling:** The README is a lot shorter now and sticks to installing and using HushTelegram, with the patch table in the order of the settings pages. The long version, with its version history and build check notes, is still in the repository history at commit 0cbd721.
* **Tooling:** Refreshed all 15 settings screenshots from the patched app. Native checks cover the settings pages and editor recovery at 200% text in German, Portuguese and mirrored layouts. Shared dialogs were checked in both themes. The source-origin ledger includes the new form helper, and the README patch table matches the shipped descriptions.
* **Tooling:** Android parser checks cover ordinary UTF-8 and UTF-16 resources and confirm a refused file makes no changes and no network requests. A source check now fails the build if a patch sets up an XML parser of its own.
* **Tooling:** Native navigation checks stop when device lease ownership is lost. Recovery is tied to the original device and preserves settings that were absent before the check. Bounded main-thread callbacks keep the checks usable while the settings page animates. All 12 Android 9 and Android 16 cases passed, including cancelled Back gestures, keyboard dismissal, rotation, mirrored layouts and 200% text. Settings and permission grants were restored exactly.
* **Tooling:** Added the native settings navigation runner and its host checks. Reopening Telegram's existing activity uses a bounded wait, and switch checks read the actual accessibility row. Settings snapshots accept device-specific provider names while keeping recovery limited to the required settings.
* **Tooling:** Verified the original sign-in reporter's successful recovery with registered credentials. Delivery without another signed-in Telegram session still needs a separate check.
* **Tooling:** Refreshed the settings screenshots and added a visual reference for every page. Checked navigation and search on a patched build, including Pause and Resume from a keyboard.
