### Tooling

* **Tooling:** The source ledger is caught up with the October 11 audit (new sources, moved pins, 397 forks), and the census is fresh again. Sources hosted somewhere other than GitHub or GitLab now get their own list with the version an index last showed, so the audit stops flagging one it can't read and speaks up again when a new version appears.
* **Tooling:** The settings screen's code is split into one method per page, and patch helpers nothing called anymore are gone. The release script keeps gh's warnings out of what it publishes, and the release receipt stops on a clone git can't open instead of reading it as a copy with no history.
* **Tooling:** The selection matrix expects the Firebase crash and session report switches only on a build that ships those SDKs, which is Telegram Beta. It also rebuilds the one call Turn off beta debug logs adds to Telegram's startup settings the way the patcher adds it, so a default build no longer fails there, while a call in the wrong place, on the wrong register or added twice still does. With HushTelegram icon and name in the selection, it expects the app and Telegram's default launcher entry to point at the icon that patch adds, and nothing else in the manifest to change.
* **Tooling:** The selection matrix no longer fails every selection that includes Save downloaded files. That patch has the patcher rewrite one of Telegram's classes, which drops two values set to zero and false, and a field left without a value starts at zero or false anyway. The check now reads those as the same, and a real value that goes missing still fails it.
* **Tooling:** The source audit reads the Morphe Patch Tracker again. The tracker now names some bundles twice in different case, like `ImmortalZeus:dev` and `immortalzeus:dev`, and PowerShell couldn't hold both, so the whole source failed. Files like that are now read with case kept, and both bundles count.
* **Tooling:** The source audit reads Jman's bundle index again. It moved to `Jman-Github/Patch-Bundle-Registry`, and the bundle list and patch catalog the audit used to read are gone. The audit now reads the registry's own snapshot: the newest generation, every latest bundle that targets Telegram, and the Telegram patches in each. The ledger points at the registry and at HushTelegram's listing there.
* **Tooling:** Awesome Morphe lists HushTelegram now, so the ledger records the listing and the release check stops calling it pending.

### Tooling

* **Tooling:** The scripts that patch Telegram with the desktop CLI (the all-patches check, the release receipt and the selection matrix) now wait their turn in the build queue that `BUILD_QUEUE_SCRIPT` names, so they don't fight a Gradle build for the same cores. Release runs go to the front. Without a queue they run straight away and print a warning.
* **Tooling:** The pre-push hook now reads `HUSHTELEGRAM_BUILD_WRAPPER` and its other settings from your user environment when the shell has them empty, not only when they're missing, since pwsh keeps an empty variable around. With no wrapper at all, its own `gradlew` run waits in the build queue too.
* **Tooling:** The selection matrix reads the whole fixture APK for its hash twice a run, before the first case and after the last, instead of up to three times in each of its 74 cases. Each case still checks the APK's size and write time, and a changed APK still fails the run.
* **Tooling:** The patch tests that open the vendor Telegram APKs now run in their own Gradle task, `:patches:fixtureTest`. `:patches:test` still runs every patch test and passes `--tests` on to it, while `:patches:test -x :patches:fixtureTest` runs the rest without opening an APK. The release check counts the results from both folders.
* **Tooling:** The pre-push gate runs its cheap checks before the long fixture suite. After the script suites it checks the release facts right away when no code changed, then runs every Gradle task except the fixture tests, the advisory scan and the facts that read the runtime results, and only then the fixture tests. A broken script, lint error or stale fact now stops a push before any vendor APK is patched.
* **Tooling:** `verify-all-patches.ps1 -KeepIn <dir>` keeps a clean run's patched APK and CLI report, stamped with the commit and the hashes of the fixture, bundle, patch list and CLI. `build-release-receipt.ps1 -AppliedDir <dir>` reads a kept run whose stamp matches instead of patching that fixture a second time, and still runs every check on it. Anything that doesn't match gets patched as before.
* **Tooling:** Releases now run from `scripts/release/release.ps1`, one command per stage: prepare, preflight, build, publish and index. Each stage records the commit it finished on and won't start until the one before it has finished. A stage can be run again after a fix, and one that already finished checks its work and says so. Preflight is a five-minute check of the scripts, release text, facts and the patch tests without the fixture suite. Build runs the full tests, the bundle and every declared Telegram build once, and the receipt reads those runs. The release notes builder now lives in the repo too, and it carries every bullet of the version's CHANGELOG section and checks the published notes still do.

## What's new

* **Telegram:** Repair Firebase push registration now works on slower phones. Firebase starts its first Installations request while Telegram is still starting, and on a slow phone that request could get there before HushTelegram's settings were ready. It then went out with the re-signed certificate, Firebase refused it, and no push token was saved. The request now waits for the settings, up to 10 seconds, on Firebase's own background thread. The diagnostic report counts requests that waited and any that still went out early.
* **Telegram:** The beta target is now telegram.org's current 12.10.7 build, version code 71179, which replaced build 71159. Every patch applies and passes its fixture tests on it.

- **Disable analytics** keeps two reports on your phone. One is the device statistics report, which lists your storage folders. The other says how long each channel post stayed on your screen. View counts still work.
- **Disable update checks** turns off telegram.org's own update offer. Those updates are signed with Telegram's key and can't install over a patched build, so you update through Morphe Manager instead.
- **HushTelegram settings** opens from a long-press on the Telegram icon, or from Additional settings in the app on Telegram's App info page. Each feature has its own switch, and you can pause everything, back up your switches and export a diagnostic report.

## Install

1. Install [Morphe Manager](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-manager) 1.32.0 or newer.
2. Add HushTelegram as a patch source: https://morphe.software/add-source?github=SysAdminDoc%2FHushTelegram
3. Download Telegram **12.10.6** from [telegram.org](https://telegram.org/android), version code **71129**, and patch it.
4. Uninstall the stock Telegram before you install the patched one, since Android won't put one over the other. Your chats come back when you sign in again, but secret chats don't. Back up Morphe Manager's signing key after your first patch. You'll need it for every update.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a Telegram APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushTelegram#install).

## Known limitations

- Push notifications don't arrive. Google's Firebase only delivers them to an app signed with Telegram's own key. Telegram's Keep-Alive Service and Background Connection (Settings, then Notifications and Sounds) keep its own connection open instead, at some cost in battery, though that hasn't been tried on a patched build yet. Getting Firebase to accept a patched Telegram is the next thing being worked on.
- The map in the location picker stays blank for the same reason. Google's Maps key only answers Telegram's own signature.
- Only telegram.org's Telegram is supported. The Play Store one (`org.telegram.messenger`) comes once it has a checked build of its own.
- Hide ads was seen taking a live search ad off the screen. The test account wasn't shown a channel or video ad, so those two haven't been seen on a real one yet. If an ad gets through, please open an issue with a diagnostic report.

## Validation

336 runtime tests and 100 patch tests passed locally, along with both Android lints and the release script checks. All 4 patches applied without forcing to Telegram 12.10.6, and the only change to the app's manifest is the settings entry on App info. The dependency advisory check passed. The same patch code ran on a signed-in Android 16 phone. A search that showed an ad with Hide ads off showed none with it on, and the diagnostic report counted the skipped search ad, read-time and update requests.

The accent color can follow your wallpaper now with Material You on Android 12 and newer, and the red badges can take your color too. You can add your own story fonts, pick a different app icon and hide the rows you never use in Instagram's settings. Messages can go full screen, tall reels can fill the screen, and a left swipe on a reel opens the profile. A new lock keeps HushGram's settings from changing for up to 72 hours. The glass tab bar and the like animations got a round of fixes too.

Behind the scenes

- The HushGram settings code is split into one file per category, so a row is easier to find. Every category lists the same rows in the same order, and search finds the same ones.

The [changelog](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushGram/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) has every earlier release too.

* **Instagram:** HushGram now patches Instagram 452.1.0.53.64 instead of 452.0.0.48.64. Get APKMirror's (arm64-v8a) (480-640dpi) (Android 9.0+) variant, build 385811006. The armeabi-v7a build (385811005) patches too, and so do the x86 and x86_64 builds (385811007 and 385811008), which Instagram is shipping again.
* **Instagram:** HushGram now builds on Morphe patcher 2.0.0, so update Morphe Manager to 2.0.0 or newer before patching. On a computer, use morphe-desktop 1.19.0 or newer. Patching with every patch on takes about 40% less time there. (#60)
* **Instagram - Find the reel you came from:** Trial reels (shown to people who don't follow the creator) aren't on the creator's profile, so the search could only give up. Tapping the creator of one now shows a short note and skips the search. Reported in #225.
* **Instagram - Download any video:** Skip what's already saved reads its history file in small, fixed amounts now. A damaged file can't slow a save down, and it gets written out fresh at the next save, so newer saves aren't lost behind the damage. (#150)
* **Instagram - Turn off double tap to like:** Patching takes about 4% less time with every patch on. The patch reads code only in the places its targets can be, instead of every method in the app. The patched app comes out the same. Refs #173.
* **Instagram - View stories anonymously:** Patching with every patch on takes about 3% less time and 5% less processor work. Its checks for other callers now read only the classes that can hold one. The patched app doesn't change. Refs #173.
* **Instagram:** HushGram launch screen and Emoji style now ask the patcher's index where their code is, instead of reading every method. With every patch on, that's about 3% less processor work. Same patched app as before. Refs #173.
* **Instagram:** Patches that find their code by a piece of text, or by Instagram's internal labels, now look it up directly instead of checking every string. Patching is about 2% quicker. The patched app is the same. Refs #173.
* **Tooling:** `scripts/native-runner.ps1` runs checks inside the installed patched Instagram on an offline emulator, as a throwaway signed-out Android user. Each verdict names the exact APK it ran on. Two controls (build identity, a missing hook) must hold before feature checks count.
* **Tooling:** The native runner's first feature checks cover Hide your active status. They build Instagram's own presence requests without sending them, and only Active may turn Idle, only while the switch is on and HushGram isn't paused.
* **Tooling:** The native runner checks View DM photos and videos anonymously on Instagram's receipt handler. Switched on, the handler finishes a stand-in receipt on the phone without building its request. Voice receipts, a paused HushGram and the switch off stay Instagram's.
* **Tooling:** Nothing goes public until the whole app has been walked with that exact bundle on a release phone or an emulator. `publish-release.ps1` stops before GitHub without a full, crash-free walk of that bundle.
* **Tooling:** `scripts/find-release-for-identity.ps1` reads the `hg1:` build identity from a diagnostics report and names the release it came from, or says the build isn't one of ours, so a repackaged fork shows up before anyone digs in.

HushGram v0.0.8 has 79 patches for Instagram 450.0.0.50.77, 1 more than v0.0.7. All seven builds of that version patch, and it needs Morphe Manager 1.34.0 or newer on Android 9 and newer. Here's everything that changed.

## Instagram

* HushGram 0.0.8 adds 1 patch, for 79 in all, and stays on Instagram 450.0.0.50.77 with Morphe Manager 1.34.0 or newer. All seven builds of that version patch: the arm64 ones (385611395, 385611400, 385611404, 385611431 and 385611438) and the x86 and x86_64 ones (385611439 and 385611440).
* New patch, Hide suggested accounts in DMs. Turn on its switch under Messages and restart Instagram, and the Accounts to follow section at the bottom of your messages isn't built. Your chats and follow requests stay, and so does a section of people who follow you. It's in the default selection with its switch off. Asked for in #112.
* Copy the commenter's username only shows up in HushGram settings when Copy username actually went into your build. On an Instagram build where it couldn't, Copy comment still works, the extra switch stays out of the way, and the diagnostic report says why.

* Disable analytics is stricter about which saved address it treats as the crash reporter's. ## Tooling

* The patch contract check can count a name Instagram asks its shared string pool for, on the rules marked for it. Some 450 builds (385611395, 400, 439 and 440) ask the pool for a few names that 438 loads itself, so the check turned down the story link parser, the setup screen presenter and the share sheet's target list there even with the patch in the right place. Other rules still count only names a method loads itself, so a pool ask elsewhere can't confuse them.
* Release notes now have to open with a short What's new list of 5 to 8 one-line bullets, with the full list of changes under it. The notes builder won't write them without one, or with one that's grown too long to scan. Asked for in #86 and #106.
* Hide ads has tests of its own. One checks that only an on switch with HushGram ready and not paused hides an ad. The other checks that each supported Instagram build has exactly one place where ads go into a feed, and that HushGram's check is the first thing that runs there.
* The Instagram internals reference now includes measured network traffic, background activity and unplugged battery discharge, with exact installed-build evidence and the limits of each measurement. The observation uses an installation reporting HushGram 0.0.5 and does not establish savings against stock or validate the current release.
* The push gate, the release receipt, the dependency audit and the all-patches check wait their turn in the machine's build queue now, when it has one, instead of starting Gradle or the patcher straight away. The gate holds one slot from its first build to its last patch run, and a push made with `HUSHGRAM_ALLOW_RELEASE=1` goes ahead of everyday builds in the line. `BUILD_QUEUE_SCRIPT` names the queue and `HUSHGRAM_BUILD_WRAPPER` the script that runs Gradle. Without them the scripts run as they did before and say so.
* The push gate runs its quick checks first. The catalog, both lints and the runtime tests go in one build, and the patch tests (most of a quarter hour) and the bundle come after it, so a lint slip or a stale catalog stops the push in a few minutes. A declared build with no fixture stops it before anything is built.
* The push gate keeps its results when it removes its worktree, pass or fail. The test results, the bundle and its SBOM, each declared build's patch reports and its passing patch run go in a folder named for the commit, under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HushGram\gate` unless `HUSHGRAM_GATE_CACHE` names another place, with a manifest of what the gate ran and how far it got. The newest three are kept. Before, a gate's test results went with its worktree, and the release check had to run the patch tests again.
* `build-release-receipt.ps1 -FromGate` and `validate-release-facts.ps1 -FromGate` read the gate's run of the commit they check instead of doing its work again. The receipt takes the gate's bundle and SBOM when none was built here, and reads each declared build's patch run back when the gate made it with the same bundle, catalog, desktop CLI and APK. The release check takes the gate's test results, bundle and receipt when the checkout has none, and the index push passes `-FromGate` by itself. A run is read only when its manifest, tree, hashes and test counts still hold up for that commit, and every check runs on what's read. Anything else and the scripts build, test and patch as before.
* The index push that follows a release doesn't build and test the release's sources all over again. When every file it pushes is an index file and the only lines changed since a commit the gate passed are the index, the README's latest release sentence and the bug form's version, the gate is skipped. The release switch, the commit checks, the suites and the release check against the published release still run. The gate runs anyway when the kept run doesn't hold up, or when it would patch a build here that the kept run didn't patch with the same fixture and desktop CLI.
* The gate's kept run is held to more before a push or a release leans on it. An index push is gated in full when the fixture folder has changed since the gate ran, since a build added or replaced there changes what the patch tests read. The same goes when `pre-push.ps1` or `gate-evidence.ps1` changed after the run was made, or when a kept patched APK, patch report or merge no longer matches what the gate stamped. Two gates of one commit no longer write into the same folder. The second one stops until the first is done. Pruning still keeps the newest three runs, and failed runs go before passed ones, so a release's passed run survives a busy day of pushes.
* When the fixture folder holds more than one copy of the Instagram version the bundle declares, the gate patches the declared build, picked by its version code. It used to take whichever file sorted first, so a second full bundle kept beside the declared one sent the patch step to the wrong build.
* `scripts/release/` holds the helpers a release used to need by hand. `preflight.ps1` runs the quick checks in a few minutes before the source push (a clean checkout on main, every declared build in the fixture folder, the desktop CLI, the release facts, the CHANGELOG section and the patch tests that read no Instagram build) and says how long each took. `patch-all-builds.ps1` patches every Instagram build in the fixture folder with the whole catalog and reports the patches each applied and missed and the CLI's warnings, patching a build kept as a bundle from the bundle rather than its base split, and reading the gate's run back with `-FromGate`. `release_notes.py` builds the GitHub notes from a CHANGELOG section with every bullet in it, and `count_tests.py` counts the test results, the gate's included, and prints the index description's validation sentence. The release steps in CONTRIBUTING.md use all four.
* A push that changes a PowerShell script has every tracked script parsed before anything else runs, and a script that doesn't parse stops the push. Most of them run only for a release or with a phone, so a slip such as a variable name run into a colon used to surface there first.

## Tooling

* AGP's host test tools use Netty 4.1.139, which fixes 13 advisories. They stay on the 4.1 line for now, since every AGP up to 9.4.1 and the 9.5 previews builds its emulator control on gRPC 1.69.1, and that needs Netty 4.1. None of this is in the shipped extension payload.
* Moved to Morphe patcher 1.15.1, which fixes a reused patch match handing back stale classes and speeds up signing, DEX output and matching. With it, the patch step for all 48 patches takes 54 seconds on a desktop, down from 147 at v0.0.5. The next release needs Morphe Manager 1.34.0 or newer, the first Manager that carries this patcher. v0.0.5 keeps working in Manager 1.33.0.
* Verification fixtures find the compiler beside the selected Java executable when Java comes from PATH.
* Advisory checks now hold unread or conflicting severity for review, including CVSS 4 beside a low label. Package ratings stay tied to the queried dependency and version, and aliases retain the strongest evidence. Malformed, repeated or whitespace-terminated CVSS 3 metrics are refused. Known HIGH and CRITICAL ratings remain visible beside unread evidence.
* The release check counts every top-level test class a Kotlin test file declares, so a second class in one file no longer reads as left over from a deleted one and the index push goes through.
* The injected-code contracts no longer count a method another rule picks for the same hook as a stray call, so the two touch methods Stop swiping between tabs hooks each pass on their own. A rule can also say how many times its method calls the hook, which Hide the home feed needs since it filters both reads of Home's saved feed.
* The patched APK check now holds Hide the comment bar on reposted reels' guards where they belong: first thing in the comment bar's show, and once in the step that sets the bar up.

## Install or update

* Update Morphe Manager to 1.34.0 or newer first. Older versions ask for an update before they load this bundle.
* Add the source with the link in the README, or update it if you already have it.
* Patch the arm64-v8a build of Instagram 450.0.0.50.77, version code 385611438. APKMirror lists another build under the same label, so check the number. The .mpp is a patch bundle, not an Instagram APK.
* Keep the manager's signing key for updates, so a new build installs over the old one and you stay signed in.
* Read Before you sign in in the README first. A spare account keeps your main one out of it.

## Validation

2607 runtime tests and all 1053 patch tests passed locally. All 75 patches applied to Instagram 450.0.0.50.77 without forcing, and the resource and injected-code checks passed. The receipt and SHA256SUMS.txt beside the bundle list every file's hash.

HushGram v0.0.5 has 48 patches for Instagram 449.0.0.52.84 (arm64-v8a, version code 385511871), two more than v0.0.4. The new ones are Hide the notes row and View DM photos and videos anonymously, and both start off until you turn them on. This release needs Morphe Manager 1.33.0 or newer. It still runs on Android 9 and newer. Here's everything that changed.

* Bind current dependency audits to source, catalog, toolchain, SBOM and bundle bytes, preserve resolved dependency edges, and update affected settings and UTP tools to compatible Commons Lang and HttpClient fixes.

## Tooling

* The translation scripts stop straight away on Python older than 3.12 with one line naming the version they need. On Python 3.11 under Windows, every import used to fail with "destination changed after validation", which pointed at the wrong problem. The same cause on a newer Python with an older Windows build now gets its own plain message too.
* The injected-register verifier no longer clears a shared phone's log buffer. It writes its own marker line, reads only what follows it, and stops with a plain message if the buffer has already rotated past the marker.
* Device identity checks read ADB's standard output separately from diagnostic messages. A successful daemon startup no longer rejects the selected phone or emulator, while command failures keep their full diagnostics and invalid identities still refuse installation.
* Troubleshooting now checks the Instagram build and other enabled patch sources before blaming a changed app. Report #11 succeeded after its other source was removed. Signing-conflict guidance explains which updates preserve data and that removing a differently signed app deletes its local data.
* Device installs and verifier runs require an exclusive lease and verified device identity. Updates keep installed data and permissions, replacement uninstalls refuse, and verification selects the device's actual instruction set. Windows emulator identity replies accept their native line endings.
* Protect translation replacement with an enforced Windows file transaction. Stale edits and conflicting writers refuse the import, existing readers retain complete old bytes, and unsupported storage refuses writes. Unchanged imports still preserve exact bytes.
* Exercise every native override writer and reload prohibition with its own failing DEX fixture. Calls inside Instagram's native package remain allowed, and all existing shortcut checks stay in place.
* Refresh the settings, diagnostics and About captures from the published v0.0.3 bundle. Document their actual patch selection and verified build tools, and label source-only controls as unreleased.
* Accept reordered numbered arguments within mixed translation formats while keeping bare arguments in their original order. Changed types, indices and argument counts still stop the import.
* Export the English catalog and translations as Crowdin-compatible JSON, then validate complete or explicit partial local imports before replacing a table. Unchanged round trips keep their exact bytes. Format, escape, plural and input limits are all checked. Imports coordinate through owned locks. Hosted translation approval remains separate.
* Android 9 and Android 17 regression cases exercise settings opening, large text, right-to-left layout, system bars, recovery, diagnostic export, storage and save cancellation with Instagram 449's target SDK 36. The local push check refuses missing or skipped boundary cases, including search focus, filtered Cancel, carousel cancellation across pages and phases, and cleanup of Android 9's hidden unfinished files without deleting finished media.

## New patches

* `Hide suggested posts`. Posts and reels from accounts you don't follow come out of your home feed, along with the rows of suggested accounts and what Instagram mixes in from Threads. Each has its own switch in a new Feed section. If nobody you follow has posted lately, Home shows Instagram's own welcome card instead of a placeholder that never loads.

* `Hide suggested stories`. Stories from accounts you don't follow leave the row at the top of Home. A second switch, off to start, takes the whole row away.
* `Hide Meta AI`. The search bars in the Search tab and in your messages go back to a plain search, and a search's results lose the "Ask a follow-up" bar. Home's top bar loses Meta AI's buttons, and Meta AI's videos and chats come out of your feed too.
* `Hide the Explore grid`, off until you pick it. The Search tab keeps its search bar and the grid of posts and reels under it is gone. Searching still works.
* `Keep the reel speed`. Lock a reel at 2x with Instagram's own lock and the next reels play at 2x as well. Slide the lock off, or restart Instagram, to go back to normal speed. Ads always start at normal speed.
* `Show if a profile follows you`. Someone's profile says Follows you or Doesn't follow you beside their name. piko had it first.
* `Remove the empty space at the bottom`, off until you pick it. When your phone hides its navigation bar completely, or Instagram runs in a pop-up window, the tab bar sits on the bottom edge instead of over an empty strip. MyInsta and piko had this fix first.
* `Hide the Repost button`, off until you pick it. The Repost button and its count are gone from posts and reels. Share still sends a post to someone.
* `Story ring size`, off until you pick it. The rings in the stories row can be drawn anywhere from 70% to 130% of Instagram's size.

* `Open developer options`, off until you pick it. A long press on the Home tab opens Instagram's own developer options, where its server flags can be looked at and overridden. piko had the idea first.

## Under the hood

* The build moved to Gradle 9.8.0 and Guava 33.7.2, which fixes GHSA-xxph-c9ww-hj94. Guava only runs while the patches are built, and the bundle doesn't ship it.

* Eighteen more hooks are pinned in the patched-build check, and a hook that takes a boolean fails the build.
* The release receipt reads each patch's target coverage out of the patched APK, so a required target that's missing stops the release even when its patch applied.

## What's in it

* New patch, `Hide ads`. Sponsored posts, reels and stories don't go in, and Instagram is told the ad didn't go in, so it doesn't leave a gap.
* New patch, `Sanitize sharing links`. Copy link, the Android share sheet and the app buttons in Instagram's own share sheet (WhatsApp, SMS and the rest, which skip Android's) lose `stkn` (the per-share id Instagram 449 adds to every shared link), `igsh`, `igshid`, `utm_source` and Instagram's other tracking keys, and so do the post and story links Instagram's server hands out for sharing. Keys come off Instagram's own links only. A link in someone's bio opens its page directly instead of going through `l.instagram.com`, Instagram's click tracker.
* New patch, `Disable analytics`. Instagram's usage events go to your phone's loopback address, which refuses them, instead of to Instagram's and Facebook's logging servers.
* New patch, `Remove build expired popup`. A patched Instagram doesn't update itself, and without this Instagram locks it out after a few weeks with a screen that says the version is too old.
* `Restore trust on re-signed builds`, from Hushfacebook. Instagram's own signature checks see Instagram's two original certificates on a build you signed yourself.
* `HushGram settings`, from Hushfacebook: a switch for each feature, Pause, automatic safe mode after three quick crashes in a row, Debug logging and a diagnostic report that leaves out links, IDs, cookies and sign-in tokens. It opens from a shortcut on Instagram's launcher icon or from a row at the top of Instagram's own Settings and activity screen, and the shortcut works before you sign in too: when Instagram's sign-in screen comes up over it, the settings move in front.
* Runs on Android 9 and newer, which is Instagram 449's own floor. The settings screen, the launcher shortcut, safe mode and the report export all have Android 9 and 10 paths, since Hushfacebook's code expected Android 11.
* German, Spanish, Indonesian, Brazilian Portuguese and Turkish translations for everything HushGram shows.
* Checked beside a patched Threads signed with the same key: neither declares anything the other does, and both open and run side by side.
* New patch, `Clean up Reels`. The Follow button beside a reel's author goes, and so do the pills that push Edits, templates, Meta AI and Ray-Ban Meta glasses, and friends' activity with the comment preview. Each of the three has its own switch under Reels, and they're all on once the patch is in.
* New patch, `Don't send reel watch history`. Instagram isn't told which reels you watched or how far into them you got. It only uses that to rank your Reels, so reels you've already seen may come back.
* New patch, `Hide Reels in the feed`. The rows of suggested reels between posts in your home feed are gone, along with the other units that open the Reels viewer from there. A reel from someone you follow still shows as a post.
* New patch, `Download any reel`. Every reel's more menu has Download, including the shorter menu some accounts get, and a tap saves the reel at your download quality (the best there is by default) without Instagram's watermark. Its switch is under Reels.
* New patch, `Download any story`. The menu on anyone's story has Download. A video story saves at your download quality and a photo story at its largest size, into the same folders as reels. Its switch is under Stories.
* New patch, `Download any video`, off until you pick it. Someone else's post in your feed that is a video gets Download in its menu, first in the short menu most posts open now, including the one under an "About this reel" summary. A tap saves it at your download quality without Instagram's watermark. On your own video, Instagram's own Download row, where it shows one, saves the same way. Its switch is under Downloads.
* New patch, `Tap to play`, off until you pick it. Videos, reels and stories wait for your tap instead of starting on their own, and feed videos show a play button that goes away once your tap starts the video and comes back when it stops. A story or video that takes a few seconds to load after your tap still starts. In Reels, a tap on a reel that's waiting starts it and a tap on a playing one pauses it. A story that's waiting starts when you press, hold and let go, the way a paused one does. A video you started keeps playing when you drag its scrubber. Its switch is in a new Playback section.
* New patch, `Resume long videos`. A video or reel over two minutes that you left partway picks up there the next time it plays, once. Drag the scrubber to start somewhere else. Live videos, ads and anything you watched to the end start as usual. Its switch under Playback starts off, and the spots it keeps are dropped after 30 days.
* New patch, `Default playback quality`, off until you pick it, for anyone who wants to save data or always get the sharpest picture. Pick Data saver, Up to 480p, Up to 720p or Highest under Playback in HushGram's settings, and videos, reels and video stories start at that quality where Instagram offers it. A video with nothing at or under your pick plays the closest quality above. Instagram has no quality menu of its own, so this is the only way to choose one. Once it's in, the list starts at Auto, Instagram's own choice, so nothing changes until you pick a quality. Checked on a phone: a reel started at 240p with Data saver and at 1080p with Highest, and a video story took the pick too.
* New patch, `View stories anonymously`, off until you pick it. Instagram isn't told which stories you watch, so you stay off their viewer lists. Replying or reacting still shows you, and a story you've watched can show as new again. Its switch is in the Stories section.
* New patch, `Remove the advertising ID`. Instagram can't read your phone's advertising ID or tell Android's ad services which ads you saw or tapped, because the permissions for them are taken out of the build. It shows under Set when you patched.
* New patch, `Turn off double tap to like`, off until you pick it. A double tap on a reel or on any post in the feed, whether it's a photo, a carousel or a video, doesn't like it, and the heart doesn't show. A single tap, double tap to skip and the Like button work as before. Its switch is under Reels.
* New patch, `Open links in external browser`, on by default. A web link you tap opens in your default browser instead of Instagram's in-app browser, and a bio or caption link skips Instagram's click tracker on the way. Pages on Instagram, Facebook, Messenger, Threads and Meta stay in the app, and so do ads. Its switch is under Ads and privacy.
* New patch, `Hide the Reels tab`, off until you pick it. Reels leaves the tab bar, and a start or a notification meant for it opens Home, including on accounts Instagram opens on Reels. Reels in your feed and shared reels still play. Its switch is under Reels and takes effect after Instagram restarts.
* New Downloads section in HushGram's settings. It lists the saves that are running, each with a Cancel button, and holds the download quality, the save folder, the video file name and a switch that saves videos other apps can open.
* New patch, `Stop Story auto-advance`. A story stays on screen until you tap or swipe, however long it runs. Turn its switch off for Instagram's timing.
* `Disable analytics` also covers the analytics address Instagram's server can hand its push connection. Before, only the address built into the app went to the loopback address, and a different one from the server went through as is.
* With Debug logging on, the diagnostic report says what `Disable analytics` did with each analytics address Instagram used, and which of Instagram's processes asked for it. Checked on a phone: with the switch on, nothing reached Instagram's logging server at all.
* HushGram's settings screen opens with a Before you sign in note under the status line: how to sign in with the least risk to your account. The settings open before you sign in too, so it's there when it matters. A tap hides it for good, and pausing HushGram doesn't bring it back. Checked on a phone in English and German.
* Morphe Manager and bundle sites like morphe-patches.software show HushGram's own icon next to the source instead of the owner's GitHub picture. The icon is `patches-bundle.png` in the repository's root.
* README now leads with a Before you sign in section that spells out how to keep your account: the sign-in is the moment Instagram checks the app with Play Integrity and your phone's hardware, so use a seasoned account, prefer a Root Mount install if you're rooted, and don't clear the app's data afterward. The account section says plainly that a re-signed build can't pass those checks.

## Under the hood

* Every patched build is checked before it ships. Its resource table has to match the original's, each hook may only use registers that were free where it went in, and each call a patch adds has to be where the patch put it, once.
* Added a HushGram logo and README banner in the family's style, using the pink from HushGram's settings.
* The release checks keep working after the first release. A checkout with a published index no longer stops the release tooling's own tests, an ordinary push leaves an old local bundle unread instead of refusing it after the patcher pin moves (a pushed commit that still carries the older check gets that check's own switch), and the tests now run the exact checks the pre-push hook runs for the index push, network lookups and quoted test counts included. CONTRIBUTING's release steps say what that push needs: a full test run with the fixtures, and a bundle description and GitHub description that name the release.
* The pre-push hook and the release scripts read git's output as UTF-8 every time. The machine-name scan and the hook's own git calls used the console's code page, which is 437 when a push starts in Git Bash, so a path with a letter past ASCII came back garbled. And with no console at all, Windows PowerShell 5.1 stopped with "The handle is invalid." before git ran. The fix comes from Hushfacebook.
* Release tooling, from Hushfacebook. Before a release, `scripts/build-release-receipt.ps1` patches every Instagram build the catalog declares and writes a receipt saying what applied, which toolchain built the bundle and what the patches changed in the manifest. It asks OSV about every library the bundle carries, and it writes `SHA256SUMS.txt` for the files a release publishes. When the index goes out, the pre-push hook downloads those files and checks them against both. `scripts/validate-release-facts.ps1` keeps the README, the CHANGELOG and the bug form in line with the patch list, and it works before the first release too.

Every file here is listed in `SHA256SUMS.txt`, and `release-receipt-0.0.2.json` says what applied to Instagram 449.0.0.52.84 and which toolchain built the bundle.

## 1.0.0 (2026-10-03)

### Features

- **Block stream ads:** replace detected live-stream ads with direct Twitch playback from alternate player contexts, preferring matching quality without an external stream proxy.
- **Hide feed and display ads:** remove sponsored feed cards and display advertisements.
- **Hide Turbo promotions:** remove Turbo entries, upsells and purchase buttons while retaining train overlays.
- **Hide subscription discount banners:** remove subscription offers and promotional labels while retaining normal subscription actions.
- **Auto-claim bonus channel points:** claim available bonus rewards during live playback.
- **BTTV and 7TV emotes:** render global and channel emotes in chat and show provider previews on tap.
- **Reload stream:** add a double-tap reload control to native, Classic Split, Vertical View and swipe-feed players, with a single-tap hint.
- **Block client-requested ads:** optionally suppress native ad requests.
- **Playback diagnostics:** provide playlist and playback diagnostics, disabled by default.
- **Inspect Twitch APK:** report package, version and DEX information without modifying the APK.

### Integration

- Add a native-style Patch settings page containing only the selected features, with saved preferences across same-key updates.
- Preserve Twitch's native and React Native player and chat paths, including V2 emote previews and Reload on initial Classic Split entry.
- Include reproducible build, test and APK evaluation tools, synthetic hook tests and original-aware DEX verification.

### Compatibility

- Evaluated target: Twitch **31.3.0 (3103006)**, ARM64, Android 13.
- Extended ad coverage remains under evaluation. An unmatched-media midroll case remains under investigation; story ads are not covered.
- Google Play billing is unavailable in the re-signed app. Other versions and ABIs require separate verification.

The new patch is GmsCore support, for phones that run microG-RE instead of Google Play services. It sends Pinterest's Google sign-in and push notifications through microG-RE. It isn't picked by default, so if you don't use microG-RE nothing changes for you.

Patch 14.41.0 with the same signing key you used before and install it over your current HushPinterest. Your settings stay as they are.

## What's new

- New GmsCore support patch, for phones that run microG-RE instead of Google Play services. Pinterest's Google sign-in and push notifications go through microG-RE, so Continue with Google opens microG-RE's sign-in. Before, it asked Play services and the account got turned down. It's left out of the default selection since without microG-RE those requests have nowhere to go. Pick it in Expert mode and Spoof signature for Google sign-in comes along with it. (#15)
- The patches are now built on Morphe patcher 2.0.0, so you'll need Morphe Manager 2.0.0 or newer to apply them. Older Manager builds can't load the bundle.

## Behind the scenes

- A release can't go public until the whole app has been walked with that exact bundle on a release phone or an emulator. The publish stage now takes the walk's receipt as `-Walk` and stops before GitHub or the index if the walk wasn't a full pass, saw a Pinterest crash, ran on some other device, or patched with a different bundle.
- A device lease another session happens to be reading no longer stops a run partway. The check waits a moment and tries again, and a lease that stays locked still stops it.
- New `scripts/walk-app.ps1` patches Pinterest from the release bundle and installs it on a leased phone or emulator. Then it opens the home feed, the patched screens and every Hush settings page, and writes the receipt publish asks for. Only a full walk with no Pinterest crash earns a PASS.

## Install

1. Install [Morphe Manager](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-manager) 2.0.0 or newer.
2. Add HushPinterest as a patch source: https://morphe.software/add-source?github=SysAdminDoc%2FHushPinterest
3. Download Pinterest 14.41.0, version code `14418010`. APKMirror has it as an arm64-v8a bundle (`.apkm`) for Android 12L or newer. Pick that file in Manager and it merges the parts before patching.
4. Uninstall the stock Pinterest first, since Android won't put one over the other. Save anything you keep only on the phone before you do. Your boards and pins come back when you sign in.
5. Sign in with your email and a Pinterest password. If you joined through Google or Facebook, tap `Forgot your password?` on Pinterest's login page to set one first. On a phone with microG-RE, pick GmsCore support when you patch and Continue with Google goes to microG-RE's sign-in instead.
6. Right after your first patch, export Morphe Manager's signing key (Settings, then System, then Import & export, then Signing key) and keep it somewhere private. Updates only install over a Pinterest signed with that same key.

Already on HushPinterest? Update Manager, then skip steps 4 and 5. Patch 14.41.0 with the same key and install it over the one you have.

HushPinterest 0.0.12 has 32 patches for Pinterest 14.41.0. It's built on Morphe patcher 1.15.1, so it needs Morphe Manager 1.34.0 or newer. This one moves to Pinterest's newest version and adds a lot of new switches, every one of them off until you turn it on. Filter feed can hide video pins and pins with words you mute. Keep Home feed stops Home from reloading on its own when you come back to it, and Show posted date puts the day a pin went up under its title. Download pins can copy or share the picture itself now, and its rows show in the full-screen pin menu too. Downloads also stopped settling for the smaller copy now and then.

It's a new Pinterest version. So far APKMirror only has 14.41.0 as an arm64 bundle (`.apkm`) for Android 12L or newer, and Manager merges it before patching. Patch it with the same signing key you used before and install it over your current HushPinterest, and your settings stay as they are. On a phone older than Android 12L, keep 0.0.11 and Pinterest 14.40.0 for now.

## What's new

- The patches now target Pinterest 14.41.0, the newest stable release. 14.40.0 is no longer supported. So far APKMirror has 14.41.0 only as an arm64 bundle (`.apkm`) for Android 12L or newer, and Manager merges it before patching.
- Download pin now shows in the full-screen pin menu some accounts get from the three dots on a pin, along with the other Hush rows, and Pinterest's own Download row in that menu gives way to it. Before, only the smaller pop-up menu had them.
- Download pins has a new switch, Copy image, that starts off. It adds a Copy image row under Download pin, in the small pin menu and in the full-screen one, and puts the full-size picture on the clipboard so you can paste it into a chat or a notes app. Video pins don't get the row. If the picture is too big, isn't really an image, or takes too long, you're told so and your clipboard stays as it was. (#11)
- Download pins also has Share image, another switch that starts off. Its row sits under Copy image and opens Android's share menu with the full-size picture itself rather than a link, so the app you pick gets the image. Video pins don't get it, and if the picture can't be fetched you get a short note instead of the share menu. (#11)
- Long-press download has three new switches on the Pin actions page: Hide Save, Hide Send and Hide Search image in the long-press menu. Each takes that one Pinterest button out of the round menu you get by holding a pin in a grid, and the pin itself still saves, shares and searches as before. They work with Download off too. If everything would be hidden and Download is off, the menu stays Pinterest's own rather than opening empty. All three start off. (#11)
- Black comments now covers the strip under the status bar too. On 14.41.0 the comments fill the whole screen, and that strip stayed dark gray above the black list on photo and video pins alike.
- Downloads no longer save the smaller copy now and then when the original is there. Finding the original asks Pinterest's media server a few quick questions, and one asked just as both lookup helpers were wrapping up the last was turned away, so the download settled for the size the feed showed. It now waits a moment for a helper to come free.
- Copy media link no longer overwrites something you copied after it. When a pin shows only a smaller size, the link to that size goes on the clipboard right away, and it becomes the original's link once Pinterest's media server answers, but only if the clipboard still holds that copy. Before, nothing was copied until the answer came, and a slow answer could replace whatever you'd copied in the meantime.
- Save list no longer hangs when the app holding the picked file stops answering. Each save gets 30 seconds in all, then you're told to check the file, and a late answer from that app doesn't add another message or remove anything. While that app is still busy, a new list says to try later instead of opening a picker. Everything that talks to the file's app now runs on its own helper, never on the screen's thread, including the clean-up after a list that couldn't be written while HushPinterest was paused.
- A list that isn't written no longer deletes an empty file you picked to write over. Only an empty file made since the picker opened gets removed. Any other file is left where it is, and you're told so.
- Save list leaves out a source link that hides a session code behind an encoded `;` (`%3B`, that encoded again, or a longer spelling some servers still read as `;`), the way it already left out a plain `;jsessionid=`. The pin's ID, title and Pinterest link still go in. Ordinary encoded spaces and accented letters stay exactly as given.
- Queue selected and Queue pins stay off until something chosen can actually be saved. A pin with no picture address, or a video Pinterest only streams, doesn't turn them on anymore, though Save list still takes those pins. A mix still queues what it can and counts the rest as unsupported.
- Morphe Manager lists every change of the release your Pinterest was patched with, not just a short summary. For that one release Manager shows the patch bundle's description instead of this changelog, and the description was one paragraph while every older release listed its changes. It now goes on with the release's changes after the summary, starting with this one.
- Hide comments has a second switch, Hide suggested replies, for the row of ready-made replies like "Yum!" and "Came out great!" next to the comment box. You can still write your own comment. It starts off, and the two switches don't turn each other on. (#14)
- Hide AI-labeled pins has a second switch, Hide pins that say they're AI, for AI pins Pinterest doesn't label. It takes a pin whose title or description says something like "AI art", "AI generated", #aiart, "made with AI", Midjourney, Stable Diffusion or PixAI, and pins from sites that only host AI images, like pixai.art and Civitai. It goes by the pin's own words, so a pin that just says "AI" stays, and names like Ai Weiwei or the Portuguese "aí" are left alone. Boards named that way stay too. It starts off, and diagnostics count these pins apart from the labeled ones.
- Hide closeup buttons has a third switch, Hide Search image label on pins. Pinterest puts a "Search image" label on the lens button for your first two pins each day, and with this on the lens shows without it, the way it looks from the third pin on. Tapping the lens still searches. It starts off and sits under Hide lens button on the Interface page. (#13)
- New Filter feed patch, with a Hide video pins switch on the Feed page. It takes pins that play a video out of your home feed, search, related pins and boards, idea pins with video included. Photos and GIFs stay. It starts off.
- Filter feed also has Muted words, a row on the Feed page where you type words and phrases you don't want to see. A pin whose title or description has one of them leaves the same lists. Capitals don't matter and only whole words count, so "cake" takes out "Wedding Cake Ideas" but not cupcakes. The list holds 50 entries of up to 40 characters, starts empty, and goes into settings files with your switches. Boards named after a muted word stay.
- New Keep Home feed patch, with its switch on the Feed page. Pinterest reloads Home with new pins on its own when you come back after five minutes or more, when you pick the Home tab again after a while and when you back out of a search, and the pin you were about to open is gone. With this on, Home stays where you left it. Pull down whenever you want new pins. The new pins prompt, a second tap on the Home tab and a pin you open from a notification still load as before. It starts off.
- New Show posted date patch, with its switch on the Interface page. Pinterest sends the day each pin was posted but never shows it, and with this on you see "Posted" and that day under the title when you open a pin. A pin without a date just doesn't get the line. The date follows the language HushPinterest shows and your phone's time zone. It starts off and shows from the next pin you open. (#11)
- With Debug logging on, the line for a kept pin also says whether Pinterest marked it as a repin or as saved to one of your boards. It shows only that the field is set, never which board.
- The Feed page has a new row under the AI switches, Pinterest's own AI setting. It opens the page where Pinterest lets you see fewer AI pins among the ones it picks for you, since neither that page nor the switches catch every AI pin alone. It's there whenever Hide AI-labeled pins is patched in.

## Behind the scenes

- The pin model fixture test also checks the fields Hide video pins reads, the two inside Pinterest's video and idea pin models included, and the grid title that the AI words and video filters use to tell a pin from other models.
- The pre-push and release checks take a declared build kept as APKMirror's `.apkm` bundle, since that's the only way 14.41.0 ships. The bug report form's example names a bundle too, and the release step keeps whatever kind of file the form names.
- The release gate's advisory check works in Windows PowerShell 5.1 again. Since 0.0.11, any failed OSV request stopped it there with an "Unable to find type" error. A dropped connection or a busy server now gets asked again in 5.1, the way it already did in PowerShell 7.
- The README's Help now goes through why Android might refuse the install. It says where Manager keeps its signing key, so an update that won't go over your patched copy can be fixed without losing your settings. It also covers stock Pinterest and the unknown apps prompt.
- The README sends people on v0.0.11 to Pinterest 14.40.0 again, the build that release patches, and names 14.41.0 as the next release's build. It had pointed them at 14.41.0, which v0.0.11 refuses. The release's prepare step now stops while the README still names a next release, so it gets rewritten for the new build before a release is cut.
- The patch verifier checks how the long-press hide switches tell Pinterest's buttons apart. The sorter has to read the held button's own id and send Save, Send and both search ids to the right answer, with the ids found the way the patch finds them, and a build without them has to keep the plain answer.
- The bug report form lists Filter feed among the patches you can tick. It was the one patch the form left out, and the release check stopped on that.
- The release check and the publish step leave a GitHub description alone when it names no version, patch count or Pinterest build, since there's nothing in it to go stale. One that names any of them still has to match the release. This release would have stopped on the shorter description the repository uses now.
- The source census reads Jman's bundle registry again. On October 14 the registry took down the files the audit read and now serves the same list from its own site, so every audit since stopped on a missing file. It reads all of the site's pages, not only the first hundred releases.
- The device scripts write their lease times in UTC with a `Z` at the end. They used `+00:00`, and the other tools sharing the test phone took a lease written that way as already expired. They also read a `Z` time as UTC now. Before, a busy phone's expiry was read as local clock time, so an expired lease looked hours from ending.
- The script tests now clean up after themselves. The pre-push cases remove the worktree the hook builds in, and a passing host reference run deletes its report folder. Each run used to leave both in the temp directory.

Save list works on a board even when every loaded pin is already in Download history, and when a list can't be written, the empty file the picker made is removed again. A file you picked to write over is never removed.

Turkish now talks to you the same informal way everywhere, puts the right ending on HushPinterest, and shows an import change as old → new where it used to say "instead of". ## Behind the scenes

- The script tests stopped failing now and then under Windows PowerShell when two device builds run at once. Both builds logged to the same stand-in build queue file, which Windows PowerShell can't append to from two processes at the same moment. That test now also reports the exact line where a build failed.
- Picking a release back up after something went wrong got easier. The build stage takes the signed files back from GitHub when the release is already up there and the local copies are gone, instead of stopping. The gate stage notices a gate that passed right before the network dropped. A failed publication puts the old GitHub description back, and a repair note under a fresh Unreleased heading no longer reads as an edit to released notes. Pushes also keep going in Windows PowerShell when a release's output goes to a log file.
- The build moved to Kotlin 2.4.21, Commons Lang 3.21.0 and androidx.annotation 1.11.0, with their hashes added to the dependency verification file. The advisory check finds nothing in the 286 libraries the build resolves.
- A feed filter test covers a module that also carries search filter chips, which Pinterest 14.39.0 keeps in a list next to the module's pins. The ads reference explains why only the pin list can leave a module empty.
- The source census reads Jman's index at its new name and layout, and the Morphe Patch Tracker's list again now that two of its keys differ only in case. Its contract suite passes under Windows PowerShell 5.1 too.
- A fixture test checks that every pin field Hide ads, Hide AI-labeled pins and Hide shopping read is still in Pinterest's build with a type the filters can use. A renamed or retyped field now fails the tests instead of quietly switching a filter off.
- The fixture tests read Pinterest's manifests and resource tables with the same ARSCLib build the patcher uses, instead of a second copy whose classes could win or lose depending on classpath order. A check stops the tests if a patcher update moves it.
- An interrupted release can resume after a commit repairs its publication checks. It keeps the prepared source, published tag, signed assets and index unchanged, including the original test counts when local results are missing or come from a focused run. It pushes only when needed and checks the index Morphe Manager receives. Changed release files or unrelated source commits stop recovery. Refs #3
- The script contract tests keep the published bug report form as it is when they build a tree whose index lags the source, the way the release check expects, and now also check that a form moved to the catalog's newer Pinterest build is refused there. They used to move the form's build along with the catalog, which went unnoticed until the published form named the catalog's newest build and held up the 0.0.7 index push.
- The published index check finds git when the pre-push hook's PATH lists more than one copy of it. Inside the hook it used to get all three paths as one name and stop the release gate.
- The published index check also runs on a release's prepare commit. Its copy of the index, README's latest release sentence and the bug form now move to the version being prepared, the way publishing moves them, instead of failing on the old one.

## What's new

- Pinterest 14.39.0 is now the supported version. All 27 patches apply to it, and 14.38.0 is no longer a target.
- New Fix push notifications patch, on by default. Google's Firebase service only signs Pinterest up for push notifications when the request names Pinterest's original signature, and a patched Pinterest is signed with a different one, so it never got a notification token. The patch gives Firebase the original signature's fingerprint when Pinterest signs up and changes nothing else in the request. Its switch is on the new Notifications page under More settings.
- Download pins has a new Save in Pinterest's folder switch, and it starts off. With it on, downloads go to Pictures/100PINT/Pins, the folder Pinterest's own image saves use, instead of filling up Download. Board downloads, long-press downloads and retries from Download history follow it too, and the download messages and Download history point to that folder instead of Downloads. (#5)
- Download pins can also save into a folder you pick. Tap Pick a download folder and choose any folder inside Pictures, DCIM, Download or Documents in Android's folder picker. Android's Downloads still does the saving, so nothing gets copied and no storage permission is needed. Each download in Download history remembers its folder, so its messages point there even after you pick another. Tap the row again to pick a different folder or go back to Download. Save in Pinterest's folder wins while it's on, and picking a folder turns it off. (#5)
- Long-press download keeps Pinterest's own buttons again. Holding a pin in a grid showed only Download, because Pinterest's Pin, Share and More ideas buttons never sprang back in after the patch laid the menu out again. Now all three show with Download after them, and letting go on any of them does what it says.
- System share sheet opens Android's share menu from a pin's Share button on 14.39.0. The pin's id is now read from the fields Pinterest's share sheet fills, found when you patch, instead of by a name that pointed somewhere else in 14.39.0, which left Pinterest's own sheet showing with the switch on.
- Hide advertising ID now keeps Pinterest's browser ID out of Google's Block Store too. Pinterest kept it there so that, on a phone with Google backup on, it would outlast an uninstall and come back on a new phone, which let a fresh install send the old ID before you'd signed in. With the switch on, Pinterest finds no saved ID, and when it tries to save one it deletes the stored copy instead, so a reinstall starts fresh. The browser cookie for the install you're using keeps working the way it did.
- The settings home ends with a Support HushPinterest row. Tapping it opens the Ko-fi page in your browser, and if no app can open it you get a message with the address instead. Its text is translated into German, Spanish, Indonesian, Brazilian Portuguese and Turkish.
- Download board no longer saves a board's pins a second time once they've dropped off Download history. The history still shows the newest 32 entries, and it now remembers the 500 before those. Removing a pin from Download history forgets its older downloads too.
- Morphe Manager and the patch index now show the HushPinterest icon next to the source instead of the owner's GitHub picture.
- Hide ads now looks inside modules. A row of ideas on Home or a group of pins under the pin you opened carries its own pins, and an ad in one got through because Hide ads only checked the row itself. Now the ad comes out of the row, and a row left with nothing in it goes too, heading and all. Hide AI-labeled pins and Hide shopping reach inside rows the same way. A pin that carries Pinterest's promotion or campaign ID also counts as an ad now. (#6)
- Hide shopping and product pins now hides a shop's product pins, the ones shown with a store name like Target or Nordstrom Rack and a tag icon under the picture. Pinterest doesn't mark them as paid, so Hide ads keeps leaving them alone, but they slipped past Hide shopping too. With Debug logging on, the diagnostic report also lists the shopping and ad fields of what stays, so a pin that still gets through can be tracked down. (#6)
- Hide ads now catches shopping spotlight stories on the feed models that keep the story kind as Pinterest's own type rather than as text. Before, only the text form counted, so a spotlight on those models stayed unless Hide shopping was on too. Other stories stay put, and Hide shopping still works on its own.
- If a Pinterest update leaves Hide ads only part of its hooks, the Feed page now names the feed lists and ad panels it couldn't reach instead of reading as if everything's covered. The diagnostic report lists every list and panel with how much of it went in, and names the two places no hook reaches yet (Shopping ideas groups in search results and shopping wrappers under related pins). A full build reads the same as before.
- Strip link tracking has a new Plain pin links switch on the Privacy page, and it starts off. With it on, a pin.it link you copy or share becomes the pin's own pinterest.com link, so it doesn't tell Pinterest who shared it. Links Pinterest makes for Copy link or a share change right away, even when you send a pin straight to another app, because HushPinterest sees which pin Pinterest made the link for. Any other short link you copy is checked with Pinterest in the background and swapped on the clipboard a moment later, as long as you haven't copied something else by then. Shared text never waits for that check, and if it fails or takes longer than 4 seconds the short link stays. A pin link from one of Pinterest's country sites, like de.pinterest.com or www.pinterest.co.uk, becomes the same www.pinterest.com link with no lookup, and a pin's sent link drops the invite code that ties it to whoever sent it. Board links and account pages stay as they are, and so does a pin link that still carries a parameter after tracking tags come off.
- HushPinterest settings has a new page under More settings, Pinterest's own settings. It shows where Pinterest keeps its own theme, privacy, notification, AI content and cellular autoplay settings, and names each step through Pinterest's menus in the language Pinterest is using. HushPinterest doesn't change any of them. The AI content row explains how it differs from Hide AI-labeled pins, and the autoplay row says Pinterest may still load part of a video ahead of time.
- HushPinterest drops its Android 9 code now that Pinterest 14.39.0 needs Android 10. The file picker saves go, along with their Pending saves page, and so does the app folder Android 9 used for diagnostic reports. Every download is handed to Android's Downloads, and a selection's summary no longer has a Saved line, since only the picker ever filled it.
- HushPinterest's short messages now show as Pinterest's own toasts. When a dialog is open, a message is long or has more than one line, or the Pinterest build's toast code isn't what the patch expects, they stay Android toasts.

## Behind the scenes

- The release receipt, the patch verifier and the device lease now hold the patched app to Android 10 (API 29), the same floor the settings patch sets since the Android 9 code went. They still expected API 28, so a target whose own floor was below 29 would have failed the receipt.
- While a release hold keeps the published index behind source, the release check now wants the bug report form to name the published release with the Pinterest build it was made for. It used to pair the published version with source's newer build, a combination nobody filing a report would have.
- The privacy doc now follows Pinterest's launch event, which carries the full URL the app was opened with, to both of its uploads: `v3/callback/event/` and `v3/callback/track_funnel/{event}/`. Disable analytics already stops both.
- The privacy doc now lists every header Pinterest puts on its API requests, with where each value comes from and whether a patch covers it. The advertising ID header is the only one a patch changes today.
- The header table now explains the last two. `X-Pinterest-AppState` only says whether the app is in front and online. `X-Pinterest-Platform-BID` is Pinterest's `_b` browser cookie, which the app keeps in Google Block Store (backed up to the cloud when Block Store offers end-to-end encryption), so it can survive a reinstall or a move to a new phone.
- The privacy doc now follows the install ID to all of its uses. Besides its own header it's Pinterest's signed-out ID, AppsFlyer's `unauth_id`, and the ID on analytics, push and reCAPTCHA events. A signed-in emulator kept its session, feed and search after the ID was swapped for a fresh one, so no hook is planned for it.
- System share sheet now checks, when you patch, that Pinterest gives a pin the share kind the patch makes pin links for. A build that numbers its kinds differently is refused instead of sharing a board's id as a pin link. The fixture tests cover that refusal and the two ways the sendable's constructor can stop naming its id and kind.
- Long-press download now checks that a menu button's detach handler really cancels the spring driver the patch clears, by finding the cancel call on that driver, not just a call that reads it. The fixture tests pin 14.39.0's spring fields and refuse a handler without the cancel.
- The patch verifier's System share and long-press checks now match the patch. The sendable's id and kind have to be its own fields written through itself, the springs reset needs a zero that isn't the button's register, and the spring driver has to be one the detach handler cancels.
- `scripts/test-app-inventory.ps1` checks the inventory tool on two tiny real APKs in `scripts/checks/inventory-fixture`, every section and the diff between them, in PowerShell 7 and 5.1. The script contract suite runs it, and `scripts/checks/build-inventory-fixtures.ps1` rebuilds the APKs from their Java sources.
- The Pinterest reference docs now describe 14.39.0. The APK facts, class and method names, endpoints and resource names were checked against the 14.39.0 build, with the old 14.38.0 name kept next to each one that moved. The patch reference covers all 27 patches. The signed-in screen survey and the runtime measurements are still the 14.38.0 runs, and the docs say so.
- The patch reference records the push sign-up check from a fresh emulator install. Without Fix push notifications, Firebase refused the sign-up with a 403. With it, the same install registered with Firebase.
- A fixture run that passes every check is now kept under a key made from the bundle, the APK, the patch selection and the hash of every verifier script, and a later run with the same key reuses it instead of patching Pinterest again. The release push gate patches each declared fixture once and the release receipt reads those runs. `scripts/patch-for-device.ps1` can sign the gate's patched APK for a phone when its key matches. A changed input means a full run, and a failed run is never kept.
- The push gate now runs the unit tests and lint in a quick Gradle pass before the fixture suite, so a broken test stops the push in minutes instead of after the Pinterest APK runs. Each pass waits for its own slot in the build queue.
- The script contract tests now parse every tracked PowerShell file, so a syntax slip in a script that only runs on a release or with a phone shows up on the next script push.
- Releases now run in stages from `scripts/release/release.ps1`: prepare, preflight, gate, build and publish. Each stage checks that the one before it finished, and running one again after it's done changes nothing. The CHANGELOG cut refuses any bullet that isn't a one-line Pinterest or Tooling entry and names it. The GitHub notes carry every bullet of the section. `publish-release.ps1` pushes the index commit as soon as the release is up and ends with `verify-published-index.ps1`. The notes and index text come from `release_text.py`, which has its own unit tests. (#3)
- `scripts/app-inventory.ps1` lists what a Pinterest build talks to and what it reads about the device. That covers its Retrofit endpoints with their verbs, the startup tasks, the hosts its code names, who opens connections, the SDK packages, and who reads the advertising ID, Android ID, install referrer or device identifiers. The lines come out sorted, with renamed packages written as `~`, so `-BaseApk` can diff two builds. The [privacy notes](docs/pinterest-14.39.0-privacy.md) now carry the 14.39.0 inventory and what changed from 14.38.0.

## What's new

- New Hide save toasts patch. Saving a pin no longer pops up "Saved to" your board or the suggestion to follow the pin's creator, and the pin still saves as usual. Pick the patch in Morphe Manager, then turn on its switch on the Interface page. Turning it off or pausing HushPinterest brings the pop-ups back.
- New optional Original-quality images patch. With its switch on, Pinterest's image model hands back the original image ahead of the large size wherever Pinterest supplied one. It uses more data, so the switch starts off.
- Hide navigation buttons has a third switch, Hide Search button, beside Create and Notifications. It starts off. Home and Profile always stay in the bottom bar.
- Hide navigation buttons keeps a hidden tab hidden when Pinterest rebuilds it, such as Search after you close a pin.
- With Download pins on, the pin menu has a Copy media link row under Download pin. It copies the address of the same original image or MP4 the download would save, read from the pin when you tap it, and it's only offered when Pinterest supplied one.

- New Hide advertising ID patch, on by default. Pinterest and the ad and analytics code bundled in it read an all-zero ad ID with ad tracking limited, the answer Android gives after you delete your ad ID. ## 1.1.1 (2026-10-11)

Re-release of 1.1.0. No patch behaviour changed: the 1.1.0 release was published with a bundle that
had been built in the wrong task order and was **missing `classes.dex`**, so Morphe Manager could not
load it (`IllegalStateException: Patch bundle is missing dex entries`) and marked the source failed.
The desktop CLI never noticed, because on a JVM it loads the `.class` entries instead.

- `build.sh` now runs `generatePatchesList` before `buildAndroid`, forces `buildAndroid --rerun`
  (it reports UP-TO-DATE even after the jar task overwrites the bundle), and fails the build if the
  bundle has no `classes.dex`.
- The release asset was replaced at the time; this version bump exists so that Manager's
  version-keyed cache re-downloads the bundle. If your source shows as failed or has no patches,
  update the source (or delete and re-add it) and it will fetch 1.1.1.

Verified: the bundle loads in Morphe Manager on an emulator, patches the original Play-signed
`railone-2.1.66.apks` (6/6 patches applied), and the Manager's own output was re-disassembled and
confirmed to carry all three screenshot edits plus the 1.0.0 anti-tamper patches.

## 1.1.0 (2026-10-11)

Two new patches that remove the app's screenshot restrictions. Everything from 1.0.0 is unchanged
and the bundle still installs over the previous build (same keystore, data preserved).

### Patches

- **Allow screenshots.** `WavesActivity` - the app's generic in-app WebView (it takes a `url` and
  `headers` extra, so every page routed through it inherits this) applies `FLAG_SECURE` in
  `onCreate`, which made screenshots of those pages come out black. The patch rewrites that call
  into `clearFlags`, and neuters the bundled `no_screenshot` Flutter plugin's own `FLAG_SECURE`
  hook (`screenshotOff`, `toggleScreenshot`, `screenshotWith*`) so no screen can re-apply it.
- **Hide screenshot detection.** The same plugin registers a MediaStore `ContentObserver` that
  reports every newly saved image to the Flutter layer as a "screenshot taken" event. The patch
  returns early from the registration, so detection is never active.

### Notes

- On Motorola firmware the platform still writes the PNG while `FLAG_SECURE` is set, compositing
  the secure layer black, so the user-visible bug was a *black screenshot* rather than a "can't
  take screenshot" refusal - a screenshot file existing is not proof that the flag is gone.
- Verified on RailOne 2.1.66 (versionCode 237), arm64, Moto Edge 50 Neo / Android 16: screenshots
  of the Home, PNR and in-app WebView screens all come out with real content, and no detection
  event is logged.
- `MainActivity` does not set `FLAG_SECURE` on any screen tested. The app's Protectt RASP SDK has
  its own capture hooks and rule-driven appliers, but none were active, so they are deliberately
  left unpatched rather than half-covered.

First release. Four patches for RailOne (org.cris.aikyam):

- **Disable native security SDK** - stops `AikyamApplication.onCreate()` loading `libnative-lib.so` (root cause of the app force-stopping and wiping its own data on a re-signed build).
- **Bypass USB-debugging detection** - `adb_enabled`, `adb_wifi_enabled`, `development_settings_enabled` -> false.
- **Bypass signature verification** - the app's own SHA-256 certificate check -> true.
- **Bypass rjsniffer ADB check** - the `armys/rjsniffer` isolated-process check.

Verified on a Motorola Edge 50 Neo against RailOne 2.1.66: Morphe CLI applied all four patches to the real split bundle, the merged APK installed as an in-place upgrade, and the app stayed alive with USB debugging enabled (no anti-tamper wipe, no native-library failure).

Supply the app yourself; the bundle pins the genuine Play signing certificate and rejects a modified original.
